en/solve/solv-build-3Gantenna.title: Build a homemade 3G antenna
en/solve/solv-build-3Gantenna.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás, and for some time now, I’ve been learning how to improve my connectivity. I’m not an expert on the subject, but through internet searches, tutorials, and, above all, trial and error, I’ve learned a lot.
I have already tested and installed several solutions, and today, I’m sharing one of them with you: the homemade 3G antenna. Let’s get started!

What is building a homemade 3G antenna?
Building a 3G antenna means that by gathering and assembling easily accessible materials, you can increase the 3G and 4G signal strength of a cell phone or a MiFi-type modem →.

What is it for?
This homemade antenna will increase the capacity to receive the waves that carry the 4G signal → (mobile internet) in order to improve the connection quality from your cell phone or a shared modem (MiFi →).

What do you need?


3 mm thick aluminum rod (it must be exactly 3 mm).
50 cm of plastic cable trunking (ideally 2 cm wide).
Quick-drying epoxy glue (comes in two tubes).
10 m of coaxial cable (or the length you need for the antenna to reach the connection point).
2 clamps or vises.
2 locking pliers.
20 cm of copper wire (recommended: 1 mm thick).
A ruler (even better if you have a “caliper,” as it allows you to be more precise).
Hacksaw (if you can get an electric grinder with a thin cutting disc, you will save a looot of time).
Fine-tip permanent marker (e.g., Sharpie).
Pencil.
Soldering iron, solder (tin), soldering paste (flux).
Pliers and wire cutters (the latter is optional).
Metal file.
Workbench with good lighting.
Plastic zip ties (also known as “cable ties”).
Pole to mount the antenna (a bamboo pole as long as possible or a rigid rod of any material).
Utility knife, cutter.
Wire stripper (optional).
Cell phone or shared modem (MiFi).
Also… good vibes.
Patience.
Lots of precision.


How to do it?

Step 0 → Before starting, some recommendations for your safety

This solution has an intermediate level of difficulty and involves the use of some tools that can cause accidents if you are not careful. Therefore, it is important to keep the following recommendations in mind:

When using any sharp object, position it so that the cutting force is directed away from your body and not toward it.
Keep pets or children away from the work area, mainly because of the risk of contact with a hot soldering iron.
Before cutting, ensure that the clamps, vises, or pliers holding the material do not allow the slightest movement when applying any type of force.
When using solder and epoxy glue, especially protect the work surface so as not to damage it.
Do not hoist the antenna during a storm, as the antenna can act as a lightning rod that attracts lightning to your surroundings.



Step 1 → Check the materials

Before starting, check and have all the necessary elements on hand to work. In case you don’t recognize any of the materials, you can find them in the photo where the numbered materials appear.
You can make your purchases at the nearest hardware store as the materials are common; it shouldn’t be too complicated to find them. Perhaps the most difficult (and important) item on the list is the aluminum rod. Sometimes you can find elements made with this type of rod in the metal supports sold in stores that carry many Chinese products. At SOLE Voltaje, we have used different metals: copper, welding rods, and galvanized wire. We chose to buy a 3mm steel welding rod. If you can’t find aluminum at the hardware store, you can ask for other options; the important thing is that its diameter is as close as possible to 3mm or 1/8 of an inch.
Now organize the workspace, have these instructions on hand, and divide the tasks among the participants in the process: someone can be in charge of measuring, others of cutting, organizing, and gluing.


Step 2 → Understand the diagram

Below we show you the final diagram and some of the assembly parts so that you have greater clarity on the final setup.


Step 3 → Measure, cut, and mark**

It’s time to start! Here we get to work; you must cut each of the 10 elements that make up the antenna. With the help of the caliper (or ruler), you have to mark the length of each one and cut them with the hacksaw or the grinder. It is recommended that you cut one or half a millimeter extra and finish adjusting its length by filing the edges with the metal file. Listed below is the length of the 10 metal rods you must cut; in the world of antennas, these have their specific names (director, reflector, and dipole) related to the function they perform.

This is the list of cuts that are necessary:

Reflector: 8.0 cm
Dipole: 18 cm (This should be the length of the element; the bent rod must be exactly 7.6 cm, for now just cut the rod to this length).
Director #1: 7.6 cm
Director #2: 7.5 cm
Director #3: 7.4 cm
Director #4: 7.4 cm
Director #5: 7.3 cm
Director #6: 7.3 cm
Director #7: 7.2 cm
Director #8: 7.2 cm

📏 Remember that 10 mm = 1 cm

It is important to mark each of the cuts with tape, as seen in the photo, so that the next step is easier to do.



Step 4 → Bend the dipole

The dipole is an element bent into a “C” shape. Its total length must be 7.6 cm, but the rod must be a little longer (approximately 18.0 cm). Making this piece is a trial-and-error task. In my case, it has helped to slowly bend the rod against a circular tube 2 cm in diameter to give it the curvature.



Step 5 → Assembling the antenna

We are reaching the middle of the process. Don’t get discouraged, there’s very little left! Now it’s time to assemble the elements onto the cable trunking. This can be replaced by wood or some other material on hand, as long as it does not conduct electricity.

On the surface of the trunking, you have to mark the following distances, on which each of the rod cuts made in the previous step will subsequently be placed.

Reflector: 1.0 cm
Dipole: 5.0 cm
Director #1: 6.2 cm
Director #2: 9.2 cm
Director #3: 12.8 cm
Director #4: 17.0 cm
Director #5: 21.7 cm
Director #6: 26.7 cm
Director #7: 31.9 cm
Director #8: 37.4 cm

Once the lines are marked, you can glue each of the rods with the epoxy glue onto the trunking; however, we have seen that this configuration is very fragile and makes our antenna not last very long. For this reason, we found a better way to attach the rods to the trunking. For this, we can use the hot soldering iron, which with its fine tip can easily pierce the plastic, so with this tool, we are going to drill the sides until it has a diameter sufficient for the rod to pass through. Take advantage of the plastic while it is still hot after you pierce it to pass the rod through and ensure it has the appropriate diameter. This should be done on both sides of the trunking so that the rod can pass from side to side.

Once you finish the 20 perforations, you must disassemble the trunking and use the metal file to remove the plastic burr to allow the rods to enter easily.

Now, before positioning each of the rods, we must make a small cut to facilitate the entry of the dipole; for this, we must disassemble the trunking and use the hacksaw to make a vertical cut so that it crosses the sides of the second measurement (5.0 cm) until it reaches the perforation we opened with the soldering iron.

Once the dipole is embedded, we can insert the other rods according to the order already mentioned.

You can add a little epoxy glue on the rod to ensure that the elements remain well adhered to the trunking. Wait for the necessary time for the glue to dry before continuing with connecting the cable to your new antenna.



Step 6 → Prepare the cable

While the glue is drying, you can proceed with the preparation of the coaxial cable. You can check the previous entry to understand how a coaxial cable is made before taking it apart.

To do this part, you can use a wire stripper or a cutter to separate each layer of the cable; you must be careful with the cut so as not to break the first layer, which is a metal mesh. Thus, at one end, you have to leave the copper wire and the cable mesh free. You can separate the mesh carefully and then braid it again.

At the other end, with the copper wire, make a wave, which will be the element that comes into contact with the phone, or MiFi, to improve the signal.



Step 7 → Solder the dipole

This is one of the most careful steps; after this, we move on to assembly. Remember that the dipole is one of the fundamental components of the antenna; it must be soldered to the end of the coaxial cable that we separated into the mesh and the copper wire, and this in turn connects with a copper wire acting as a bridge between each end of the dipole. First, we make the bridge with the copper wire as seen in the image, where each end is braided and then soldered.

Once we have the copper wire soldered to the two ends of the coaxial, we can couple it to the dipole; for this, we can first tighten it a little with the pliers and then proceed to solder.

Remember that the dipole must be perpendicular to the trunking, so to avoid sudden movements of the cable that change this position, we must secure the cable with plastic zip ties.



Step 8 → Final assembly

Finally, we are done! You can now perform the assembly and installation of the antenna! To do this, make sure it is well adjusted with plastic zip ties at the highest part of the pole; the antenna must be oriented in such a way that the dipole is as close as possible to the pole.

Remember to also tie the cable to the pole so that it does not come loose from the solder points on the antenna. Now, you have to hoist the pole and make sure that the position of the antenna is looking in the direction of the nearest cell tower.
Now, at the other end of the cable, place your cell phone so that the copper serpentine is touching the back of the device.


The antenna aiming process must be done slowly and carefully; the waves are very sensitive to movement. First, you can establish the 0 position, and from there, you can go turning to the right or left in small intervals. After each movement, you can check the connection quality with the cellular network from the “Settings” screen of the phone. This is a number expressed in decibels (dB); the higher it is, the lower the signal quality will be. You can also do it by looking at the intensity of the signal icon that appears at the top of the cell phone. The challenge is to find the place where the decibel number is lowest or where the signal intensity icon is greatest.

Now, you can proceed to secure the pole in this position and that’s it! Happy browsing!

Recommendations for potential difficulty points
If you are using solder and it slips continuously, it must be that the tin solder you possibly bought is not compatible with the metal of the rods you are using, so we recommend looking for another solder or trying to make contact between the cable and the rod by tightening them well with a wire. Normally each metal is compatible with a solder of the same metal (steel with steel solder, tin with tin solder).
__
Other possible internets
We can know if this solution works by doing speed tests →. You can contrast by taking measurements with and without the antenna to recognize how much the signal improves with this device.
Through trial and error, you will feel more and more confident to tinker, that is, to solve by doing. Now, would you be encouraged to do another solution? Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

What can you achieve with this solution?
This solution can work to temporarily improve your connectivity conditions. The antenna will serve as an amplifier for the emission and reception of waves for your devices.
Knowing this, how far would you like to go? Is this a solution you could do where you live? We hope it has been useful to you! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could benefit from it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

en/solve/solv-buy-cellphone.title: How to buy the right mobile phone for me?
en/solve/solv-buy-cellphone.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás, and just like you, I have been progressively learning how to improve my connectivity to do SOLE. I am not an expert on the subject, but through searches on Internet →, tutorials, and, above all, trial and error, I have learned a lot and set up functional solutions.
What does it mean to buy a suitable cell phone for you?
In this particular solution, we will learn how to buy a Smartphone → according to your possibilities and needs. Below you will find a series of information, criteria, and tips that aim to be as clear as possible so that you can feel supported in the decision-making process of which cell phone to buy. The estimated reading time is 12 minutes and it consists of 10 items, but don’t be scared, you can read these items with the help of other people. Remember that at SOLE Voltaje we want to promote the collective use of the internet.

What is it for?
In this solution, you will find a few practical tips to be able to make a much more informed decision about which cell phones are the most suitable for you.

Before we start, some ethical issues!
At SOLE Voltaje, we speak from the perspective of supporting people to clarify the ethical implications of a decision by problematizing the circumstance that leads you to make that decision. This solution starts from the assumption that you want to buy a cell phone, do you really need it? This is not always the best option for you. Sometimes you have an old cell phone that a family member can give you, or for different reasons, you prefer not to have a cell phone and it is a better option for you to have a computer. If, after scanning your options, you definitely consider that you need to buy a cell phone, this is the right place for you! Here we advise you on what you should keep in mind when buying a cell phone.

What do you need?

Save money for the purchase.
Internet access.
A trusted store or distributor.
Curiosity.


How to do it?

Step 0 → How do I know if I need to buy a cell phone?

One of the characteristics of our current era is the great development of international and national markets; our cell phones are made in China and we can buy them in Colombia, we can go to the market and buy rice brought from Brazil. In addition, we find disproportionate consumption options: we can buy white rice, yellow rice, bulk rice, lemon-flavored rice, etc. There are endless options to turn us into consumers of products that we often do not need, and so we end up buying non-nutritious food, and we fall into an expense that does not satisfy the main function of food: to nourish us! In the same way, we fill our homes with endless merchandise that ends up piled up or discarded because, in the end, it was of no use to us. For this reason, we want to promote responsible consumption. In the case of a cell phone, we suggest you ask yourself the following questions to know if it is a responsible purchase:

Do you need to buy a cell phone or do you have other options to access the internet and make calls?
Can you buy another option that meets your internet connection and calling needs and can be paid for by several people?
If you buy a cell phone, will your quality of life really improve or will it worsen? For example, will you now be addicted to watching content or on social media, or will you be more stressed every month thinking about how to pay for this new expense?
Finally, is this new purchase really a priority for you?




Step 1 → What do I need a cell phone for?

Just like a car, the cell phone we choose must adapt to our main needs. It doesn’t make much sense to buy a 4x4 truck if you are going to be driving through a city with paved avenues.
Now, think about what the most important activities will be and where you will spend the most time on your cell phone: Do you want to take many photos of your region? Then you should pay attention to the camera features; Are you going to be out of the house all day in the middle of the countryside, or are you going to use your phone as a modem to share your internet with other people participating in a SOLE? A good battery would be fundamental; Do you want to use the internet to learn in a group? A large screen with good definition is important; Do you want to play a high-definition video game? You will need a good processor →; Do you need to work with several applications at once? Look at the RAM memory →; Do you need to have many applications and large files? Look at the internal storage.
Now that you have decided whether to buy a cell phone, I will give an introduction using my case as an example:

💡 At the beginning of 2024, I dropped my cell phone when getting off a taxi. Because of my work and contact with my family and friends, it is important for me to have a cell phone. Some time ago, I decided that I would not invest more than 1,000,000 COP in this tool. About 5 years ago, I learned about a new brand that was emerging; it had good prices and very good references from friends and users on the internet. This brand is Xiaomi. My last two cell phones had been from this brand, each costing around 700,000 COP.
However, I searched online for references and saw that there is a new brand that is arriving and is affordable: Tecno. I looked at several references and saw that it is currently the best-selling brand on Mercado Libre, so I looked for a cell phone with similar characteristics to the previous ones: 256 GB of internal memory, a decent processor, a battery of more than 4000 mAh, a large screen, and at least 8 GB of RAM. These characteristics are compatible with my work and personal use; I don’t take professional photos, nor was I looking for it to play video games. Finally, I found a cell phone from this brand for $475,000 COP. This cell phone I bought was a Tecno Spark 20 Dual Sim with 256 GB. So far, I can say that it has been an excellent purchase!


Now it’s your turn to identify what you need the cell phone for!


Step 2 → Set a budget

First of all, define what your budget will be. For this, you can calculate how many days of work you are willing to invest in this device. Do not go into debt for a cell phone; many times they offer us financing for 1 or 2 years, and the cell phone breaks or gets stolen before we finish paying for it.

Once you are clear about the above, you will know which features you should pay the most attention to.


Camera
If you love taking photos, here are some aspects that are central when detailing your device’s camera:


Resolution
This is what we commonly know as megapixels, although it is very important, it is not everything we should look at when evaluating a camera. The more megapixels it has, the greater the detail you will see in the images. However, you should have a limit. The standard could be a 12 MP camera, because if it has good features and excellent image processing, you will get high-quality photos. If you start having higher resolution photos, the files will be very heavy and will fill your cell phone’s internal storage quickly.




Sensor and lenses
A good cell phone camera must have a quality sensor, as well as several lenses. The latter, in fact, has already become a standard. When combined, they allow for better images. One of the most popular lenses is the wide-angle lens. Thanks to this, much more information is incorporated into the photographs and it provides a visual angle of up to 120 degrees, perfect for group photos or indoors where there is not much space.



Aperture
The lens aperture will be fundamental for a good photo; this feature defines how much light the camera can capture. It is identified with the letter f followed by a number, for example, f1.9 or f2.0. The lower this number, the greater the amount of light the camera will capture. For this reason, it is important that it be low, because with a greater light intake, the images will have more detail.



Screen
A screen will define whether our eyes get tired faster or slower, whether we will see a certain degree of detail or not, or how fast the battery will be consumed.

When you are clear that your cell phone should be a device used in a group, as happens when we do SOLE, this feature becomes important, since it is not so easy for several people to read on a small screen.

Screen size
The size of cell phone screens has increased over time, although for a few years now they have remained without growing much, since they lose their portability function in the pocket. We could say that most cell phones are between 3.5” and 6” (this measures the diagonal, that is, from one upper corner to the opposite lower corner). It really depends on your taste here: do you want a large screen that allows you to watch a video from afar among several people, or do you prefer a small one so that your cell phone doesn’t attract so much attention?




Screen technology
Full HD technology is more recent than HD and the number of pixels is higher compared to HD, which works with 1,280 x 720 pixels. The Full HD system gives a much more real look to the image. This last technology is only arriving in the latest cell phones with large panels, since high resolution does not make much sense on small screens.


Screen type
There are different types of screens, but in the current market, two are the most popular: those with LCD technology, also known as inorganic, and those with OLED technologies, known as organic.


LCD: These are backlit liquid crystal screens that usually cover the entire panel. In the past, they were the most popular, but they are produced in smaller quantities every time. Being backlit, they will consume more energy, but for this very reason, they look good under direct sunlight.


OLED: These screens differ from LCDs because their materials allow them to generate light by themselves when electricity is applied; this allows them to turn each pixel off or on independently, so they consume less energy. In addition, they end up being brighter and having better definition of the color black.



Internal storage
Internal storage defines the amount of files we can save on our cell phone; it is like the hard drive → in a computer. This will determine how many programs you can have installed at once, and whether or not you can save all types of files. At the moment, we recommend buying a cell phone with at least 64 GB of internal memory. Also, check if it has the option to receive microSD cards to expand the capacity in the future.




RAM memory
This is the cell phone’s temporary memory; it helps with performance and gives a clue as to how fast applications open and how fast the cell phone flows. We recommend a minimum of 4GB of RAM.



Processor
The processor is the brain; it is the one that is always awake and receives instructions. The more cores the processor has, the better performance it will have, although it will also depend on the brand. Here, the best option is to look at the name of the processor used by the cell phone that catches your attention and do a little research on your own. Hopefully, it hasn’t been released more than 4 years ago.




Battery



Compare it with another cell phone
Once you have some interesting options, it is important that you compare them. For this, you don’t have to do it manually; there are several pages that already do this automatically. Below, we leave you some:


Versus
Movilcelular
Here we compare my cell phone against a Motorola:

Besides the fact that the Tecno Spark 20 is better rated in its features, we can see that in the Colombian market they have the following prices:

Motorola Edge 30 Neo Dual SIM 128 GB very peri 8 GB RAM - $ 849,900 COP
Tecno Spark 20 Dual SIM 256 GB Black 8 GB RAM - $ 499,000 COP

💡 We can have a better cell phone saving $ 350,000 COP by risking trying an emerging brand.

Don’t be fooled
It is important that you constantly check emerging brands; normally, brands with little advertising, very good features, and a low price appear. However, many times out of habit and experience, we continue to buy the same brand as the previous cell phone. For example, my best friend has been with the Motorola brand since university; I think that although it is a good brand, it handles very high costs and I prefer new, cheaper brands that have good references to save some money.
Another important element has to do with the warranty. When you live in a central city, it is easy that if something happens to the cell phone, there is a branch of all available brands in case you have to use the warranty. But in less central cities, for example in Bucaramanga, the brand of my current cell phone, “Tecno,” does not have an office, so if you live there, you would have to send the cell phone to Bogotá, pay more money, and wait longer for them to return it. But possibly in this city, there is a service center for more popular brands, as is the case with Motorola.

How much is enough?
This question is difficult to answer, but I think we can rephrase it as follows: Does the option you chose meet the need and intention you projected at the beginning? In the previous example, I showed you how I consider that the cell phone I currently have was a very good option for my lifestyle. This type of reasoning is what we want you to do when making a decision about the option you are going to buy.

en/solve/solv-buy-computer.title: How to buy a computer?
en/solve/solv-buy-computer.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás and, just like you, I have been learning about how to improve my internet connection. I am not an expert on the subject, but by searching online, watching tutorials, and learning through trial and error, I have managed to improve the quality of the internet in areas without good connectivity.
What is buying a computer for you?
In this solution, you will be able to clarify some important things to make the decision. On one hand, you will differentiate the main characteristics of a computer and a series of recommendations based on these characteristics. You will also be able to take your needs and capabilities into account for the analysis. I hope you can feel supported and confident as you move forward in selecting a computer.
What is it for?
Making a purchase decision on topics where we are not experts can be a difficult exercise. For this reason, we have developed this solution to accompany you in this process. Ultimately, this solution serves to help you make an informed decision so you don’t spend more money than necessary or end up buying a computer that does not meet your requirements.
How do I know if I need one?
Knowing whether or not you need to make a purchase involves two fundamental criteria:

Reflect deeply and meditatively on whether you need it. To do this, ask yourself: What need is buying a computer solving? Can this need be solved in another way? For example, can you do the same thing with the cell phone you currently have, or perhaps with a tablet?
If you have already confirmed that the need you are facing can only be solved with access to a computer, it is time to look at other alternatives before buying. For example, can you borrow a computer from school or the library? Can you get a donated device from a family member or a company?

If you have exhausted the previous options and have definitely decided to buy a computer, this solution is the right one for you.
What are the advantages of a computer compared to a cell phone?
Speed and capacity are two of the great advantages that computers have compared to phones. With a computer, you have a keyboard and a mouse at your disposal, which allows you to type and navigate menus much faster. In addition, the larger screen of a computer allows you to organize your digital space in a way that a small phone screen cannot. It will also allow you to…
These factors not only save you time; they also allow you to multitask. On a computer, you can more easily switch between applications and even have them comfortably on the screen at the same time. For example, you can have one window open with your resume and another open with a job you are looking for. Or if you are looking for the best deal, you can have pages for several products open at the same time to compare them easily.

What options exist?

Desktop computer

This is a computer designed to be installed in a static location, such as a desk or table. The hardware components usually consist of a computer case that houses the motherboard with the respective components.


Laptop

Simply called a laptop, this is a computer that can be moved or transported with relative ease. Laptops are small, lightweight, and specially designed so that their batteries are capable of powering them for an extended period of time (usually 4 to 5 hours). Screen sizes range from 11 to 15 inches.


Pros and cons









































CategoryDesktopLaptopPortabilityIt is in a fixed location.It can be transported with ease.CostIt is more economical.It is more expensive.Upgradability and CustomizationIts hardware components can be updated and improved with ease. This makes it easy to customize to your needs.It is increasingly difficult to update its hardware components, as most come integrated. In some, you can change the RAM memory and the hard drive.Energy independenceIt must always be connected to an electrical power source.By having a battery, it can be disconnected from an electrical power source for a few hours; however, over time this battery wears out and lasts less time until it needs to be replaced.Energy consumptionThey consume more energy.They consume less energy as their components are more compact.SpaceThey take up more space.They take up little space.

What should I keep in mind to make this decision?

Step 0 → Before starting: ALERT! What is hardware and software?

It is important to know that there are two basic components in a computer: Hardware → and software:

Hardware →: It is the set of components that make up the material part of a computer.
Software: It is the set of programs, instructions, data, and computer rules for executing certain tasks on a computer.

Below we will explain what the main hardware components of a computer are, which are important when buying one.













































ElementImageDescriptionProcessor (CPU) →This is the brain of the machine, undoubtedly one of the fundamental factors to keep in mind. Remember that depending on the power of this element, the equipment will be able to execute the instructions you give it faster.StorageThe hard drive → marks the storage capacity of your equipment.RAM MemoryThe RAM memory → temporarily stores the data of the applications that are running. The more RAM your computer has, the greater its capacity to run different programs at the same time optimally.Graphics cardThe graphics card is responsible for processing data related to images and videos that are played on the computer.PeripheralsThese refer to the input and output access points of other devices that you will connect to your computer. For example: USB connection → ports, audio outputs, HDMI connections, etc.ScreenIt is what allows you to see what you are doing on your computer.BatteryOnly applies to laptops and determines the usage time you have without being connected to power.


Step 1 → The fundamental criteria

Now that you know each of the main hardware components, we will tell you what the characteristics are that differentiate their performance, cost, and the questions you should ask yourself to choose one option or another.








































ElementDetailRelevant questionsProcessorIf you are looking for a fast computer that performs tasks effectively without slowing down, you have to take into account the number of cores. In addition, the frequency or working speed must be detailed. The higher the number, the better the performance; this factor is measured in GHz (gigahertz). So 3GHz is much better than 2.5GHz. Regarding brands, this is the recommendation: If you can afford it, opt for an Intel; if you need something cheaper, an AMD. And if you are really tight on money, choose a Celeron.How many programs can you use at the same time? What activities will you perform with your computer, are you going to design models, browse the internet, play games?Intel or AMD?How many cores?Storage500 GB is more than enough for “normal” home use. If you like to save movies, series, etc., it may be necessary to choose a hard drive of 1 TB (terabyte) or higher. Speed is also fundamental. It is measured in revolutions per minute (rpm); the higher the speed, the better the data reading and writing will be. Currently, there are two different technologies: The traditional hard drive (HDD), which is slower but cheaper. The other is the solid-state drive (SSD), faster but more expensive.Solid-state drive or hard drive? How much information are you going to save? Do I want the computer to turn on quickly?RAM MemoryThe more RAM your computer has, the greater its capacity to run different programs at the same time optimally. Calculating how much RAM you need for your equipment is 100% related to the type of use you give it. The more programs you use (such as design programs, editing, among others), the more you will need. If you are going to use design programs, video games, or simply have the money and want a very fast computer, buy 16GB; if your use is for conventional tasks (writing, browsing, etc.), 8GB will be enough; if you don’t have much budget, you must settle for 4GB and be willing to accept that the computer will not be very fast.What programs am I going to use? How many GB do I need?Graphics cardIt can be an important factor or not depending on the use you are going to give it. If in your case you only need it for basic tasks and standard use, any graphics card will work. But, if you require graphic work or gaming, a dedicated graphics card is ideal. Don’t complicate your life. For standard use, you don’t need a spectacular graphics card. Any of the Radeon or Nvidia brands will give you great service.Am I going to use it for video games or design programs?Nvidia and Radeon?ScreenInteraction with a screen is increasingly frequent, so it is important that it provides comfort and takes care of your eyesight. For this, we must take into account:Size: If you need to take the equipment from one place to another, 14 inches is ideal, but if your purpose is graphic work, you need a larger size.Resolution: It is useless to buy a large screen with poor resolution. From 1080p is full HD and is a quite good resolution. Monitors up to 23” are recommended to avoid the pixelated effect caused by images with low resolution.How many inches do I need? What resolution is enough for my requirements?Do you need to manage several programs and at the same time design or watch your favorite movies?AudioThis will depend on the speakers you buy for a desktop computer. In laptops, this feature is not their strong suit, but “gamer” type computers usually come with great sound.Do you need extraordinary sound for your parties or to watch movies, or do you already have a great speaker that you can connect to your computer?


Step 2 → Let’s make the decision

Now that you know the fundamental elements, it is time to make a decision. For this, we have developed a series of simple questions, and depending on your answer, we would recommend one hardware feature or another:

Criterion 0: Set a budget

Now it’s time to define a budget! For this, you can calculate how many days of work per month buying this computer represents. Ultimately, the decision will fall on this point. This purchase can easily mean more than a month of work, so it is very important to try to be as informed as possible before deciding.

Criterion 1: Usage habits

Now let’s remember some of the most relevant questions when defining our usage habits:

Do I need the computer to be portable, or do I prefer to use it in one place?
Am I going to use it for video games and design programs or for office tasks?
How much information are you going to save?
Do I need to use several programs at the same time?

With these questions and your budget, you can now narrow down to a smaller list of options. Choose wisely.

Don’t be fooled
It is important to remember that when going to a store, a salesperson usually tries to push the “star product” on us. However, many times the cost of computers from 6 months or a year ago is significantly lower than the technologies of that moment. Sometimes, you can find second-hand computers that have been in good hands and make a good deal. On the other hand, I can only recommend that if possible, you buy a desktop computer or a laptop that allows you to upgrade its hardware.
The computer I am writing to you from, I bought 13 years ago. It has gone through a hard drive change and an increase in RAM, in addition to a few repairs, but right now it works well and has been a great long-term investment.
Finally, remember that now it is very easy to find pages and people dedicated exclusively to making reviews and evaluating the performance of computers. Additionally, some pages allow you to compare between several options. Once you have selected the computers available on the market that best fit your case, use these pages and user comments to make a more accurate decision.
Another recommendation that never hurts is to be guided by the reputation of the brand and the seller. In my case, from experience, I recommend the ASUS brand in terms of value for money, although from SOLE, we have also done well with the Lenovo brand.

How much is enough?
This question is difficult to answer, but I think we can rephrase it as follows: Does the option you chose meet the need and intention you projected at the beginning? In my case, 13 years ago I bought a computer for university, but also one that would allow me to play video games, download, and watch many movies. That is, going for the minimum (that it would work for university), I should have selected a laptop, lightweight, with good battery, a small screen, an intermediate processor, 8GB of RAM, and a generic graphics card. However, I did the exact opposite: I selected a large, heavy computer with low battery and a dedicated graphics card, what they would call a “gamer” computer: The ASUS N53SV.
By not thinking through my decision well, I ended up buying a computer that was too big and heavy to transport and had poor battery life. Ultimately, its main function was to be used for university; the video games and movies were secondary. Right now, although I use it, I almost never transport it; it ended up being, in practice, a desktop computer. That is why from SOLE Voltaje, we don’t want you to fall into mistakes like mine! Always remember that many times “less is more.”
With what we have just seen, you can no longer be fooled, it’s time to make the decision!

Do you need to buy a cell phone plan or do you have other options to access the internet?
Is there any other option that covers your internet connection and can be paid for by several people?
If you buy a cell phone plan, will it really improve your quality of life or will it worsen it? How much time will you spend connected to social networks? Will it be difficult for you to disconnect from the content? Will knowing how you will pay for this new expense imply a dose of monthly stress?
Finally, is this new consumption really a priority for you? What real use will you give it?
Don’t forget this consideration: the decision you make can be reversible when conditions change. It’s not a child; it’s just a payment plan that you can change when and how you need to.




Step 1 → What do I need a cell phone plan for?

Now that you have decided, it is time to understand what you are going to need it for.
Do you need the plan to facilitate your work, to study, to stay connected with your family and friends, or to spend leisure time? Depending on your answer, you will identify usage patterns.
Let’s use my example case:

💡 In 2022, I had two jobs and no office. Also, I moved around a lot: I traveled around Bogotá and to different parts of the country on a recurring basis. I needed to connect to virtual meetings; one of my jobs required having Zoom video calls. So I needed a data connection and to make calls to many people. At that time, I decided to have a postpaid plan with 10 GB and unlimited minutes.
Shortly after, I started traveling and staying constantly at a family farm, where the data signal was very poor. I decided to buy a fixed internet plan for the farm.
In 2023, I only had one job and had an office with internet. I no longer needed to travel as much. I changed my postpaid plan to a cheaper one and canceled the internet plan at the farm.

Now it’s your turn to identify what you need the internet plan for!


Step 2 → According to what you need, these are the questions to ask yourself.


Do you need minutes, data, or both?
Do you need a high connection speed to download heavy files or have video calls?
Do you constantly need to have this service or is it only for a few days of the week?
Do you need coverage in several territories or just one?
What budget do you have available for this expense?




Step 3 → According to what is available, these are the questions to ask yourself**

Now let’s take action! We need to get the following information:
Which mobile operators are available in my territory?

Ask your neighbors: what operator do they use or have they used in the past? Which one works best? Which one has better technical support? Which one has better rates?
You can go to cell phone stores in the nearest urban center and ask directly about which operators they have available. In Colombia for 2024, there are multiple options: Claro, Movistar, TIGO, WOM, Virgin Mobile, Avantel, and Móvil Éxito are the main operators in the market. The latter two are small operators that rent the infrastructure of the large operators to provide their services.

What plans do these operators have available?
After being clear about the operators available in your territory and knowing which ones perform best, proceed to ask about the prepaid and postpaid plans they offer. Below we present some comparative tables of the prepaid and postpaid plans that were offered for 2023.
Prepaid plan rates 7-10 days

Selectra, What is the best prepaid cell phone plan in Colombia?


Step 4 → Evaluate which is the best option: What do I really need?**

It’s time to make a decision! With the information you obtained, we will give you some criteria that we consider fundamental when making a decision:

Frequency of use, how much are you going to use it?


Photo: Pixabay License
If, for example, most of your days you need to make calls and be connected to the internet, balancing it out, postpaid plans end up being the best option.
But if, on the other hand, your demand is occasional, has variability throughout the month, and/or you can be constantly connected to a WiFi network at your workplace or home, making sporadic prepaid top-ups might be the most useful.

Budget, how much money do you want to spend?

Now it’s time to define a budget! An easy calculation: how many hours of work per week does this new consumption represent? This can become a permanent expense, so it is important to reason the purchase.
The final decision may fall on this point: people who use prepaid plans normally do not have a constant flow of money that ensures they can pay a monthly fee. While the use of postpaid is associated with people who can guarantee the payment of a monthly fee on a constant basis.
Currently, prepaid top-ups in the Colombian market start from 2,000 COP with one day of validity.** On the other hand, the cheapest postpaid plans are around **27,000 COP per month**.**
To make this decision, take a count of how much you are willing to invest in this service and what its frequency of use is.

Usage habits, what and how are you going to use it for?

Are you a person who makes long-duration calls or do you spend more time connected to the internet? Depending on this, you will be able to prioritize the number of minutes, the number of Gigabytes, or both, when choosing your consumption option.
Below, we explain each of these variables if you are still not very clear about how they work:





















MinutesDataThe minutes associated with your plan determine how long you can spend talking to other mobile phones nationwide; in some cases, a number of minutes to other countries such as Venezuela, Canada, or the United States is also included. Currently, most postpaid plans come with unlimited minutes.They are the amount of mobile data intended for internet use on your phone. Their use is the amount that your cell phone uploads or downloads when using them. You can configure them so as not to spend them, save them, or restrict what they are used for. Remember that depending on the content you upload or download, data consumption will be higher or lower; for example, watching a two-hour movie from your cell phone can consume approximately 300 MB, almost a third of a Gigabyte. Content such as high-resolution videos, audio, or images has high data consumption compared to other types of files such as text.Photo: CC0 Public Domain,
For example, when we do a SOLE, we need to connect a few computers to be able to research Big Questions. That means that the plan we contract must necessarily have data.
You can make your phone’s internet connection available to the group so that everyone can use it.
Although the internet searches that take place in a SOLE do not use much data, you might want to watch videos or other content that requires a larger amount of data than you have contracted. However, you do not need that amount of data available all the time.
So you can buy a prepaid plan that allows you to be connected, specifically for the SOLE, and solve your Big Questions.
If you decide to meet once a week or want to have the space available with the connection at any time, you can consider paying for a postpaid plan together… how does that sound?

Signal, where are you going to use it?

We have to look at coverage, upload and download speed, 3G, 4G signal.
Although we often hear people say that one operator is better than another, this will depend on the region and can change over time.
Sometimes they install more antennas → or their networks become saturated due to an excess of users.

Other benefits, information that may be useful


Watch out for “Free data usage in applications”
Remember, nothing is free!

Most plans currently in Colombia have the use of applications such as Facebook or WhatsApp as “unlimited” as long as the top-up lasts or for the whole month in the case of postpaid plans.
They never explain to us that this unlimited consumption is only related to messages that contain text, that is, if you see a photo or a video, via WhatsApp or Facebook, the data associated with this consumption will be deducted from your plan.

‘Free’ applications

Some postpaid plans offer us a license for applications such as Amazon Prime (series and movie platform) or Spotify (music playback application), that is, for the payment of a cell phone plan they give you access to the Premium version of these platforms. This can be beneficial if they are platforms you already use; if not, ignore it, it will be one more expense.
They also don’t tell you that this way of ‘forcing’ you to use certain applications to communicate, entertain yourself, inform yourself, or create your digital presence is part of a commercial strategy. That is, companies will use the information from your profiles to offer you consumer goods, which will affect the benefit of the corporations responsible for their processing… that is, those companies are profiting from the information they extract about you. So, watch out, when a product is free, it’s because you are the product.

Don’t be fooled
It is important that you constantly check the plans and offers of the operators.
Currently, in Colombia, you can perform “portability,” that is, switch from one operator to another, change from one operator’s plan to another while keeping your number, just by requesting the new operator to carry out this process**. There are no longer any permanence clauses that force you to stay with the same operator for a certain time**. So if you see that there is a better option for you ****don’t hesitate to switch!
There is a small offer available from small operators; these are prepaid plans with long validity periods.
I, who live in Bogotá, am evaluating switching to Móvil Éxito. I currently have a postpaid plan at WOM where I pay 40,000 COP**, this entitles me to **60 GB and unlimited minutes**—this is a lot! Initially, I switched to WOM because, by doing portability, they gave me the **first three months free, plus 20GB** and they **charged me 35,000 COP. Now that I am in Bogotá and work from home and the office, I have internet available from these places. I was checking options while writing this solution and saw that Móvil Éxito offers the following prepaid plans:

Per month, my consumption does not exceed 5 GB and I make, at most, 30 calls per month. For this reason, the first plan would cost me $13,000 COP, less than a third of what I pay now! Mind you, I have to make the payment for the whole year at once, but I am not tied to any type of contract.

How much is enough?
This question is difficult to answer, but I think we can rephrase it as follows: does the option you chose meet the need and intention you projected at the beginning?
In the previous example, I showed you how I consider the plan I currently have to be excessive and I found options that do meet my initial requirement, at a third of the price I currently pay.
These types of reasoning are what we would like you to have when making a decision about the option you are going to buy.

en/solve/solv-buy-satellite-antenna.title: How to buy a satellite antenna?
en/solve/solv-buy-satellite-antenna.content:
Photo: Satellite antenna - Wikipedia
Hi, I’m Nicolás and I’m learning about how the internet works. I’m not an expert on the subject, but through internet searches, tutorials, and, above all, a lot of curiosity, I have learned how to set up functional internet solutions.
What is choosing an internet service for non-interconnected places?
In this particular solution, we will learn how to choose a satellite internet service for rural or remote areas that do not have Wi-Fi or wired internet connection. For this, we will look at three technologies available in Colombia: Satellite dish, WiMax, and Starlink.

What is it for?
This solution serves to provide greater clarity on which satellite internet service you can choose if you are located in areas that do not have Wi-Fi or wired internet connection.

How do I know if I need it?
Now, the quality of the internet service you can choose will depend on your possibilities and needs, as well as the availability of internet providers in your region.
This solution is an option that you can pay for together with the people in the community where you live. Consult with the people to have a common criterion and decide jointly, sharing the decision, care, expenses, benefits, and advantages of the services; this will make the decision you make more sustainable and long-lasting in the long run.

Options to review
What you need:

A budget, that is, knowing what you can spend
A list of internet providers in your region
A lot of curiosity!
It can help to have reference people from your community with whom to review the information; making a decision together will be simpler and more beneficial for everyone


How to do it?

Step 0 → What are the types of internet connection that work in non-interconnected regions?

Now let’s get down to business. Digital technologies are changing rapidly over the years. In this article, we want to present you with research on the options available in Colombia for 2024: satellite dish, WiMax, and Starlink.

Satellite dish


The most popular internet option for rural or remote areas these days is the satellite dish. The great advantage of this solution is its coverage, accessibility, and price, which makes it a viable and functional option. To access this technology, the company in charge must install a satellite dish at your home.

WiMax


Image: Alvarion WiMAX CPE Equipment - Wikipedia
The first thing you need is to contact a company that offers these services and has a repeater near your home to be able to send you the internet signal. Subsequently, you have to put an antenna on the facade of your house. This antenna will have to point directly to the company’s repeater that will provide you with the service or to an intermediate connection point used to overcome obstacles between your antenna and their repeater. The installation of the antenna will be done by the company itself.

Starlink


Image: Starlink Standard Actuated Antenna - Starlink
Starlink is Elon Musk’s satellite internet project. It is a private satellite internet that facilitates connections, especially in rural areas. The company is considered the first and largest satellite constellation in the world that uses a low Earth orbit to offer broadband, high-speed, and low-latency satellite internet, which allows for streaming content, playing online, making video calls, and more.
To put it into operation, you must buy a kit with the antenna that must be placed outside your house and that automatically orients itself to establish a connection in a matter of minutes, provided you have a clear view of the sky.
We already have an introduction to the available options, now we can move on to moment 1 where we will talk about the advantages and disadvantages of each option.


Step 1 → Advantages and disadvantages of the satellite dish connection

Advantages

Global coverage: This means that people living in remote regions or rural areas can access the Internet reliably.
Fast access: Faster than DSL and dial-up services with speeds of up to 25 Mbps and 100 Mbps. Although satellite internet used to have a reputation for being slow, today it is possible to enjoy speeds comparable to terrestrial connections.
Constant connectivity: One of the most prominent advantages of the satellite dish is its ability to provide a constant and stable connection. Unlike terrestrial connections that can be affected by infrastructure interruptions or adverse weather conditions, satellite internet does not depend on physical cables and relies on satellites in orbit for data transmission. This ensures a reliable and continuous connection, even in areas prone to natural disasters.
High flexibility and mobility: Satellite internet also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have Internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, making it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
Does not require residential telephone service: It is not a requirement to have a telephone line to access this Internet service.

Disadvantages

High latency →: One of the main disadvantages of the satellite dish is the latency →, that is, the time it takes for the signal to travel from the satellite to Earth. Due to the distance the signal must travel, latency can be higher compared to terrestrial connections. This can affect real-time activities, such as video conferencing or online gaming, where even small delays can be noticeable.
High cost: Satellite internet tends to be more expensive compared to other connectivity options. Service prices are higher than other types of internet, due to the high costs of equipment, operation, and satellites.
Weather conditions: The proper functioning of satellite internet can depend on good weather conditions. For the use of the satellite dish, a clear sky is needed. Signal stability could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
Data limitations: Many satellite internet providers apply monthly data caps to their plans. This means that users have a limited amount of data they can download and upload during a given period. If this limit is exceeded, the speed may be reduced or additional charges may apply.




Step 2 → Advantages and disadvantages of the WiMax connection

Advantages

High fluidity and low latency: This allows for a fast and fluid connection with low latency.
Does not require residential telephone service: It is not a requirement to have a telephone line to access the Internet service.
VoIP calls: There will be companies that, with the installation of this technology, will allow you to make VoIP calls (a technology that allows you to make and receive voice calls over the Internet).

Disadvantages

Direct contact with the repeater is necessary: This means that the antenna you install in your house must be oriented directly to the site from where the connection is being sent, and if possible, avoiding obstacles that prevent direct vision, such as trees or buildings. This can sometimes make it necessary to install intermediate connection points to overcome obstacles.
Asymmetric speeds: which means that the download speed will be much higher than the upload speed. WiMAX connections can reach speeds of up to 1Gbps at fixed points, for example, a house, and 365Mbps at mobile points. Even so, it will always depend on what the company you contract the service from offers you.
Congestion traffic: Speed could be affected more easily during peak hours.




Step 3 → Advantages and disadvantages of the Starlink connection

Advantages

Easy installation: The user buys a kit and can mount it autonomously.
High fluidity and low latency: High-speed, low-latency broadband internet. It will have latencies of around 20ms, compared to the average of 600ms.
High flexibility and mobility: Starlink also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have Internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, making it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
Possibility of a full refund of the equipment cost in the first month: If you purchase the service directly from Starlink, there is this possibility: “Try it for 30 days and, if you are not satisfied, return the equipment and get a full refund,” says Starlink on its website.

Disadvantages

Weather conditions: The proper functioning of satellite internet can depend on good weather conditions. For the use of the satellite dish, a clear sky is needed. Signal stability could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
High cost: Starlink’s satellite internet tends to be more expensive compared to other connectivity options. This is due to the high costs associated with launching and maintaining satellites, as well as the infrastructure needed on Earth for the operation of ground stations. The cost of this service is 300,000 COP** per month with a one-time payment for the equipment of **1,900,000 COP.
Capacity limitations: Since the Starlink system relies on satellites in low orbit, capacity is limited and shared among users in a given area. In congested areas, this could result in reduced speed during peak hours.
Interference problems: Some reports suggest that Starlink may experience interference problems, especially in densely populated areas or regions with high satellite activity.
Environmental impact: The deployment of thousands of satellites in low orbit has raised concerns about the environmental impact and the generation of space debris.
Need for direct view of the sky: To use Starlink, it is necessary to have a direct view of the sky, which may limit its viability in areas with significant obstructions such as tall trees or buildings.




Step 4 → How to choose the best option for my community?

Now that you are clearer about what each of the three options consists of, their advantages and disadvantages, you can make a more informed decision together with your community. We consider the following to be important elements when choosing an option:


Availability
Although we did this analysis in 2024 for Colombia, it may be useful for other countries. However, the first thing is to contact the companies that offer internet services in your region; they will be able to guide you better and tell you if they offer WiMax technology. But remember, their interest is to sell, but you are the one who decides. Satellite internet and Starlink have global coverage, so they will not depend exclusively on the providers in your region.


Budget
First of all, define what your budget will be; for this, you can calculate how many days of work you are willing to invest together with your community to contract this service. Don’t get into debt for an internet plan!



Photo: Maxi Gagliano - Pexels


Reliability
It is important to know if the company you selected has a good reputation or not. You can find this out from other users who have hired them, and it will be vital when you have any inconvenience or have to do any type of equipment maintenance.


Usage habits
Depending on what your community uses the internet for, you can choose a technology that benefits you more. Here you can evaluate if latency is important because you need to make video calls or play online, if you are willing to contract a monthly payment service, or simply, since the use is occasional, you only pay for the internet service in the months of greatest use, or if these options are simply not the most appropriate and you prefer to continue without an internet connection.



Don’t be fooled
Define your usage and number of devices to estimate the speed and Bandwidth → needed, and then evaluate the available technology (satellite is a common option) and the reliability and technical support of the provider.
Research the provider’s reputation with neighbors and ask if they offer specific plans for rural areas. The upload speed, download speed, and latency must be adequate for your activities, and it is useful to ask about data restrictions and the quality of the provider’s infrastructure.

How much is enough?
One of these three solutions may be the right one to solve connectivity in your region, because they are all designed for places far from cities and do not depend on a wired internet service for their operation.
You can take into account the following criteria and think about them in terms of the people and the content you need to access:

For basic use (emails, social networks, browsing): A moderate download speed and a basic data plan might be enough.
For streaming and online work: A higher download speed and greater bandwidth are required to avoid interruptions.
For intensive upload use (cloud, large files): It is important to look for a symmetric connection, where the upload speed is close to the download speed.

en/solve/solv-choose-satellite-internet.title: Which satellite internet should I choose based on my needs?
en/solve/solv-choose-satellite-internet.content:
Hi, I’m Nicolás, and like you, I’ve been learning about how to improve my internet connection. I’m not an expert on the subject, but by searching, following tutorials, and learning through trial and error, I have worked on improving internet quality in places that lack good connectivity.
In this particular solution, we will understand the criteria for choosing which satellite internet best fits our connectivity needs. We will also face some ethical questions that may influence our choice.
Our advice: decide with your head and your heart, choosing the option that best serves your needs and those of your community.
What does it mean to choose satellite internet with criteria?
Satellite internet is a technology designed so that the internet signal is sent via a satellite located in orbit to the satellite dish at your home or business.
With satellite internet, you can connect computers, cell phones →, tablets, etc. This technology does not require the cabling used by, for example, fiber optic internet.

What is it for?
This solution is for you to decide which satellite internet is best for you to purchase if you are located in a place that does not have an internet connection.
In this solution, we will address the advantages and disadvantages of three different solutions so that you can make a conscious and responsible decision: satellite dish, WiMax, or Starlink.
Before starting, we suggest that, if you decide to purchase any of the options presented in this solution, you pay for it together with other people so that you can enjoy community use of the internet.

Before starting, some ethical questions
Do you believe that all people, regardless of where they are, should have access to the internet? In Colombia, for example, a 2021 legislative act established and elevated the internet as a fundamental right, making it an obligation to expand internet coverage to unconnected communities and territories. For their part, international organizations like the UN state that denying access to the internet is like denying the right to freedom of expression.
This may sound very good, but the reality is complex and unequal. On one hand, not all people and communities have the internet: about a third of the world’s population remains without an internet connection, some 2.6 billion people. It is not profitable for companies that offer internet to reach places where there is no infrastructure, as the possibilities for profitability are lower. This expands and maintains inequity regarding internet access. On the other hand, the deployment of thousands of satellites in low earth orbit has raised concerns about the environmental impact and the generation of space debris.
So, at SOLE Colombia, we see satellite internet as one of the existing options, especially designed for places that do not have an internet connection or nearby telecommunications towers to distribute it. If this is not your case, perhaps you can find a more conscious solution tailored to your needs in the content of this guide.

How do I know if I need this solution?
Before we begin, we would like to ask you a few questions:

Do you currently have fiber optic or mobile internet of fair or good quality?
Where you live, can you see telecommunications towers that distribute the internet?
Are there companies that can offer you an internet service at a good cost?

If your answer was yes to any of these questions, we recommend that you continue with your mobile or fiber optic internet and look for other solutions on SOLE Voltaje → that allow you to improve your internet connection. But don’t go! We invite you to continue reading this guide so you can learn more about satellite internet and make your own decisions.
If, on the other hand, you answered “no” to all the previous questions, you have a poor internet connection and have already checked other solutions, we invite you to continue reading this solution.

Options to review
In this solution, we will work with three technologies available in Colombia: Satellite internet, WiMax, and Starlink for the year 2024. The estimated reading time for this solution is about 15 minutes, but don’t be scared, you can read these recommendations with the help of other people. Remember that at SOLE Voltaje, we want to promote the collective use of the internet.

Satellite internet
The most popular internet option in rural areas is satellite internet. Although the name is self-explanatory, it is an internet connection via satellites. The great advantage of this option is that it can reach anywhere, including the most remote rural areas! To access this technology, the company will need to install a satellite dish at your home.



WiMax
The operation of WiMAX is simple, as it is a repeater from the company you want to hire emitting microwave signals that reach your antenna. Therefore, the first thing you need to do is contact a company that offers these services and has a repeater near your house to be able to send you the signal. Then, you have to put an antenna on the facade of your house. This antenna will have to point directly to the service provider’s repeater or to an intermediate connection point used to overcome obstacles between your antenna and their repeater. The installation of the antenna will be done by the company itself.


_Image taken from Wikipedia

Starlink
Starlink is Elon Musk’s satellite internet project. It is a private satellite internet that facilitates connections, especially in rural areas. The company is considered the first and largest satellite constellation in the world that uses a low earth orbit to offer broadband, high-speed, and low-latency satellite internet. This allows for streaming content, online gaming, video calls, and more.

To put it into operation, the user buys a kit with everything necessary, most notably the antenna, which must be placed outdoors and automatically orients itself to establish a connection in a matter of minutes, provided it has a clear sky.

_Image taken from Starlink

We already have an introduction to the available options; now we want you to know the criteria you should take into account to choose the option that suits you best.

What should I take into account to make this decision?
Availability: Are these options available for the place where I live?
Although we conducted this analysis in 2024 for Colombia, it may be useful for other countries. To know the availability of these three options, you must take into account that, unlike WiMax, Satellite internet and Starlink have global coverage, so they will not depend exclusively on the providers in your region. For the WiMax option, the first thing you should do is contact the companies that offer internet services in your region; they will be able to guide you and tell you if they actually offer this technology.
Budget: How much money can I pay?

The cost of WiMax service can start from 150,000 COP** per month with a payment for equipment between **300,000 COP and $2,000,000 COP depending on the company you want to hire.
The cost of satellite internet service can start from 150,000 COP** per month with a payment for equipment between **300,000 COP and $2,000,000 COP depending on the company you want to hire.
The cost of Starlink service can start from 180,000 COP** per month with a one-time payment for the equipment of **1,900,000 COP.

Weather conditions: Can the weather affect the internet signal?

In the case of Starlink and Satellite internet, the quality of the internet will depend on weather conditions. For the use of a satellite dish, a clear sky is needed; for this reason, the stability of the signal could be compromised by rain or thunderstorms.
In the case of WiMax, keep in mind that direct contact with the repeater is necessary; this means that the antenna you install at your house must be oriented directly to the site where the connection is being sent, and if possible, avoiding obstacles that prevent direct line-of-sight, such as trees or buildings. Sometimes it may be necessary to install intermediate connection points to overcome obstacles.

Signal and coverage: Which option offers me the best quality?

The advantage of Satellite internet is that it has global coverage, which means that people living in remote regions or rural areas can access the internet reliably. One of the most prominent advantages of satellite internet is its ability to provide a constant and stable connection. Unlike terrestrial connections that can be affected by infrastructure interruptions or adverse weather conditions, satellite internet does not depend on cables. This guarantees a reliable and continuous connection, even in areas prone to natural disasters.
However, the disadvantage of satellite internet is that many providers offer a limited amount of data that can be downloaded and uploaded during a certain period. If this limit is exceeded, the speed may be reduced or additional charges may apply.
In the case of WiMax, the advantage is that a residential telephone service is not needed. It is not a requirement to have a telephone line to access the internet service.
However, a disadvantage is that the download speed will be much higher than the upload speed. WiMAX connections can reach speeds of up to 1Gbps at fixed points, for example, a house, and 365Mbps at mobile points. Even so, it will always depend on what the company you hire offers you. Also, keep in mind that the speed could be affected more easily during peak hours.
For its part, Starlink offers an easy installation that you and your community can carry out: the company offers the user the purchase of a kit with the necessary instructions to assemble it. Starlink also offers flexibility and mobility. You can have internet access from anywhere covered by the satellite signal, making it an ideal option for people who travel frequently, remote workers, or those who need connectivity in temporary or expanding areas.
However, since the Starlink system is based on satellites in low orbit, the capacity is limited and shared among users in a given area. In congested areas, this could result in reduced speed during peak hours, although its coverage is improving more and more. Some reports suggest that Starlink may experience interference issues, especially in densely populated areas or regions with high satellite activity. For this reason, keep in mind that to use Starlink, it is necessary to have a direct view of the sky, which may limit its viability in areas with significant obstructions such as tall trees or buildings.

What signal speed do I need?
By latency →, we refer to the time it takes for the signal to travel from the satellite to Earth. In the case of Starlink, the broadband internet is high-speed and low-latency. It will have latencies of around 20ms, compared to the average of 600ms.
For its part, WiMax allows for a fast and fluid connection with low latencies.
However, the speed of satellite internet can be lower compared to terrestrial connections. This can affect real-time activities, such as video conferencing or online gaming, where even small delays can be noticeable.
