en/solve/solv-community-meeting-space.title: How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet as a group?
en/solve/solv-community-meeting-space.content:
Hi, I’m Manu. As a SOLE Explorer, I’ve had to learn how to request community spaces in the places where we’ve gone to conduct SOLEs, and I know it’s not always easy to know where to start.

What is requesting a community hall, or any community space?
This is a solution that guides you on how you can reserve a common space to use the Internet as a group, or for whatever else you want to do in this space. Remember that each space has its own rules and application procedures, so this solution can guide you on the criteria, but it is not a definitive solution.
If you have any suggestions on how you do it in your community that you think might help other people, I invite you to comment on the solution—we create the Internet together!

What is it for?
At SOLE Colombia, we believe it’s more fun when we do things together. Community spaces are places for us to meet others, to connect, to celebrate, to share, and you can use them too.
Here I will tell you some steps you can follow to reserve the community hall closest to you. Good luck!

What do you need?

A good attitude, believe in yourself.
Identity document to sign the reservation (optional).
A letter to request the reservation of the space (optional).


How to do it?

Step 1 → Discover the place and go there

Once you decide where you want to carry out your activity, go to the community hall and talk to the people in charge.
Introduce yourself to them and tell them why you want to use the space, what for, and how many people have confirmed.
Encourage them to participate in your activity as well; for example, if you are going to do a SOLE, you can invite them to become participants.



Step 2 → Ask about the requirements, what you need to formalize the request


Once you are in contact with the people in charge, ask them what availability there is at the place and what requirements you need, or how you can reserve it.


Step 3 → Write the reservation letter or meet the venue’s requirements

Generally, community halls request a letter to be able to reserve the place.
Write what the activity will consist of, when it will take place, and who the organizers and participants will be.
Also, it is very important that you include your contact details; they will need them to be able to confirm if it is possible for your activity to take place at the time you have planned.
We also advise you to include a few words of thanks for the authorization to use the space.
You may need to attach a photocopy of your identity document, so be prepared for that.
Do you think an example could help you? Here we leave you the steps to keep in mind and what the example would look like:

Include the place and date where you are.
Head the letter with the name or designation of the person, or entity, that owns or manages the space.
Introduce yourself as the person responsible for the request or the organization of the activity.
Explain the purpose of the activity and its details. You can also request items you need to carry out your activity, for example, chairs, tables, computers, or other elements you require that are within reach of the person providing the hall.
Thank them for their attention and inform them how they can respond to you. It can be your phone number or some other way to contact you.
Finally, sign the letter.

This is what this written formula would look like:


💡 El Montecillo Village
Municipality of Arracachal
February 13, 2038
Good morning,
My name is (your full name), I am identified with ID No. (ID Number), and I am contacting you to request the use of the (name of the space or meeting hall) to carry out an activity, in the company of people from the community.
My idea is to use the space to learn, dialogue, and solve some challenges in my community that we will identify in the meeting, using the Internet as a group.
The details of the meeting are:

Date: (day of the week), (day) of (month) of (year)
Time: at (time)
Number of people: (number) people will meet
Duration of the meeting: (time)

To carry out the activity, we need some conditions and furniture: one chair per person, some tables where we can place some computers, and the possibility of plugging them in (so they don’t run out of battery). It is also necessary to have electricity and an Internet connection available.
We commit to taking care of the common space and complying with the rules of use in this space for everyone.
You can contact me at (phone number) or through (other contact method).
Thank you very much for your attention, I look forward to hearing from you.
(Name of the person signing).



Remember that this is just an example; you can draft the letter however you want. Don’t forget to ask the person in charge what information, data, or attachments you must include in the document.


Step 4 → Request a contact for follow-up and ask for confirmation, don’t wait too long

It may happen that your confirmation requires going through some filters or that the process takes a while. Although you shouldn’t lose your cool, it doesn’t hurt to ask for the contact person’s details to follow up on the process; this way, you will ensure that you can plan and make your activity a reality within the deadlines you had devised.


Step 5 → Thank them for the management and celebrate, you have found an ally in your community!

Once they confirm that you can use the space, don’t forget to thank the person in charge with whom you were in contact from the beginning.
You can send them an email, a WhatsApp message, or greet them on the street, reminding them how important their support was in getting the activity carried out. They are a good ally for future occasions when you want to use the community hall again.

You can share your experience reserving the community hall of your village, community, or housing complex with others :) Remember that learning in a group is very powerful, and your experience can help or inspire others!

Other possible internets
Once you have your space reserved, it’s just a matter of iterating the process as many times as you need. Perhaps you can make a broader request that lasts longer. For this, it may be useful to make use of the good news, findings, and successes of the activity you have proposed in the space and how it is bearing fruit in the community.
For example, when you manage to get a group of people to do SOLEs recurrently, you will be able to verify the benefits it has for skills such as communication, negotiation, reading comprehension, digital competencies, autonomy, and leadership… making a small report, for example, with the result of the Reflection capsules (available on the SOLE Colombia website n9.cl/reflexionatusole), can be very powerful to strengthen the relationship with your ally and with the people in your community.

What can you achieve with this solution?
Sometimes, procedures that involve large entities, or that involve the decision of many people, can take time. It is important that, at the time of the request, you are clear about the deadlines and can set reminders to follow up on your petition.
Often, it is enough to remind the person with whom you made the request, stop by to say hello kindly, and remind them that you are waiting for an answer. They will appreciate your attention and will surely put more care into having an answer to give you.

en/solve/solv-create-poweful-message.title: How to mobilize others for your cause?
en/solve/solv-create-poweful-message.content:
Hello! I’m Manu, the storyteller for SOLE Colombia, and today I want to talk to you about the power of a message.
If you are here, it is because you want to learn how you can mobilize others with your cause and build a powerful message. Shall we do it together?
What is creating a powerful message?
In this solution, we are going to dive into a very special methodology in the world of storytelling: the Golden Circle, created by Simon Sinek. We will use this step-by-step methodology to help you develop a clear and powerful message.
Through the three fundamental questions posed by Sinek, I will guide you to unravel the message behind your cause. When you summon others with a clear and powerful message, you make them feel deeply connected to you.
Get ready, because this is going to be exciting!

What is it for?
Creating a powerful message, focused on purpose, involves connecting emotionally with your audience and inspiring them to take action. It serves to inspire others, appealing to their emotions and values, creating a deeper and more meaningful connection. You will create more coherent and consistent communication.

What do you need?

Paper.
Pen/Pencil or any digital tool.
And, of course, enthusiasm.


How to do it?

file.notion.so/f/f/d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a/a6e3ad9c-19b6-46e9-8ef3-2184ad609e21/Vdeo_sin_ttulo__Hecho_con_Clipchamp_(5).mp4?table=block&id=12a2bd68-c5b6-81cc-a580-d32a8d9dbe02&spaceId=d2a8cf29-6055-4dd9-8971-801014f46b2a&expirationTimestamp=1764108000000&signature=cF6F8pUItq0BKbFpFL9XY_q_cAeRXqgTtKC6-I3s08Q&downloadName=V%C3%ADdeo+sin+t%C3%ADtulo+%E2%80%90+Hecho+con+Clipchamp+%285%29.mp4

Step 1 → Start with the what
What is it that you do or want to do? What do you want to share or offer the world? That is the “what” of your message. Starting with the what will help you glimpse your why more easily.
Here your ideas take shape and become tangible actions: a product, a service, or an offer.
Activity: To discover it, I invite you to write on a blank sheet of paper what you are doing or offering in tangible terms… A SOLE? An activity? A product?
If you still have doubts, use the examples to start your golden circle. Cheer up!



Step 2 → Define the how
We are on the right track! With the purpose clear, the rest follows… Now that you know that flame that moves you, it’s time to think about how to fuel it and take your message to the world. What strategies, actions, or methods will you use to make your why shine?
The moment has arrived to determine the methods and processes you will use to carry out your “what.” For this step, you need to know how you do what you do to fulfill your motivation. Think about whether it is a format that makes you unique, a product that no one else had thought of, or an original service that you offer. Here, what matters are the qualities.
Activity:

Write a list on a sheet of paper of the activities you do to fulfill your “what” and select the ones you find most relevant.
Now put them all in the same place and draft your how.

See how I did it to guide you:




Step 3 → Give shape to your why
To finish, it is necessary that you are clear about the fundamental purpose behind the message. What is the inspiring reason that motivates you?
When we are clear about our “why,” we create an emotional bond with our audience, awakening their interest and commitment from a deeper level.
Activity: To discover the why of your message, grab a blank sheet of paper and write down the first thing that comes to your head. Don’t overthink it. It’s okay if it’s just a few words; little by little they will take shape 😉 This is how my why turned out:


Tip: Think about what it is that motivates you to do what you are doing, and you will see that the words will appear little by little.

Other possible internets
There you have it, your why is ready, and thus your message is much more powerful. Now you can have more clarity when you want to infect others with your purpose or that of your product. Remember, the most important thing is that it is authentic, that it reflects your essence, and that it makes you feel identified.
Now it’s your time to shine! Go ahead, conquer the world with your message! 🚀 Show us in the comments what your Golden Circle looks like!

Why might this solution work?
Your message must reflect your purpose, that which drives you to action. It must be authentic and resonate with the people who listen to you.
Aligning your messages and your actions with your purpose makes communication coherent; take care of it. If your message is genuine, authentic, and reflects your true passion, you will be honoring your why.
It is very important that your message creates an emotional connection with the recipient; remember that only when we create emotional bonds with others do we manage to have words truly touch the hearts of others.
Remember! The goal of a powerful message is to motivate others to do something, to take action, and to follow you, be inspired, connect, and be motivated to follow your vision.

en/solve/solv-discover-audience.title: How to reach the people who will value your message the most?
en/solve/solv-discover-audience.content:
Hello! 😊
I’m Manu, and I was a storyteller at SOLE Colombia for several years. Among all the stories I spend my time telling, I always keep in mind who I am directing my words to… have you ever wondered how to really reach the people who will value your message the most, or who will participate in your projects?
In this solution, we are going to discover your audience together. Are you ready?
What is discovering your audience?
Knowing your audience means deeply understanding who the people you are directing your content to are. When you know your audience, you can focus your efforts where you know they will have an impact. What good is it to send a message by email if what you want is to invite your family?
Knowing your audience is knowing by heart the shortest path to reach the hearts of your people, and connecting with the right people so that your message goes further.

What is it for?
When you know who you are addressing and you know them well, it allows you to adapt your message, tone, and communication style so that it resonates with the people you are addressing and what you say resonates with them.
You will create more relevant content for those people, suited to their interests and needs, that is useful, interesting, and valuable to them… without a doubt, you will improve the way they perceive you, but most importantly, you will be able to create genuine and authentic connections because your message will reach them straight to the heart.

What do you need?

Paper
Pen/Pencil
Enthusiasm
Cell phone or computer (to write and carry out the activities)


How to do it?

Step 1 → Define your ‘target audience’ in detail

Before starting, clearly establish who the people you want to reach with your message or call are… Think about the key characteristics of the people you want to reach.
Take out your pencil or pen and answer on a sheet of paper:

What are the interests, needs, or challenges of your audience?
What type of people would be most interested in what you have to offer?

See how I did with this exercise:



Step 2 → Create your characters, dig deeper to create your ideal persona

Keeping in mind the answers to the questions below, create detailed profiles of your target audience. This will help you visualize and better understand who you are addressing and what motivates them.

Discover their characteristics: write down the basic qualities of your ideal audience, such as age, gender, geographic location, education level, etc.
Interests and motivations: describe what motivates or interests these people; what are they looking for or what do they need?
Behaviors and preferences: where do they usually spend their time? What type of content do they consume or what activities do they enjoy?
Challenges: what are the things that prevent them from getting where they want to go or where you want to invite them? What are the challenges they face?

When you have finished this exercise, it will be easier to visualize your ideal audience. See how I did it:



Step 3 → Observe and listen to your people, look for answers

Now that you have a clear idea of who your potential participants are, it is time to observe and listen.

Start interacting with your potential audience through surveys, interviews, or simply by observing their interactions online.
Note down any responses, comments, or patterns that help you better understand their needs and preferences, and spread your message while keeping their reactions or behaviors in mind.



Other possible internets
It is very important that you invent ways to analyze how your audience lets you know that you are reaching them. How can you tell?
Observe: how do the people who interact with your messages behave? Talk to them directly, invent easy ways to collect data about their experiences, opinions, expectations… you can design a survey or form to obtain more data and be able to process it statistically.
Looking for patterns, trends, and motivations can lead you to more qualitative analyses, where you can find more complex and interesting explanations about your audience.
It is exciting to find the best way to communicate with those people you want to reach! Constantly ask yourself questions about them so you can communicate better and better.
Is it working for you? Write to me and tell me!

What can you achieve with this solution?
Often, as you better define your audience, you realize that there are subgroups you want to approach, and you necessarily have to do it differently.
For example, at SOLE Colombia, we have a very large community in which there are different ‘characters’ we speak to. We cannot speak to the Grandmas in the same way we speak to the Tinkerer/Handy folks, because it simply wouldn’t work. The content we create aims to accommodate all of them, but by directing specific messages to each group, building community from the affection we give to each collective.
That is what we do! We give a lot of thought to the ways we communicate and the audiences we are discovering. Experimenting continuously. Adapting to the findings. And doing it all over again. Many times. To connect more and more with people.
Now it’s your turn! Cheer up, it’s fun!

en/solve/solv-donated-equipment.title: How to get donated equipment?
en/solve/solv-donated-equipment.content:
slug: solv-donatedequipment
Hello, are you there? My name is Mateo and I will accompany you in the development of this solution. If you are reading, listening to, or watching this, it is because you are interested or curious about how to obtain donated equipment. If so, you are in the right place.

What is obtaining donated equipment?
In short, this solution is about reuse. It is about being consistent with caring for the world we live in; it is about taking advantage of things that are obsolete to others, but that we can perhaps use for much longer.
This solution serves to give a second chance to equipment that is no longer needed. Did you know that there are companies that want to upgrade their equipment and donate what they have? This equipment is usually in good condition and your community could take advantage of it.

What is this solution for?
While this solution does not require money to purchase equipment, keep in mind that it can take weeks, or even months, depending on the steps we will tell you about below. For your part, you have a better chance of receiving a donation if you demonstrate that the use of the equipment will be communal and that its purpose is to improve people’s quality of life.

What do you need?

Persistence.
Patience.
Support from others. Teamwork increases the chances of success.


How to do it?
Let’s get started!
This solution is developed in three steps in which we will tell you everything we know and have learned at the SOLE Colombia Foundation about how to get donated equipment. All cases are different, so it is important that you are willing to adapt these steps depending on the difficulties you encounter along the way.

Photo: veerasak Piyawatanakul - Pexels


Step 1 → Find the donor company and identify the relationship model

Generally, equipment donors are companies with great economic capacity, payroll, and infrastructure. Think of telephone or computer companies, universities, or find out about the sponsors of social projects in your region. However, we suggest you start with small companies. For this, you have two options:

Option 1: Direct search

You can search for companies or people who donate equipment through the internet, social networks, or by consulting your contact networks or close circles.

💬 For option 1, make a list of the companies and the ways you have to contact them; it could be through the people who manage the organization’s finances or those who manage the computer equipment.
The key is to get a direct contact at the donor company with whom you can speak in person, send an email, make a call, or send a letter. If you send a letter or an email, make sure it will be read and, in case they are not the person responsible for making that decision, ensure they will redirect it to the person you need.


Option 2: Dissemination

You can write a message or post on social networks making it explicit that: 1. you need donated equipment in good condition; 2. you have a community project in which many people will benefit; 3. write the number where they can contact you; 4. Be clear about who you are and try to make the message evoke empathy and trust. An example of a message could be:


“Hello everyone! My name is Amaranta and I am part of the XYZ FOUNDATION. Does anyone know of organizations that are donating computer equipment in good condition? We are looking for support to implement a project with older adults in rural areas of Colombia. Any information or contact would be of great help. Thank you!
My contact number is 123456789
We suggest you carry out both options at the same time, this will expand the possibilities you have to find a donor company.



💪🏽 Cheer up! At this moment, it is key that you are persistent. This does not have a magic formula; it is a matter of knocking on doors and opening paths. In any case, if you have read this far, it is because you already have the will to do it and that is to be admired.



Step 2 → Wait for your response and don’t let the contact “cool down.”


Photo by Fauxels: Pexels
Once you have sent the requests, all that remains is to wait and insist continuously to receive a response. Do not let the contact cool down; if more than a week passes without any response, write again or go in person if possible. When you get an affirmative response, be clear about the model in which you will receive the equipment: not all companies donate their equipment, some decide to give it away, so there are two types of models:


Option 1: Gifting equipment

You may find a company or person who gives away their equipment. Family members can give away equipment. When you contact them, make sure of the modality in which you will actually receive the equipment in this arrangement.


Option 2: Donating equipment

Now, in the case of companies that donate, it is a different model in which a second chance is given to equipment that is in good condition and can be used by people and communities that need it.
How does it work? Many companies have to make updates that require changing their equipment or need new technologies to carry out their work, so they decide to donate and thus can receive a tax deduction.

⚠️ Keep in mind that, for this to be possible, donor companies need to receive a donation certificate. If you are not part of a foundation, you must find an ally who can issue this certificate for you.

Who and how is this certificate issued for companies that want to donate? To find an ally, think of a non-profit entity that has an active legal status and can issue these certificates for the companies that will donate the equipment. For example, foundations, cooperatives, or similar entities in your region. Talk to them and tell them about your purpose. If they decide to support you, ask them for guidance in this process.
We invite you to look up the story of Alex Cortés, an engineer who founded Fundación Click → with the goal of giving a second life to computers that many people, organizations, or companies no longer need; he decides to repair them, perform maintenance, and give them away or donate them to those who need them most. If you want to know more about his story, we invite you to look up him, his foundation, and his history.

⚠️⚠️ Important: you must be clear about how the equipment will be used, since legally the equipment will belong to the ally you found. Don’t forget to check that the equipment they give you is functional. We don’t want you to end up storing technological trash that you will have to repair.



Step 3 → Receiving the equipment and building the relationship


Photo: Ketut Subiyanto - Pexels

Photo: Cytonn photography - Pexels
For the reception of the equipment, in either of the two modalities, keep in mind that each company or person has their own procedure.
The delivery of the equipment can be a shipment, you may have to pick it up, or reach an agreement on the place of delivery with the company or person who will make the donation. After delivery, it is important to know what kind of relationship you want and can build with them:


Option 1: Gifting equipment

In this modality, paperwork is usually not required to formalize the delivery. However, it is likely that donors will seek to establish a short or medium-term relationship to know the destination and use of the equipment. If this is your case, we suggest you make it explicit and maintain cordial communication with them.

For example, although it is not mandatory, at the SOLE Colombia Foundation, we usually formalize the process through a thank-you letter signed by both parties, where the delivery, the condition of the equipment, and our commitment to make good use of them are corroborated.



Option 2: Donating equipment

For the delivery, make a donation request explaining your interests, conditions, and the cooperation you will build.
How many computers do you need? What condition is the equipment you are going to receive in? What does the donor company need from you? What will you use the equipment for? Who will be the people and communities benefited? For this option, we suggest that, as in option 1, you consider the possibility of building a bond with the donor company.

At SOLE Colombia we usually send the donor companies photographs that thank them and show the communal use of the equipment, with which we try to open the possibilities for future donations.


What does the communal use of equipment imply?
Do you remember what we mentioned at the beginning of this solution about the possibilities you can have of receiving a donation if you demonstrate that the use of the equipment will be communal? Now we invite you to reflect on the importance that the collective use of equipment can have in a community. It is not just about receiving them, but about reaching agreements on who will manage them, how they will use them, and how often; this will involve fostering dialogue and teamwork. It is not about having a lot of equipment, but about knowing how to use it in a community.

See you soon! We invite you to investigate other solutions and keep tinkering.


Other possible internets
When you receive equipment that others do not use, you have proven that this solution works. You will also have created a relationship with someone; that is beautiful and powerful. Someone who has tuned into your purpose and wants to give you a hand.
As you create new relationships, you will feel increasingly confident in finding potential donors. Now that you have equipment, would you be encouraged to do another solution? Browse more Voltaje solutions →

What can you achieve with this solution?
When you cultivate the relationship with your donors, it is possible that they can make donations more than once. Can you imagine if they donated a few computers to you every year? What would you do then with all that equipment?

If you want to know what we do at SOLE Colombia with the computers that are donated to us, take a look at www.solecolombia.org

Thinking about how you can extend this benefit to others is a way to make this world a fairer place. Would you like to try it in your community? Was this solution useful to you? We hope so! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

en/solve/solv-endless.title: Un pedazo de Internet en computadores sin conexión
en/solve/solv-endless.content:
If you are reading this, it is because, like me, you are the type of person who doesn’t sit still and likes to “tinker” with computers so they serve for more than just typing in Word.
I have spent many hours fighting with Dual Boot installations, partitions that get erased, and USB drives that won’t boot. That is why I want to give you a hand so you can take “a piece of the internet” where it is needed most, without failing in the attempt. Installing Endless OS is like putting a giant library into an old or new computer, and here I explain how to do it like a “tinkering” professional.
What is this solution for?
Endless OS is not just a program; it is a complete Operating System → designed to work where the internet is a luxury. It comes with Wikipedia, cooking courses, health manuals, and educational games already downloaded. For a SOLE, it is the perfect tool: it allows children to look for answers to their Big Questions even if the router → is turned off.
What do you need for this mission?

A computer with Windows (which is where we will normally “coexist”).
Internet connection (only for the initial download).
A USB → drive of at least 32GB (if you are going to use the memory stick method).
Disk space: At least 32GB free on the computer.
Lots of patience and a desire to experiment.

How to do it?
1. The initial “Check-up”
Before downloading anything, check if the computer has space. In Windows, open the file explorer and make sure the “C: Drive” is not red. If you are going to install the full version (the one with the content), you need about 20GB to 32GB free.

Tinkerer’s trick: If the internet is very slow in the library, use a download manager like jdownloader. If the power or Wi-Fi cuts out, you won’t lose what you have already downloaded.

2. Download: Windows Installer or ISO Image?
If you go to the official Endless site, you will see two options:

Windows Installer: It is the easiest. It is a .exe program that you install as if it were a game. It creates an automatic Dual Boot. When you turn on the PC, it will ask you: “Do you want to enter Windows or Endless?“.
ISO Image: This is for the more advanced users. It allows you to create a USB that “formats” the PC or runs from the memory stick. You will need balenaEtcher to “burn” the ISO onto the USB. This option is good if the computer does not have Windows or if you want to use Endless without touching the existing Windows installation.

3. The installation (The moment of truth)
If you use the Windows installer:

Double-click the file.
Select “Install alongside Windows”.
Choose the “Full” version. Don’t hesitate! The basic version is like a desert without internet; the Full version is the one that brings Wikipedia and videos.
Let the PC work. If it seems to get stuck at 99%, don’t turn it off. It is moving heavy files.

4. The “Jump to BIOS” (If the USB doesn’t boot)
If you decided to use a USB and the computer ignores the memory and goes straight into Windows, you have to enter the BIOS/UEFI.

The trick: As soon as you turn on the PC, repeatedly press F2, F12, or Delete (depending on the brand). Look for the “Boot” tab and put the USB first in the list.

Collective Glossary (To speak the same language)
As we agreed, here we are building the meaning of the strange words we use. If you find another one, write it down on the SOLE wall!

Operating System (OS): It is the main program that makes the computer work. Examples: Windows, Linux, Android, Endless OS.
Dual Boot: It is having two operating systems on the same computer. When you turn it on, you choose which one to use. It’s like having a house with two doors.
ISO Image: It is a file that contains the entire operating system packaged, ready to be “burned” onto a USB or DVD.
BIOS / UEFI: It is the most basic program of the computer that tells it what parts it has and which disk should boot first.
Bootable USB: A USB memory stick prepared so that the computer can boot (start) an operating system from it.
Partition: It is dividing the hard drive into several “virtual” parts, as if you put walls in a room so that two people can live separately.

Final “Tinkerer” Recommendations

Update before you leave: If you already have Endless installed and still have internet, open it and let it update. Once in the field (without a connection), you won’t be able to download new programs easily.
Test the search engine: Open the Endless search engine and type “Dinosaurs” or “Ozone layer”. If Wikipedia articles with photos appear, you did it! You have a piece of the internet in your hands.
The forum is your friend: If something fails, search Google for the error followed by the words “Endless OS forum”. There is always someone who has already gone through that problem and left the solution.

How far can you go?
Having Endless is like having an offline library. It is not the infinite internet of Google, but to look for answers in a SOLE (How to do a SOLE? →), it is a thousand times better than an empty computer.

en/solve/solv-express-invite.title: Learn how to design an express invitation without being an expert!
en/solve/solv-express-invite.content:
Hi! I’m Manuela and I’m not a professional designer, but that’s what tinkering (cacharreo) is all about: learning autonomously, solving by doing. I love designing, drawing, and creating. In fact, making collages is one of my favorite hobbies. And today, I would like to share how to make an invitation based on my experience.
Here I will talk mainly about the form, that is, how to make an invitation in general terms. You can also consult the solution How to write a good invitation? → if you are more interested in some recommendations regarding content.

What is designing an invitation, without being an expert?
Have you ever felt that you don’t know how to make an invitation as pretty as the ones other people make?
Designing an invitation consists of choosing the graphic elements (such as the font color, the accompanying images, etc.) through which you will make an invitation message striking and attractive.
Invitations can be handmade or digital; choose whichever you prefer! In this solution, you will find tips for both. Shall we start?

💡 Remember that this solution is focused more on form than content. You don’t need to have design experience to start designing.


What is it for?
Very quickly: an invitation is used to convene. When we organize activities or events that we want different people to attend, the invitation is the first contact we have with them and, therefore, the most important opportunity to attract their attention.
Whether by hand or using digital tools, you can create a powerful invitation. Keep reading and I’ll tell you how to make an excellent invitation.

What do you need?

If you are going to make your digital invitation: a computer, tablet, or phone with Internet access.
If you are going to make it by hand: colored paper, colored pencils, markers, and felt-tip pens.
Creativity.
Freedom to express whatever you want.


How to do it?
Let’s start with the analog → Your invitation by hand or with traditional technique
To create your invitation by hand, keep in mind:
Color: make it look pretty

Use colored paper or whatever you have on hand and start bringing your invitation to life using colored pencils, markers, or felt-tip pens.
Add creative details like decorative borders, simple illustrations, or symbols that represent the essence of your event. You can also think about colored boxes to highlight information you consider valuable.
Play with different colors and shading techniques to make your design visually attractive and unique.

The text: say what is necessary

Write the event details so that they can be read well. You can use your own handwriting or cut and paste printed letters like those from newspapers, magazines, posters… you can even make some with modeling clay or other materials you have on hand!
Use the resources from the previous section to highlight essential information.
Be creative with the text and make sure it is clear to your guests. You can ask someone close to you for their opinion; several pairs of eyes always read better than just one.
Be careful not to overload it, otherwise, people might get lost in so much information… remember, ‘less is more’.

Review: a second look is always important

Review your design and add the finishing touches to perfect it; ask for opinions! I’m sure the input from people you trust will help.
Don’t forget to check the spelling of the words very carefully. A message that is well-written is understood well and does not lead to confusion; remember that your goal is for people to understand everything well and be able to attend what you are inviting them to.
If you want to get your invitation further, you can distribute it digitally: scan your creation or simply take a high-quality photo to distribute it via electronic messaging (email, WhatsApp, Telegram…) or social networks.



Now, let’s go digital → Venture to try the available technology
Log in to Canva
Canva is a design tool created so that anyone can use it. Open your browser and visit canva.com.
To start, you must have an account. If you don’t have one yet, you can create one for free. You only need to have an email address.

Select an invitation size
Once in Canva, choose the ideal size for your invitation. Canva offers you many options to start with (for example, standard postcard size, social media post, etc.).
You can also customize the dimensions according to your needs using the “custom size” button.

Choose a template or start from scratch
A template is a pre-designed file, meaning someone else already designed the content and you just need to enter and edit it.
Do you prefer to start with a template or let your creativity fly from scratch? Use the search engine to explore the wide variety of options that Canva offers and choose the style you like best:

Customize your design
Change the background and add elements like text, images, and decorations that represent the theme of your event. Experiment with different color combinations, fonts, and styles to make your invitation unique and exciting.
On the right side of the screen, you will find thousands of pre-designed graphic resources that you can choose and arrange as you wish. In the “uploads” option, you can upload your own photos, videos (yours or from a link on the internet like YouTube), or audio.
Don’t be afraid to try new ideas and adjust the details until your design shines!
Look at how mine turned out:

Download your invitation
When you are happy with your design, click the “Share” button and select the “Download” option. Then, choose the format you want (usually JPG or PNG for images and PDF for longer files) and click the download button in the box that appears.

You can find your invitation in your computer’s “downloads” folder. If you can’t find it, use your computer’s file search tool to locate it.
Congratulations, your invitation is ready to print or share online! We hope this solution has been useful to you. If it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

Other possible internets
The easiest way to know is by consulting an outside opinion to ensure the invitation is clear and striking. It is also useful to take a break or do some other activity and then return to review the invitation with “fresh eyes.” You can look at aspects such as:

Is the information clear enough (time, place…)? Is it easy to find and understand? Check the text, the font type, and the configuration of the text and image so it doesn’t look too cluttered.
Is it visually attractive, consistent with the event theme, does it capture attention, and generate interest?
Is the style aligned with the formality of the event and appropriate for the target audience?
Is it easy to share and view? Are the steps to follow or the “call to action” you are proposing clear?

After reviewing your invitation, it’s time for the “litmus test”: go ahead and share your invitation and see if people are interested in your activity or event.


⚠️⚠️ Remember: people not attending does not always mean your invitation is the failure. Check if the time you scheduled it, the day of the week, the weather, or other external factors influenced the lack of attendance.


What can you achieve with this solution?
Convene the people you would like from a visual aspect. They say that “everything is perceived through the eyes,” and in that, the form of an invitation is key.
The recommendations in this solution work for you, but you can also help others make theirs… or share the solution with those you consider.
Although you are not an expert now, with practice you surely will be! We hope it has been useful to you. Keep practicing; now you have more tools and inspiration to create increasingly memorable invitations!
See you soon! 👋🏽

If what you want is to spread what you do to others, this is the solution for you: How to mobilize others with your cause? →

en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.title: Does your community need financial support to connect to the internet?
en/solve/solv-financial-support-connect.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Although I didn’t write the original version of this solution, I am reviewing it today so you can understand it better. Sometimes we feel like we are alone, working against the tide. I would like you to know that it doesn’t have to be that way, and that there are people and organizations that can help you. I hope this solution shows you possible paths forward.
What is seeking financial support in your community to connect to the Internet?
There are initiatives that seek to connect people who do not have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for communities and local organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, such as community networks and complementary access solutions.
In addition, they provide information on how to obtain low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

What is it for?
Contacting some of them could lead you to obtain internet access for your community at affordable prices, with guarantees of maintenance, training, and sustainability that you might not imagine right now… dare to try!

What do you need?

A computer with a web browser and an Internet connection
A web translator like google translate, deepl, or an artificial intelligence to help you translate (you can type “AI to translate text” into a search engine)
Patience and time to dedicate to the search; it is better if you do it with others
A dose of courage to send your request to one of the initiatives… you have all our encouragement! That is how we did it.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Think of the best question you can ask the internet and dare to dive in to find… you can do a SOLE!

In the case of Colombia, it could be something like “what initiatives connect rural, remote, and low-income communities to the internet in Colombia?”, or “how to get subsidized internet in Colombia?”, or “what organizations connect communities to low-cost Internet in Colombia?” Be creative with your question to find varied answers!
You can also research the suggestions in search engines to dive deeper and find more related information.
Don’t hesitate to contact the companies and programs suggested by the search engine.


Step 2 → At SOLE Colombia, we know some low-cost connectivity initiatives around the world; take a look, we encourage you to get in touch with them!


Mintic - “Connecting the Unconnected” program by MINTIC and Colnodo

The “Connecting the Unconnected” program is an initiative of the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) of Colombia, which seeks to bring the Internet to rural areas and communities with little or no connectivity.
The Digital Centers are free Wi-Fi access points installed in strategic locations to facilitate internet access in these areas.
Steps to access, according to the program’s website:

Locate a Digital Center: Digital Centers are located in rural areas and communities with little connectivity. You can find information about their location on the MinTIC website.
Turn on your device’s Wi-Fi: Turn on the Wi-Fi on your phone, tablet, or other device you want to connect.
Search for the “MinTIC Conecta” network: Your device will show available Wi-Fi networks. Select the network named “Mintic Conecta”.
Fill in the requested data: You will be asked to enter some information to register. Fill in the required fields.
Accept the terms and conditions: Read the terms and conditions carefully and, if you agree, accept them to connect. Done! Once the previous steps are completed, you will be able to use the Internet connection.


Colnodo

In Colombia, access to the 900 MHz band for communities is being addressed through a public consultation led by the Ministry of Information and Communications Technologies (MinTIC) and the National Spectrum Agency (ANE).
The objective is to make the use of this band more flexible for community networks, especially in rural areas with little or no commercial network coverage.
Process and Participation:

Public Consultation: A public consultation has been opened so that organized communities, community networks, and other interested actors can express their interest and provide comments on the proposal.
Participation Form: An online form is available for communities to describe their situation, interests, and suggestions regarding the use of the band.
Information and Documentation: The ANE has published documents and guidelines for the consultation, which can be viewed and downloaded.
Deadline: The public consultation is open until July 1, 2025.

Focus on Rural Areas:

The 900 MHz band, with its capacity for good coverage and penetration, is considered ideal for supporting connectivity in rural and remote areas.
The goal is for community networks to be able to leverage this band to bring connectivity to places where there is no commercial coverage or it is limited.

Potential Benefits:

Community Connectivity: Facilitate internet access for rural communities through community networks.
Economic and Social Development: Boost access to services such as telemedicine, virtual education, and other opportunities thanks to connectivity.
Community Empowerment: Community networks can generate experience and autonomy in managing their own networks.
Future Readiness: Experience with this band can pave the way for the adoption of more advanced technologies and services in the future.

Active Participation:
It is crucial that interested communities actively participate in the public consultation, expressing their needs, expectations, and proposals for the use of the 900 MHz band. The participation of all interested sectors is fundamental to building a strategy that guarantees fair and sustainable connectivity for everyone.
In summary, the 900 MHz band represents an opportunity for Colombian communities to access the internet and improve their connectivity, especially in rural areas, through community networks.
The public consultation is the space for communities to express their needs and contribute to the construction of a public policy that recognizes the importance of the spectrum for social and economic development.

Internet Society

Offers funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Supports the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.

NUPEF

NUPEF.org, through its focus on community networks and affordable internet access, can facilitate access to funding and resources to build or strengthen community internet networks, in addition to offering training to manage and maintain these networks.
It also promotes the creation of safe and inclusive virtual communities, empowering marginalized groups to use technology and advocate for their digital rights:


It can help you apply for grants and funding for community network projects, including building new access solutions or expanding existing ones, especially for marginalized and underserved populations.


Offers training and resources so that community members develop skills in building, managing, and maintaining community networks.


If you already have a network, NUPEF can help strengthen it by improving infrastructure, updating technology, and providing technical support to ensure its continuous operation.


Promotes the creation of safe and welcoming online communities, where diversity is valued and users are protected from violence and abuse.


Works so that excluded people can use and adapt the internet and digital technology for their needs, including the development of fair and equitable solutions for universal access.


Seeks economic models that allow for affordable and sustainable internet access, generating value in the community and promoting self-sufficiency.


Facilitates the exchange of knowledge and experiences between different communities and movements, promoting collective action for digital inclusion.


APC


It is a network of civil society organizations that helps people access the internet where there is no connectivity or it is not affordable.
It also supports local and grassroots groups so they can use technology to develop their communities and advance the defense and exercise of their rights.
It promotes government ICT policies that serve the interests of the population, especially in the context of the Global South.

Unconnected

It is an initiative that seeks to connect people who do not have internet access, especially in rural, remote, and low-income areas.
They offer funding programs and resources for communities and local organizations that are working on building and expanding internet infrastructure, such as community networks and complementary access solutions.
In addition, they provide information on how to obtain low-cost internet through government programs and non-profit organizations.

High Speed Internet

If you know of any other way to get support to connect your community to low-cost Internet, don’t forget to comment on this Solution so we can incorporate it. We also ask that, if you see this solution is outdated or contains erroneous information, you let us know so we can continue researching and bringing this information to the ends of the earth.

How to know if this solution works?
How having low-cost internet can help:

Infrastructure funding: there are organizations that offer funding to organizations that build and expand internet networks in underserved areas, which can result in more affordable options for residents.
Information on subsidy programs: other organizations provide information on government and non-government programs that offer subsidies or reduced rates for internet access for low-income individuals.
Community networks: others support the creation of community networks, which are often a more economical alternative to commercial options.
Resources to build networks: some others offer a toolkit for building and maintaining community networks, which can help reduce infrastructure costs.
Training for the installation and maintenance of equipment and networks.
Strengthening the social fabric and bonds between the community and the community of practice: initiatives usually include content and practice in digital rights, equity, community ties, and human connection, which make the internet an excuse to have more conscious and connected communities.


What can you achieve with this solution?
The continuous search for Internet Solutions has led us at SOLE Colombia to research and be curious enough to find the “Parceros” (partners) who have helped us bring the internet to very remote places.
In that same way, you, yes you, having access to this information, can be encouraged to explore relationships with people and organizations that can guarantee the right that you and your community have to access the internet wherever you are.
When people come together to achieve things, the sky is the limit.

en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.title: ¿Cómo conseguir espacios con la ayuda de aliados?
en/solve/solv-find-allied-spaces.content:
Hello! I’m Catalina, welcome 👋🏽
This solution was written by Nicolás and Belén. Then, an artificial intelligence (AI) assistant helped me organize it according to the sections we always use as a guide, and finally, here I am adding the experience and warmth that characterizes Voltaje ⚡⚡ solutions.
Sometimes it is relatively easy to find meeting spaces in our community. Other times it is not, either because they don’t know us or because it is simply not easy to access the people who manage them. In this solution, we have gathered some recommendations for managing spaces through allies, that is, other organizations or people who have closer access to the space you need.

Remember that you don’t always have to solve things alone. In the end, managing these spaces, like many other things, is fundamentally about weaving trust; about creating bonds. So, let’s get started!

What is finding spaces with the help of allies?
It is the process of identifying, talking to, and reaching agreements with organizations that “custody” places (NGOs, foundations, libraries), so that they lend them to you and thus transform them into environments where the community can meet and learn using the Internet in a group.
Finding spaces with allies is not just a matter of paperwork (although it usually involves some of that) or the place itself. It is more about the way you infect someone with what you do, how you make them feel that it is worth lending you their space or helping you manage one because they believe in your mission.
Here I will talk mainly about physical space, but you can also go to another solution where we tell you how to mobilize others with your cause..

What is it for?
A space where you can connect to the Internet is an opportunity to transform it into a place of exchange with the community; one where you can support each other and open the doors to the world. Since it is not always easy to find one on your own, the recommendations you find here can be helpful so you don’t have to walk this process alone.
But besides getting a space, weaving bonds with others is something that will allow you to collaborate in different ways in the future, not only to manage spaces or anything else, but to continue building a more equitable and beautiful world one Big question at a time.
Imagine that your ally is also encouraged to create their own learning sessions using the Internet in a group after seeing you and your community!

What do you need?

A good purpose that explains why you want the space.
Patience, because bonds of trust are cooked over low heat.
Courage to launch yourself into conversations with others who are not waiting for you.


How to do it?

Recommendation #1 → Recognize the actors in the territory

There are multiple public and private institutions that work in the territories where we live: governments, NGOs, cooperatives, foundations, among others.
Before knocking on a door, observe who is already there. Talk to your neighbors about past social projects. Ask at the school or the mayor’s office which organizations have a presence in the area.
Write it all down. It can be in a notebook or on a bulletin board with colored sticky notes to differentiate one actor from another. The key is to make your directory as rich as possible.

⚠️💬 Keep in mind that in your search it is also important to know what stories have already been told or what other organizations or collectives have already participated in the spaces you identify. It is always striking to mention how your proposal can add to what others are already building.



Recommendation #2 → Contact them from the purpose

Once you recognize who you would like to approach, it’s time to do it!
As much as possible, always try to make contact in person. In-person meetings tend to be more effective than emails or letters. Once you manage to contact the person from this institution or organization, tell them about your projects and the difficulties you encounter in having adequate spaces to gather your community.
When your search has a brave and powerful purpose, it is easier to get what you need. If your intention is to do a SOLE, then you can tell how any place can become a Self-Organized Learning Environment and how this allows people to discover ways to learn when there are no teachers around.

Remember that when your search is born from a genuine need of the community, doors usually open more easily.



Recommendation #3 → Cultivate autonomy and trust

Once you have spoken with several actors and have identified which one you have the most affinity with and want to work with, see if you can speak on behalf of their institution or organization to manage the spaces that work for you, since the person will not be able to accompany you every time you need to make a loan. Of course, give this time; first allow a bond of trust to be generated with that person, showing them how your collective, organization, or community is autonomous and responsible.
Once you get their company and/or their authorization, start the formal request for the spaces you have identified as most convenient for your community’s activities.
If you have to write a letter to request the space and don’t know how, go to the solution How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet in a group? or How to write an invitation that summons?, you will surely find help 💪🏽

Other possible internets
The moment you manage to manage a space thanks to the company or support of another person, you will have achieved part of the initial goal!
Then comes the second part: when the space(s) stop feeling foreign and start to be recognized by the community as places of meeting and learning, you will have reached the full potential of this solution!

Other possible Internets
Managing spaces through others not only promotes the creation of networks and collaborative work.
You will create a bridge between institutions and the community, ensuring that resources that were previously closed become common goods for everyone’s learning.

en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.title: What free networks are available for me to connect to the internet?
en/solve/solv-find-wifi-app.content:
Hello! I’m Belén and I welcome you. I didn’t write this solution, but I’m going to walk you through it, and I would love it if, at the end, you could tell me if you liked it, if it was useful, and if you can apply it in your context.
What is searching for WiFi signals around you with a mobile application?
Searching for WiFi signals → with a mobile application involves using software on your smartphone to scan, analyze, and find available wireless networks in the place where you are. Many times, you might think you don’t have Internet → or that your mobile signal is weak (depending on the service provided by your operator in the place where you are), but if you look closely, there might be a WiFi network with a better connection or even one that is free.

What is it for?
Sometimes, the place where we are might not have access to Internet, but if we move and go to a nearby place, we might find WiFi networks. Sometimes, even if we find them, we won’t be able to access them because we don’t know their respective passwords.
The application WiFi Map shows us a map with WiFi networks within a 2-kilometer radius, according to your device’s location, and shares their access password with us. The networks saved in this application can be public or private.
If you want to make the most of a nearby connection, you can connect to those networks to use them in a group using SOLE. You only need a few devices, four or five people eager to learn for each device, and Big Questions to solve. Do you want to know more about how to do SOLE? See how to do it here: How to do SOLE? - Tutorial

What do you need?

Smartphone →
Available space on your cell phone
Mobile data connection
Generosity


How to do it?

Step 1 → Install the app


Before starting the installation process, it is necessary that you have a stable Internet connection.
Once you have found it, you can open the “Google Play” application for Android or Apple Store for iOS and search for the WiFi Map application.
Another alternative is to enter one of these links through a web browser: Google Play and Apple Store




Step 2 → Configure the app

Once the application is installed, open it and accept the terms of use. Among them, it is very important that you accept access to your location while the application is in use.

Open the application and swipe the top of your phone down to access the control panel. Turn on location, in case the application hasn’t already done so.


Step 3 → Use the app

When it shows you a map of the world, press the “arrowhead” shaped icon, and this will make the map locate your respective region.
At the bottom of the screen, the closest WiFi networks for which we have the access password will appear.





Step 4 → Select a network


When you can see the list of WiFi networks near you, you can select one and see its access data.
Sometimes the application will ask you to watch a video before allowing you to see the network passwords. This is how the app uses advertising to fund itself in its free version.
Sometimes the application will ask you to watch a video before allowing you to see the network passwords. This is how the app uses advertising to fund itself in its free version.





How to know if this solution works?
With this recipe, you can access multiple WiFi networks, both public and private. In cities or urban areas, you will have many more possibilities of finding networks with their access data available, compared to smaller populated centers.
Now, with a WiFi network, you will have more stability and speed to connect to the Internet, and why not, to look for answers to your Big Questions, to learn, take courses, or share the resource with others.
Are you ready to start?

What can you achieve with this solution?
This solution will allow you to have temporary access to the Internet, mainly from populated centers where users like you have shared access data to some public or private Internet network.
To be able to access these passwords, you must have internet access, since only the paid application allows you to download the map with the access information.

en/solve/solv-fish-game.title: How to use gaming to learn community equipment care?
en/solve/solv-fish-game.content:
A governance solution for common resources
Solution Video
You can watch this video while you develop this solution.

Hello, my name is Mateo and I will accompany you through this solution. If you are here, it is because you are interested in knowing how to care for and use technological equipment that belongs to your community or work team. In this case, when we talk about technological equipment, we refer to a computer, an antenna, a tablet, a data plan, etc., and to a material good that does not belong to anyone in particular, but to a community or group of people.

💡 Inspiration! At SOLE Colombia we want more people to use the internet and technological equipment as a group, as it brings many benefits:

Using it together is more fun and invites us to share ideas.
It is more economical and invites us to work as a team.
When there is another person by your side, you are less likely to fall into malicious websites or cyber scams.


What is using games to learn how to care for equipment as a community?
We develop teamwork skills, learn to value collective responsibility, and understand the importance of cooperating for the common good in a supportive environment. An excellent strategy to do this is through games and participatory activities.
What is this solution for?
To begin with, you will be surprised if I tell you that we do not want to give you magic formulas on how to care for and use technological equipment in a community, because we do not know the particularities of where you live and we understand that each context is different. However, we do have a fun and profound game that will allow you to reach agreements with your community or work team called the Fish Game. With this game, we hope your community reflects on the care, distribution, and management of common resources on planet Earth, while discussing how to reach agreements for the shared use of the equipment they have at their disposal.
What do you need?

You must have a bag of at least 80 candies, beans, or tokens of the same size with which you will represent the fish in the game.
A table.
Chairs surrounding the table.
Large poster board (pliego size).
Markers.

How to do it?


Moment 1: first game


💡 For the first game, place 50 of the 80 fish in the center of a table and tell the participants: “There are 50 fish in a lake and you are fishermen/women. To fish, you must follow these instructions:
a. Each person can fish between 0 and 5 fish per round.
b. You cannot speak; you can only use your body language.
c. The fish reproduce: 1 new fish is born for every 10 fish that remain available on the table after the round ends. Example: if there are 30 fish left on the table, you must add three new fish.
d. You decide when the game ends.”
After giving the instructions, leave the bag with the 30 extra fish on the table and verify that each person has their moment to decide how many fish they are going to take.
At the end of the round, ask the players to return the fish and ask the group:

How did you feel about the distribution of the fish? Does it seem fair to you?






Moment 2: second game


💡 For the second game, the conditions change, so explain the following instructions out loud: “Now there are 50 fish in a lake and you are still fishermen/women, the difference is that you are in a drought season, so fishing is much more difficult. There is a lot of scarcity and you must guarantee food to feed your families in the coming weeks.”
The rules of the game are the same. Remind the participants of the rules if necessary.
At the end of the round, ask them:


What changed now? How do you feel about the distribution?


Do you think there could be similar difficulties when sharing the technological equipment of your community?


Moment 3: third game


💡 For the third game, the situation is the same as the second game but the instructions change: “there are 50 fish in a lake and you are still fishermen/women, the difference is that you are in a drought season, so fishing is much more difficult. There is a lot of scarcity and you must guarantee food to feed your families in the coming weeks. There is not much time, so you must make quick decisions.”
a. Each person can fish between 0 and 5 fish per round.
b. You can talk for 2 minutes before fishing to decide the best way to do it.
c. The fish reproduce: 1 new fish is born for every 10 fish that remain available after the round ends. Example: if there are 30 fish left on the table, you must add three new fish.
d. You decide when the game ends.”
At the end of the round, ask the participants:


Did the agreement you reached at the beginning of the game change anything?


Which of the games do you think had a fairer distribution? What are the differences between the three games?


How could the agreement you have made be applied to the use and care of the technological equipment you have at your disposal?


Moment 4: the secret to reaching agreements


💡 Tell people the secrets of the game for reaching agreements:

The fishermen represent each of the people in your community.
The fish represent the finite resources or technological equipment that are available to the community, for example, computers, internet antennas, data plans, etc. These fish also apply as an analogy for the management of finite resources such as land, water, food, or the air we breathe.

The key to this game is that the more fish we take for ourselves, the fewer fish will reproduce; so we all lose.
Likewise, the fewer fish we take, the more fish will reproduce on the table and the community will have more resources.



Moment 5: let’s reach an agreement

Give the participants the poster board and markers. Invite them to write down agreements on how to manage the resources or technological equipment they have at their disposal. We recommend downloading the following template to guide you in the conversation.
Reglas uso y cuidado compartido de equipo tecnológicos.pptx
These questions are only a guide, so you can add or remove the questions you see fit. Ask the participants to put the agreements they reached in writing and invite them to share them with the rest of the community. This is fundamental because, in moments of conflict or difficulties in solving a problem, they can return to what was written to reach solutions or to rethink new agreements.
How does the game work?
First game: in the first game, people tend to consume fish based on their interests and the behaviors of other people. If one person consumes many fish (5), the others tend to be driven to consume the same amount; the same applies in reverse, if one person consumes few fish, the others (with some exceptions) tend to be motivated to consume less. Now, there are no magic formulas nor is the future written about what might happen; the key is to observe people’s behaviors, as this will allow you to make powerful reflections on the responsible and community management of finite resources.
Second game: due to the conditioning of the drought and the urgency of feeding the family, in the second game people tend to consume more than in the first and third, which causes the distribution of the fish to be more inequitable and run out faster. In other words, more tension is generated between personal benefit and common benefit. In behavioral psychology, this situation is called present bias: human beings, upon feeling that a resource is about to run out, activate a sense of loss that drives us to consume irrationally even when we do not need it.
Third game: by this point, participants usually reach agreements by consuming fewer fish so that more reproduce, preventing situations of scarcity and finding community alternatives for the equitable and fair management of resources; however, it is possible that this does not happen, the important thing is that you tell them the value of reaching agreements in the management of finite resources or technological equipment. When we reach agreements, we can all benefit; conversely, when we all seek our personal benefits, the resources from which we can benefit tend to be destroyed, as well as our opportunity to continue benefiting from them.
How much is enough? The tragedy of the commons
The tragedy of the commons is a problem regarding social relations and human behavior described by Garret Hardin in 1968 for the journal Science, in which he proposes a thought experiment imagining a farmer who decides, on land shared with other farmers, to start putting more cows, since it generates more profits and personal benefits. The other farmers decide to do the same, so the field fills up with cows, the land is overexploited and deteriorates rapidly. Likewise, the farmers are left with many cows and no land to produce. This dilemma shows how we can destroy shared finite resources if each of us seeks only personal benefit and invites us to think about the importance of reaching agreements on shared resources.
Reaching agreements really works!
We want to share with you the story of Alexander, a leader from the community of the village in Agrado, located in the Department of Cauca. Alexander, together with his community, managed to reach an agreement on how to use the internet through an agreement they made with the store located next to the community hall. Let’s listen to his story:

en/solve/solv-full-server.title: How to create your own Pocket Server (Full Server)?
en/solve/solv-full-server.content:
Hello! I’m David. This solution is the natural evolution of the Pocket Internet → or giving a second life to an old computer →. Here, we are going to transform that equipment into a robust server capable of managing files and more complex applications.

What is it for?
By setting up a “Full” server →, you give your community a digital meeting point where they can easily upload and download files, as if it were a local cloud, but without the need for the internet. It is a toolkit that can be passed from hand to hand via a USB connection →.

An analogy to understand it (Possibility)
If it helps you visualize it, you can think of this server as a Community Kitchen:

The RAM memory → is the work counter where you prepare the information.
The Storage → is the pantry where you keep the ingredients (files) forever.
This server is the space where everyone can come to look for “recipes” (information) or leave their own ingredients.


What do you need?

A computer with Linux → or a Raspberry Pi →.
Internet connection (only for the initial installation).
A USB drive →.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Connect via Terminal

Access your equipment through a Terminal → using SSH →.


Step 2 → Create the public directory

We are going to define the folder where all the shared information will live:
mkdir www
chmod 777 www


Step 3 → Install support for applications (PHP)

We will install the necessary packages so that the server can execute dynamic web applications:
sudo apt install php-fpm php-mbstring php-mysql php-curl php-gd php-zip php-xml -y


Step 4 → Configure the web server

You must adjust the Nginx → configuration so that it recognizes the new folder and the PHP language. This is done in the /etc/nginx/sites-available/default file.


Step 5 → Install the File Manager (Tiny File Manager)

So that anyone can upload files from their browser without using code, we will install this tool:
cd www
wget raw.githubusercontent.com/prasathmani/tinyfilemanager.php


Future possibilities (Under construction)
This solution opens doors to larger projects that we are documenting:

Hand-to-Hand Replica: How to copy this entire system onto a USB drive so that another community can use it just as easily.
Local AI and Agents: The possibility of having an intelligent assistant that summarizes texts or helps with tasks, running directly from your server’s RAM memory → without internet.
Processes with AI: Optimize how information is organized using small local artificial brains.


How to know if it works?
Visit solevoltaje.local/tinyfilemanager.php. If you can see the file manager, your server is ready for action!

Recommended solutions

Second life to an old computer →
