en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.title: How to collect financial resources as a community?
en/solve/solv-funding-community-internet.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay and one of my great ventures is giving communal use to the resources we have available. I like to tinker, yes, but I am also interested in the ways in which we humans coordinate ourselves to live better together.
What is a fundraiser to pay for community internet?
This solution gathers ideas on how to collect money to pay for a community connection, that is, getting a community to agree to financially support a good that will be used and enjoyed in common.

What is it for?
Finding ways to organize ourselves to acquire the things that improve our living conditions is sometimes a complex task.
If you are clear that you need the Internet, but you don’t know how to get the people in your community to follow your idea, support you in the maintenance and sustainability of the contract, or you don’t know what steps to follow to be able to do it together, you can find useful guidance in this solution.

What do you need?

A very clear idea of why you want to collect the money.
Charisma, eloquence, and people skills to convince people to participate in the fundraiser.
Order to keep the accounts, manage the money, and inform the people who collaborate with you about the progress of the fundraiser and the status of the accounts.
Communication skills to inform collaborators about the status of the service, maintenance needs, or incidents. Also to receive suggestions or handle the procedures required for the formalization or maintenance of the service.


How to do it?
These recommendations are relevant when raising money for community purposes. They are not necessarily followed in order, nor are they the only ones, but we believe they can help you.

Step 1 → Moment 1: Let’s build a team, it’s easier with several people

Look for partners to start this campaign.
When we undertake projects for a common good, it is easy to get allies to distribute responsibilities. When you do these types of initiatives alone, you can quickly get tired and give up, but with others, this project will be more bearable.
Define who will be in charge of what, that will make the work more organized and you will be able to follow up more easily.


Step 2 → Let’s give the fundraiser a purpose, one that is clear and excites us

It is important to have the time to reflect and project ourselves on what we want to do. What is it that we want to achieve? Remember, money is only a means to reach something bigger and more important… that is called purpose.
In this case, what is it that unites us in this fundraiser, that inspires us to move to get the funds? When you are establishing the purpose of any project, it is time to ask ourselves tirelessly what for, until we are convinced.
Doing SOLE is a great way to find a purpose for the fundraiser; in addition to paying for it together, you can learn, dialogue, and create flourishing communities by using the internet as a group. Paying for the internet together allows you to use it for SOLE, or for anything you can think of!
For example:

What do we want internet in a public access place for? So that people in my community can learn new things they need or want to learn, converse and dialogue with other people and communities in a Great Conversation, and take action in a self-organized way to live better together.
What do we want people in our community to be able to learn together for? So that it is not necessary to depend exclusively on learning spaces and people related to the educational system, to realize that anyone can learn anything using the internet. Why in a group? Because going anywhere alone is a difficult path; instead, when we do it together, it is done better.
What do we want them to be able to converse via the internet for? Interacting with other people with the goal of learning or so that others can be part of our lives always makes us feel better. Learning together when there are other people who participate in our findings and with whom we can walk the path together makes us feel that what we learn transcends and is bigger than us. If we connect with each other through the internet, it is because we are mutually interested and can accompany each other; we are not alone on the path… Do you want to connect with people around the world in your SOLE sessions? Take a look at The Granny Cloud SOLE! They are volunteers from all over the world who connect to SOLE sessions to accompany, offer warm encouragement, share, learn, and have fun together.
What do we want to help our community flourish for? So that we all have a happier, fuller, and tastier life!

Does it make sense to have public access internet in our community? Of course!


Step 3 → Let’s identify those potentially interested in participating

Which of our neighbors would be interested in having community internet? What interest could they have in contributing monetarily to this project? This way we can translate our project into their possible interests.
Here are some examples of SOLEros who have self-organized to learn together using the internet:

Elainer, when she used SOLE so that the young people in her community could learn to make video games.
Robinson, who used SOLE so that his community could find sustainable alternatives to the traditional crops of his community.
María, when, through SOLE, she got her students to take responsibility for their own educational process and changed the way of researching and learning at her school.




Step 4 → A story, the best way to communicate an idea

Now that we know who we are going to direct our campaign to, let’s create a story. We recommend answering five fundamental questions: who, what, when, where, and why.
Here is ours:
In the community of La Piche, delicious honey is produced. Everyone in the community works in trades related to the production of its delicious honey: some have hives, others collect the honey, others market it, some manufacture related products…
We are a group of young people interested in creating natural cosmetic products based on honey and beeswax, but we don’t know how to start manufacturing those products, nor the instruments we need, nor the permits we require, or how we could market them, etc. We want to start with: how can we manufacture a honey and beeswax lipstick?
Using the Internet, we could find answers to these and other Great Questions!
The cheapest Internet plan is 120,000 COP; no one in the village could pay for it. But we have thought that, by collecting money among 12 people or families, we could pay a monthly fee of 10,000 COP and put the fiber optic broadband internet in a place that is easily accessible to everyone, such as the nursing home, the community hall, or Doña Adela’s store, which is the business that is open most of the time and where we could all connect. We could all use the connection, even the children in the village, to do their homework.
So, if you are interested and can be part of this fundraiser, join this list! Soon we will be able to have internet for ourselves!
I will send all expenses and payment receipts on the first of each month to a WhatsApp → group, and through there we can be aware of any news.
Are you joining the cause?


Step 5 → Purchase, communicate, and organize expenses

With the money collected, you just have to make the purchase.
Remember that none of these contracts have permanent clauses, so if you are not satisfied with the service, you can cancel it and switch to another operator.
It is important to be organized with the accounts and communicate payments and any news or issues in a timely manner to everyone involved.
This way, everyone can take co-responsibility for any decision related to this fundraiser and can assume the responsibilities or consequences together.
Make sure to create a communication flow with your collaborators, so you can communicate in both directions and agilely solve the problems that may arise.

Other possible internets
With this solution, it is possible to organize neighbors towards a common good, embodied in the payment of a service, to take advantage of it collectively and make the most of it.
It also manages to improve the connectivity conditions of the place where we live, making it a place where life is better.

Why could this solution work?
Organizing ourselves to achieve things will take us as far as we want.
In this case, it allows us to have a shared internet public access point. It is important to measure the bandwidth → offered by the service to be contracted very well. This way, we will be able to contract a service that is fast and powerful enough in relation to the number of people we want to link to that connection.
The next step would be how to improve the conditions of this connectivity without a significant increase in costs.

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.title: How to improve my mobile signal with a can?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-can.content:
Hello! It is a pleasure to greet you. My name is Mateo, and I will accompany you in the development of this solution. If you are reading, listening to, or watching this, it is because you are interested or curious about how to improve your cell phone signal in a very simple way. If so, you are in the right place.

What is this solution for?
This solution allows you to improve your cell phone signal provisionally. That is to say, it helps to improve it, but keep in mind that the quality of the signal also depends on other external factors such as the weather, the conditions of the place where you are, your operator, and the number of towers emitting radio waves around you to allow calls or internet browsing.
This solution that I am sharing with you is a simple, fast, and very interesting option. You will see that the results of this test are exciting and revealing.

What do you need?


One person to work on this solution is enough. Although everything is easier to solve in company. Go for it!
A clean metal can, it can be from a drink.
Scissors.
Utility knife (optional).
A ruler, preferably metal.
A fine-tip marker.
Thick transparent tape.
Safety gloves.


Before starting, some safety issues
Although this solution has a basic level of difficulty, it is important that you take into account some recommendations for your safety:

Work on a flat and rigid surface, preferably on a table where you can cut.
Find a clean can that is not rusty.
We recommend being in a quiet place, without distractions, and having as much time and patience as possible.
Keep your hands at a safe distance from the cuts you will make with the scissors or the utility knife.
Preferably, wear safety gloves.
We recommend being seated in a comfortable place to work.


How to do it?
This solution has 3 steps through which I will accompany you. Keep in mind that some of them can be frustrating and others very exciting, and both things are fine; they are part of “tinkering” (cacharrear). The important thing is to keep trying. Let’s start!

Step 1 → Draw the base metal sheet

To start, prepare all the mentioned materials.
Then, cut the base and the top of the can with the scissors or the utility knife, so that an open sheet remains; imagine it were a rectangular sheet of paper. You can do this using scissors or a utility knife. Place the drink can on a flat and rigid surface, preferably on a table.

⚠️⚠️ Do this with patience and care, placing your hand at a safe distance from the cut you are going to make. Remember that the can also cuts.


When you have the rectangular sheet cut out, flatten it until you eliminate as many irregularities as possible on the surface. Imagine that it should look like a smooth sheet of paper. This will be the metal sheet we will work with from now on.
With the ruler and the fine-tip marker, draw a 4cm x 4cm square on the metal sheet.

⚠️⚠️ Be careful when making all cuts. If you have them, I recommend using safety gloves.




Step 2 → Turn the can into an antenna

Cut the 4 cm x 4 cm square you drew with the scissors until you get a square metal sheet.

Now, choose one of the edges of this square sheet and mark the center with a fine-tip marker, that is, 2 centimeters from the edge.
Place the ruler on the center you previously marked and with the marker make two marks 0.5 cm on each side of the center. Repeat this same step on the opposite edge of the side you are working on. Join the marks and draw the lines so that you have a 1 cm rectangle.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  


💬❓ How are you doing so far? If your can looks like the last image 👆🏽, we are on the right track. If not, you can try again following the same steps. There is no rush, I’ll wait for you here!

Continue drawing marks every 0.5 cm on each of the two you already drew. In the end, you should have 7 marks on each of the lines as seen in this image:

Draw lines from side to side for each of the marks you made in the previous step. Then, cut along the 7 lines that remained, without cutting the central column that is 1cm wide.

If your can looks like this 👆🏽, you can proceed to fold one tab, skip one: the second, the fourth, the sixth, and the eighth. Then, you must trim each of the tabs that remained folded.
Finally, cover your metal piece on both sides with thick transparent tape; this will allow you to protect it so it lasts.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

We are done! Now, the simple part: using your can to improve the mobile signal.

Step 3 → Install your antenna on the cell phone
The main antenna of cell phones is usually on the back of your phone, on the upper right side.
Use transparent tape to stick this metal piece in the mentioned place and protect it, preferably, with the cell phone case you are using.

🎉💪🏽 We are done! Now you are ready to enjoy a better signal. Congratulations on finishing this solution; I hope this journey has been challenging and exciting.
Like this one, in Voltaje you can find many more solutions to be able to connect without fear of using the internet in a group. Dare to keep browsing! See more solutions →

Other possible internets

The easiest way is to check if the signal bars or dots on your cell phone (located in the upper left or right corner of your screen) change with and without the can. These bars measure how strong the signal you are receiving is. In theory, the more bars you have, the better the signal you should be receiving.
Another option is to measure the download speed on your cell phone. Consult the solution How to test your Internet connection speed? →.
This solution can achieve a significant improvement in your cell phone’s signal reception by one or at most two bars or dots. Keep in mind that the signal cannot improve in places where there has never been a signal.


What can you achieve with this solution?
Keep in mind that there are two types of signal: that of your cell phone → with which you can make calls and send text messages, and the WiFi → signal with which you can connect to the internet.
With this solution, you can improve both signals because it amplifies the reception and transmission of waves from the antenna built into your cell phone. It is a little “help” for that antenna. You can test this solution in different conditions and draw your own conclusions about whether it is working for you or not.
But also, amplifying your cell phone signal can help you share internet with other people → who need it. Group internet is safer and can help other people in their work, studies, or to enjoy various entertainment activities.
We invite you to be part of a new way of using the internet together! 💪🏽 Amplify your signal, enjoy, and share your internet.
Thank you for reaching the end of this solution. We hope it has been useful to you! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could use it.
See you soon! 👋🏽

Related solutions

In this solution, you will find some additional tricks to improve your mobile signal: How to amplify your mobile signal within a space? →
If what you want is to improve the signal of your WiFi modem, you can consult this solution: How to improve your router’s signal? →

en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.title: How to improve your modem signal?
en/solve/solv-improve-signal-router.content:
Hi! I’m Manu, the storyteller for SOLE Colombia, and I have also felt very frustrated by losing my Internet signal right in the middle of an important meeting or a SOLE session.
What is improving your router’s signal?
Just when you need it most, the connection disappears—has that happened to you? It has to me, more than once. But don’t worry, because you are about to learn how to improve your Router signal so that it happens less frequently.
Additionally, I will teach you how to optimize the Router → configuration so that you can browse faster by changing the DNS → servers → and adjusting the WiFi → channel.
This isn’t difficult and you can do it from home! So get ready, because we are going to get the most out of your network.

What is it for?
I am going to guide you so you can get the most out of your Router. Together, we will improve the distribution of the WiFi signal in your space, achieving a more stable connection so that it doesn’t fail you in those moments when you need it most, whether it’s for a meeting, a class, or a SOLE session. No more interrupted signals when you are investigating a Big Question!
Remember that these adjustments will not increase your contracted speed, but they will help the signal reach every corner of your house better by optimizing the DNS.

What do you need?

Use an Internet service that connects through a Router.
The Router’s access credentials.
A computer connected to the network.
A little patience (I hope not too much!).
A tinkerer’s attitude.


How to do it?
Now, I am going to guide you step by step so you can improve your WiFi signal. Trust me! Something is bound to change!

Step 1 → Measure your connection speed

The first thing you have to do is measure the speed of your current connection. In this solution, we tell you how to do it: How to know your Internet connection speed? →
Knowing your speed will allow you to compare the “before” and “after” of making the adjustments.


Step 2 → Explore your space and locate the Router

It may seem obvious, but we often forget the simplest thing: get closer to the Router. If you are organizing a SOLE session or have several devices connected, make sure they are as close as possible so that the signal reaches them with more strength.
The place where you put the Router is key. Make sure to place it in an elevated spot, such as on a table or even on the ceiling. Ideally, it should be in a central location, not in a corner or near a window, where installers often leave it. Moving the Router to a more strategic place will make the signal spread more evenly throughout the house.

Photo taken from Pexels, (2024).

Photo taken by Manuela Córdoba, (2024).

Step 3 → Place the Router antennas in a perpendicular position

Have you seen your router’s antennas? Check them right now. An important detail to improve the signal is to make sure they are in a perpendicular position, that is, pointing toward the ceiling. This helps the signal waves distribute better.


Make that adjustment and you will notice the difference. Well done!
With these 3 actions, you should already see some kind of improvement. If you want to go further, expand the last, more advanced steps.


Step 4 → Configure the DNS

What is that thing?
DNS are like an address book that helps your computer find websites faster. By using faster DNS servers, such as those from Google or Cloudflare, you ensure that pages load with greater speed. The default servers from your Internet provider are not always the most optimal, so switching to more efficient ones can improve your browsing experience.
Now we are going to do something interesting: configure the DNS. This will help the web pages you visit load faster, since DNS are the IP address directories that the Router consults when browsing.
If you want to switch to faster and more reliable DNS servers, you will make your Internet queries more agile. To achieve this, follow these steps:

Access your Router’s administration interface. To do this, in your computer’s network settings, look for the gateway. There you will find an IP address →, something like 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1.
Log in with the credentials, which are usually admin/admin, or check your device’s manual for the default passwords.
Change the values to 1.1.1.1, 1.0.0.1 (from Cloudflare) and 8.8.8.8 (from Google).
Open your browser and enter that address in the address bar. This will take you to the Router’s control panel.
Look for the Network Settings section and, there, the DNS Servers option.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

Very good! Now your network will use these DNS servers, which are faster and more reliable.


Step 5 → Configure the WiFi channel

Another key adjustment is the WiFi channel configuration. Channels determine the frequency at which the Router emits the signal. To avoid interference with other nearby networks, configure your Router on the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11. To do this:

Enter your Router’s configuration interface again.
Look for the Wireless section.
Choose one of the recommended channels: 1, 6, or 11.
Save the changes and restart the Router.

With this adjustment, you will reduce interference and improve signal quality. Very good, we’re almost done!

Other possible internets
Did you manage it? I’m sure you did! By following these steps, I am sure that the Router signal will have improved and, therefore, the WiFi distribution in your space.

Why could this Solution work?
Although you won’t be able to increase the speed beyond what you have contracted :c, you will have ensured that every corner of your house receives a stronger and more stable signal.
I hope these tips are useful to you and that you no longer have any Internet cuts in the middle of an important meeting or an exciting investigation in SOLE.

en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.title: How to install my 3G/4G antenna?
en/solve/solv-install-3G-antenna.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and although I’m not an expert on connectivity, I’ve learned by tinkering: that is, through trial and error and by asking others about the subject. Today, I’ll join you in installing your own antenna!
It is important to know that there are many types of 3G or 4G antennas, although, in general, this solution should work for you to install whichever one you have. It is possible that your antenna comes with a manual or instructions. We recommend reading it first. But, if you don’t have one, or if the person who sold you the antenna didn’t explain how to do it, what follows might help!

What is installing a 3G/4G antenna?
In short, it is placing and putting into operation equipment that allows for improved access to cellular signal in an area where it was previously weak. Keep in mind that for this solution, you need to have the antenna. If you don’t have one yet, you can go to the solution How to buy a 3G-4G antenna? → to find out which one works best for you.

Remember, the instructions and what you find here may look a bit different.


What is it for?
There are places where cellular phone signal is very weak. You can see this in the connection bars on your cell phone (you might see only one bar or something that says H+, E or, even, no signal). An antenna that has the necessary characteristics for the conditions of the place from which you want to connect can help you achieve better connection quality.
I recently understood that the Internet signal that reaches cell phones travels through invisible electromagnetic waves, and that cell phones have a small antenna inside that captures those waves, allowing us to have access to the internet.
What the antenna does is capture and amplify the specific cellular data signal (3G or 4G); that is, the signal travels in electromagnetic waves through the air from a place higher than where you are—above trees, buildings, or hills—and then comes down through a cable to your height. When it is at your height, the signal can be shared through the air using a WiFi network, or by cable using a modem or router.
I know these terms may seem confusing, but as you go through the installation steps, you will have a clearer understanding of them.

Before you start, some safety issues
Remember that you are working with electrical equipment. Be careful when connecting to the electrical current. Be aware of weather conditions, especially the risk of storms: the antenna, at the moment of installation, would act as a lightning rod. A lightning strike on the antenna could cause serious personal and material damage.

What do you need?


The 3G-4G antenna → you purchased.
Coaxial cable → to bring the signal from the antenna.
Modem → with its respective power cable, Ethernet cable, and quick start guide (or instruction manual).
SIM card → from the cellular operator that has the best signal in the area.
Computer with Ethernet connection → and/or WiFi → or smartphone → (Android / IOS).
A tall pole (of the same length as the cable or slightly less): it can be a metal pipe, wood, or bamboo. The important thing is that it is as straight as possible and sturdy.
Antenna mounts (which allow the antenna to be hung on the tall pole).
Wrench for tightening nuts.
Materials and tools to fix the pole (depends on where you install it).


How is it done?
This solution has 6 steps, some simpler than others, but don’t worry, if I could do it, you can too. Let’s start!

Step 1 → Define the place where the antenna and modem will be installed

Before unpacking your purchase, define where you want (or they want) the modem and antenna to be permanently located. If it’s in your home, it could be in the living room. If it’s in a community space, it could be in a room that is secure, but where the signal reaches everyone who wants to use it.
Keep in mind that the antenna must be securely attached to the pole, and the pole must be able to be firmly secured, in some way, outside the home or space. We will explain how later.
The modem needs electricity, so identify the power outlet you are going to connect it to.
Finally, define where you are going to run the cable from the antenna to the space where the modem will be. You may have to drill a hole in the wall so you don’t have to leave a window open. CAUTION! Do not do this until you have checked where the antenna works and connects best.




Step 2 → Identify the mobile phone towers in the area

For antennas to work as well as possible, they must be able to “see” each other or, at least, they should point toward the same place.
If you live in a region with many mountains, it will be a bit more difficult to access a good signal compared to a flat place. If this is your case, your antenna will need more height.
Now identify the nearest phone tower. Look for tall towers with antennas. Normally, they are located on the peaks of the highest mountains to allow for greater coverage. It is very important that you locate it because that is where your antenna should point.

If you don’t know where the nearest cellular phone tower is, you can also ask your neighbors.

Taken from Wikimedia Commons
🎉 If you made it this far, it means you have already managed to establish the location of the main elements of your solution. That is, you already know…

Where to install your antenna (where it will stay).
Where it should point, that is, toward the nearest phone tower.
Where you will put the modem that will generate the WiFi signal to connect computers or cell phones.

You’re doing great! Now comes the easy part: assembling the antenna.


Step 3 → Insert the SIM and connect the modem to electricity

Open the modem box. It should include a power cable, an Ethernet cable (to connect a computer), and a quick start guide (instructions). Read the guide carefully because every antenna is different. The following steps of this solution should match those in the guide, only in more detail.
Keep in mind that inserting the SIM can be complex. I had to make several attempts until I succeeded. Make sure the metallic part of the SIM (the chip) matches the metallic contacts of the modem. I’ll explain it a bit better below.

Identify the size of the SIM card that corresponds to the modem tray.
First, open the modem cover where the SIM is inserted (usually on the back of the modem). Identify the size of the card you must insert. The modem instructions (quick start) will indicate it. The model I have uses the Mini SIM size.

Insert the SIM card into the tray.
You will notice that both the SIM tray and the SIM card have a cut corner (beveled). This indicates the position in which you must insert the card.

Insert the SIM carefully into the tray and cover it back up.

Connect the power cable to the modem and the power outlet.
Then, turn on the modem as indicated in the guide. It may be automatic or with a power button.
Check that the modem is connected to the internet.
On the front of the modem, you will find different connection indicators, and in the instructions, what each one means. In the example model, we see that:


The first indicator from left to right shows if it is on or off.
When the second one is red, it means it has no signal. If it is blue or green, it means it is connected. (In this example, it is connected).
The third indicates that the modem is emitting a wireless or WiFi signal in the space.
The fourth shows if an ethernet cable is connected (in this case, no).
And the fifth represents the signal strength (like the signal bars on a cell phone). In this example, the signal is very good.

Once this step is finished, your modem is ready, you are halfway through the solution! If the connection indicator (the second one in the example) is red, simply turn off the modem and let’s connect the antenna to it.


Step 4 → Connect all the antenna elements and hoist the antenna

The time has come to assemble your antenna. The best way to start is to take out and put together all the elements needed to assemble it. Then, let’s start.
Adjust the antenna to the highest end of the pole.
Start by adjusting the antenna mount to the base of the antenna using the screws provided for this. Tighten the screws carefully, making sure they are well adjusted.
Then adjust the antenna mounts to the highest end of the pole. Remember that the pole must be shorter than the length of the cable you have. The mounts have a piece to “wrap” the pole so that when you tighten the nuts, it grips the pole as in the image.


  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

Extend the cable and connect the end that goes to the antenna cable.
Unrolling the cable and extending it to its full length helps make it easier to handle. Look for the connector that fits the antenna connector and connect them.


Find the modem connector to the cable and connect.
In this modem model, there is a cover on the back of the modem that you must remove with a little force (keep the cover in the modem box). There you will find the place to connect the cable. Tighten the connector thread to the maximum carefully.

  
    
      
    
    
      
    
  

Now you can hoist the antenna with the help of another person and point it toward the phone tower you identified in the second step. Then, turn on the modem and that’s it. You have only two steps left to finish. Bravo! 👏🏽


Step 5 → Connect the computer or cell phone to the modem

Turn on the WiFi on your computer or cell phone and search for the modem’s network. You usually find the network name on a sticker on the base of the modem. There you will also find the password to connect. Enter the information on your device and with this, you are ready to browse the Internet!
If your computer has an Ethernet → input, you can also connect directly by cable. Connecting by cable will always give you the best possible internet browsing speed.

If you managed to connect, go to the next step. If not, read what follows.
Couldn’t connect to the internet? I have some recommendations for you 👇🏽
Sometimes we are in places distant from cellular phone towers or with a lot of interference between the tower and our antenna. If this is your case, you can try some alternatives.

Enter the modem’s administration webpage and try pointing the antenna in other directions.

Enter your device’s browser (it could be Firefox, Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, or Explorer) and type your modem’s IP address. Generally, you can find this address on the same sticker under the modem. The IP of this modem 👇🏽, for example, is 192.168.8.1.


When you enter that IP address, you will see the modem login page. There they will ask you for the password, which you also find on the sticker. Usually, the password is admin in lowercase.
Then they will ask you some questions to configure your modem’s preferences. Read carefully and select what you think is best. When finished, you will arrive at the modem’s home page where you can find out the quality and speed of the connection.

If the green checkmarks or ticks appear, it means everything is well connected. On the other hand, if you see a red exclamation mark and an “X” on the internet bars, it means there is no connection.

This is where you must start turning the antenna, trying to point it in another direction until you find a better connection with the cellular phone tower. Do it slowly and in small intervals. Also, point it slightly more upward or downward using the different holes of the antenna mount to the pole.

Every time you change the position of your antenna, wait a few seconds to see if the indicators on the screen or on the device change. If the internet bars and the green check or tick appear, you have managed to get a signal! Congratulations! You can now browse the internet.


💡 How is internet usage measured?
Usage is measured by the amount of data downloaded to your computer or cell phone when making “a query” (for example, watching a video, listening to a song, reading an article in an online newspaper, or receiving a text message). The “weight” of each of those files is measured in bytes of information, and the most common measure when you buy a data plan is Gigas, Gb, or Gigabytes.
Do you know how many things you can do with 1 Giga (1Gb)? Go to this link → to find out!



💡 How fast can you access information on the internet?
Just like knowing how much they “weigh,” it is important to know at what speed you can access those files you are consulting. This is measured in Megabytes per second or Mbps that are downloaded to your computer or cell phone.
Do you know what speed you need to have certain services? Go to this link → to find out!



🧭 Run speed tests
Now that you know about data weight and speed, you can run your own speed test. This will allow you to know how fast data is being downloaded from the internet. For this, consult the solution How to test your Internet connection speed? →. There you will find the step-by-step guide.


Still can’t connect? 😖 Here are some more advanced recommendations for you 👇🏽
For greater precision, you can perform signal strength tests by turning the antenna in different directions.
Sometimes geographical conditions are more complex than we imagine. In those cases, we will have to determine if the antenna is effectively connected to the cellular phone tower and with what quality.
For that, enter the “Advanced” section in the modem menu and look for “System” and then “Device Information”. That’s how it appears on my modem, but it should be something similar on yours.

In this list of information, you will find several data points. The 4 parameters you are looking for are:

RSRQ, which indicates signal quality;
RSRP, which indicates signal strength;
RSSI, which indicates signal force;
SINR, which indicates the relationship between the signal and the noise being generated.

*Remember that the signal is electromagnetic waves traveling through the air.

Below, you can see a table that indicates the coverage parameters of the cellular signal your antenna is receiving. Note that three of them are negative numbers, and as they get closer to zero, the signal improves. This information may seem a bit technical, but don’t worry, it is not necessary to understand it in great depth for it to work.








































CoverageRSRQRSRPRSSISINRExcellent> -10 dB> -80 dBm> -65 dBm> 20 dBGood-10 dB to -15dB-80 dBm to -90 dBm-65 dBm to -75 dBm13 dB to 20 dBMedium-15 dB to -20 dB-90 dBm to -100 dBm-75 dBm to -85 dBm0 dB to 13 dBLow< -20 dB< -100 dBm< -85 dBm< -0 dB
*Keep in mind that ”>” means “greater than” and ”<” means “less than”. That is, ”> -10 dB” means “greater than -10dB”.
*Remember that negative numbers work in reverse to positive numbers. For example, -10dB is greater than -80dB (because it is closer to zero).
With this information in mind, what you should do is continue rotating the hoisted antenna in small intervals and wait a few seconds to see how those numbers change.
I focus mainly on the RSRP, which is the connection strength. It may be useful to draw a circle on the floor around the antenna pole and draw lines that divide the circle into equal pieces. Then, point the antenna in the direction of each line and check if the parameter improved or worsened. If it improved, keep turning and checking the parameter. If it worsened, go back to the previous point.
This is how the antenna is positioned with greater precision. Good luck capturing the signal! You have become a true internet tinkerer.


💡 Keep in mind that weather affects the signal
As you are using an outdoor antenna, weather conditions may affect how fast or slow your connection is. For example, a very humid day can make your connection slower. Don’t worry, little by little you will improve your internet usage experience together as you try new solutions.



Step 6 → Fix the antenna

We have reached our last step!
Now, knowing the best direction for the antenna, it is time to install your antenna permanently to a wall, a column, or a tree, in the place you determined in Step 1.
Tighten the antenna mounts to the pole and hoist the antenna
With the help of a wrench, tighten the antenna mounts to the pole firmly to ensure they don’t move with the wind or rain or if a bird lands on top. If you already had them well tightened, it is not necessary to do this again.


Anchor the pole to the wall or the support you have
Then, use suitable supports to anchor the pole to the base. If it is to a wall, drill and put in wall plugs and screws to secure it. If it is to a tree, tie it with wire.


Once fixed, you have finished the installation of a 3G/4G antenna that will allow you to have a WiFi signal in a fixed space.
You are, officially, the “tinkerer” of your home or community. Congratulations! 👷🏽‍♀️🎉👷🏽
Through trial and error, you will be able to feel more and more confident to tinker, that is, to solve by doing. Now, would you be encouraged to do another solution? Go ahead and keep browsing! See more solutions →

What can you achieve with this solution?
Among many connectivity solutions I have tried, this is one of the best for creating a space to access the Internet together, allowing several people to connect at the same time to a WiFi signal in places where the 3G or 4G signal is weak.
I recommend it not only for the home but for common spaces such as schools, libraries, businesses, or community halls. It also works in public spaces like parks if they have some place to leave it under lock and key and with constant electricity.

Keep in mind that if there is no mobile phone coverage, this solution will not work. But don’t be discouraged, phone coverage is gradually increasing all over the planet. In the meantime, you can consult another SOLE tool called “The Disconnected” →, where you will find solutions for places where there is no internet.

Although it is not an economical solution (the price of an antenna is between 370 - 400 USD), I have seen that it can have a great impact as it becomes a community internet access point.
For this, the community could agree, buy it with contributions from everyone, and maintain it together. This may result in a considerable initial expense, but in the future, it is cheaper than when each person buys their own individual data plan.


💡 At SOLE Colombia, we have carried out this solution with communities where an antenna is installed in a community space that everyone can access. There, the community decides how much, when, and for what the internet is used. In this way, data top-ups are collectively regulated according to needs and are maximized in a shared way.
For example, it is prioritized that children can do their homework or that the community watches a movie together, over individual uses such as access to social networks. This, of course, implies new challenges. But the starting point is clear: they already have internet access!



💬💪🏽 Learn about our experience with a community in Cáceres, Antioquia →



Knowing this, how far would you like to go? Is this a solution you could encourage where you live? We hope it has been useful to you! And if it was, share it with other people who you know could benefit from it.

en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.title: How to know how good your mobile signal is without a speed test?
en/solve/solv-internet-quality-diagnosis.content:
Hi, I’m Manuela. I’m the storyteller for SOLE Colombia and, although I don’t know much about technology, I’ve started to enjoy tinkering with things and I learn many things that constantly get me out of a jam.
What does it mean to know how good your signal is?
An Internet connection isn’t a ghost that follows us everywhere… or maybe it is a little bit of a ghost!
This is a way you can learn a little more about what the Internet is, how to know what is failing at a given moment, or how to improve your signal.

What is it for?
Knowing how good your Internet connection is can give you clues to understand its performance and solve potential problems.
For example, it will let you know if the speed you contracted with your mobile phone or internet service provider is what you are actually receiving… or if they are ripping you off.
You can identify the areas in your community, or in your house, where you have the best signal. This way, you can know where the movie you are watching will hang, or where you should stand to receive someone’s call better.
You will be able to make decisions if you need to restart the router →, or change the reception channel of your WiFi → signal. Or also determine if your modem needs to be replaced.
By optimizing the signal, you will have a faster and more stable connection to be able to do SOLE or access certain content that requires a better signal.

What do you need?

Your device
To be connected to the Internet signal


How to do it?

Step 1 → Take your cell phone and see if you have a mobile signal

Look at one of the top corners of your cell phone. There you will find some mobile signal bars: If you see one or more bars, it means that the phone is receiving a signal and reading your SIM card →.

Step 2 → How much power does your connection have?

Power is not the same as speed. The little bars measure the RSSI (Received Signal Strength Indicator), that is, the power. Think of this as the volume of a voice in a room: when there are more bars, it means someone is speaking loudly; when there are few bars, it means someone is speaking softly.
However, just because you hear someone loudly doesn’t guarantee that the person is speaking fast. The actual speed of your internet depends on the bandwidth → available at the tower and how many people are connected at the same time.
The more bars you have, the more power the mobile signal you receive has. You need both, power and speed, to perform different activities on the Internet. If you don’t have a way to measure the speed of your connection, you can get an idea of the speed thanks to the type of connection.


Step 2 → What type of mobile connection do you have and what are they for?

Look next to the mobile signal bars and you will see some letters that indicate the type of signal you have. These letters refer to the speeds and technologies that operators use to send you information (Internet data).
Did you find them? If so, check the following list to see what you can do with each one.

G: It is the abbreviation for the GPRS signal type, the slowest of all technologies. It is a second-generation or 2G network that only allows you to send text messages.
E: It is the abbreviation for the EDGE signal type, it is an improved version of GPRS, also called 2.5G, and it is used for simple internet searches.


3G: Also called UMTS, it is a third-generation network, designed for browsing multimedia content.
H: It uses HSPA technology; it is something like an improved 3G. It is more than enough to access social networks or listen to music on the Internet.
H+: It is an evolved HSPA to watch videos online or download them more quickly.
4G: It is the technology also called LTE, it is considered the fourth generation or 4G. The speed of this network reaches 100 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload, this is what we call “broadband.” Very fast!
5G: It is the fastest technology of all, for now, and it can be 100 times faster than 4G. You need a phone that supports 5G to be able to use it.




Step 3 → How good is your connection?

How many bars do you see? What type of signal do you have? Now that you have been able to explore these questions, you can have an idea of how good your connection is without doing a speed test. Remember, with the different types of signal you can…

G: only send text messages
E: browse web pages
3G, H, H+: browse social networks, listen to music, and watch videos
4G, LTE: have video calls and watch high-definition videos




Other possible internets
If you managed to identify how many signal bars you have and the type of signal, you will be able to know how good your connection is, and if you know the above, you will have achieved the goal of this solution!

What can you achieve with this solution?
Internet speed tests need… Internet. So in situations where the connection is very low or slow, the speed meters might not work. In these cases, this solution is very useful!
It also helps you better understand what the different codes on your cell phone mean and even to know the current connectivity situation of the place where you are. If the signal is very bad, you can call your neighbors to look for places with a better connection together or even to pay for a shared Internet plan or some other connectivity solution to use the Internet as a group.

en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.title: How to check your internet connection speed?
en/solve/solv-internet-speedtest.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. Until very recently, I didn’t know that one could test the speed of my Internet connection. I found it very easy and very useful to learn how to do it because it allows me to know the status of my connection at any given moment.
Understanding why some things don’t work for me at certain times gives me peace of mind and allows me to look for solutions. Would you like to learn too? Let’s get started! 🧭💪🏽

What is testing your internet connection speed?
An internet connection speed test, or “speed test”, is a tool that measures the speed of your internet connection by evaluating the download and upload speed of data and the network latency →.

What is it for?
A speed test is useful for several things.


It is useful to verify if the speed contracted with your provider matches the actual speed you receive. This allows you to make informed decisions about your internet service provider. For example: Am I really receiving what I was offered? Is it worth staying with this provider? Are there others that offer me a better connection?


It also helps you to identify connection problems, or places and situations where your signal is better or worse. For example, to 4G antenna →, you need to measure the speed several times until you find the direction where you have the best reception.


Knowing the quality of your internet also allows you to know the services you can access. For example, do you know what speed you need to watch a video on YouTube? Keep reading to find out!👇🏽



What do you need?

The device you are going to connect to the Internet with (cell phone, computer, tablet, etc.)
Access to a website, or download a measurement app, such as “Fast”, “Speedtest” or nPerf. There are also mobile applications such as Speedtest by Ookla.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Access a speed test service

You can do your test directly here 👇🏽

  
  
  
    This measurement is made possible thanks to Meter.net
  

If it doesn’t work for you, here are some more options:

Web services: Fast →, Speedtest → or nPerf →.
There are also mobile applications such as Speedtest by Ookla →.



Step 2 → Run the test

Start the test on the website or application. Wait a few seconds until the number stabilizes.
If you need to take a new measurement, press the restart button.

⚠️⚠️ Remember that every time you run a test, you are consuming data. So if you have a limited data plan, try to run tests only when necessary.



Step 3 → Interpret the results

The results generally show the download speed, upload speed, and latency →. Let me explain better:

Download speed: This is the speed at which you can receive data from the Internet, such as when downloading files or watching videos. The higher, the better.
Upload speed: This is the speed at which you can send data to the Internet, such as when sending emails or uploading videos to social networks. Here too, the higher, the better.
Latency (ping): This is the time it takes for a signal to travel back and forth between your device and a remote server →, measured in milliseconds.
Here, a lower ping is better, especially for online games, video calls, or high-quality videos.


💬❓ Now the big question, how much speed is enough? Go to this link → to find out how much speed you need to access different services.

Now that you know your internet speed and the speed you need to access different services, you can see more solutions → that will allow you to get, improve, or share your internet.


Additional considerations:

Wired connection → vs. WiFi →: Wired (Ethernet) speed tests are usually more accurate than WiFi tests, as the WiFi connection can be affected by interference.
Test servers →: Some services allow you to choose the test server to get more accurate results or to test different locations.
Interpreting the results: Compare the results with the speed contracted with your provider and consider factors such as the time of day and the activity on your network →, as this can affect the results.


Other possible internets
If you managed to find out the upload and download values and the latency of your internet connection, you have achieved the first part of the solution. Congratulations!
Beyond the technical aspect, this solution works when it allows people like you to:

Verify the performance of the internet connection, so that you have more information to make decisions, for example, regarding the internet provider.
Diagnose connection problems to, for example, identify places where there is a better or worse connection.
Optimize the online experience, so that you can optimize your activities for what you need. For example, you can avoid downloading heavy files during peak hours, close windows you are not using, disconnect equipment so as not to overload the modem, among others.


What can you achieve with this solution?
Diagnosing the state of connectivity in remote contexts is fundamental to knowing what type of connectivity solution is most appropriate for each context.

For us at SOLE, it has been very important to know how to do this when we go to work with communities. We have discovered that having a complete experience of the internet, in which people learn to recognize their own internet connection conditions, as well as the fluctuations and inconveniences of the place where a solution is to be installed, encourages people to get more engaged. It is a very powerful and intense strategy to promote self-organized learning.
Feeling capable of being able to establish or improve the Internet signal to be able to use it in a group makes everything more powerful… you can see the stories in the inspirations section → of Voltaje⚡⚡.

en/solve/solv-jangala-install-box.title: How to install a Jangala Big Box?
en/solve/solv-jangala-install-box.content:
Hello! My name is Catalina. I recently discovered the Jangala Big Box, and I think they are a brilliant connectivity solution! This is the first solution I am writing to share on Voltaje. It will be short but substantial; I hope you find it useful. Let’s get started!

What is installing a Jangala Big Box?
A Jangala Big Box is a very powerful modem that can capture different types of signals to redistribute them to up to 100 people.
In this solution, I will guide you to access the Big Box installation manual, where you will find instructions for linking different signal sources (SIM Card, cable antennas, among others) to the device.

What is it for?
To install the Jangala Big Box yourself and enjoy the internet as a community.

💬⚠️ Keep in mind that you need to have a Jangala for this solution to be useful. Consult the solution “The internet in a box: Jangala’s Big Box” → to learn how to get a Jangala Big Box.


What do you need?

A Jangala Big Box.
A device to connect to the internet (cell phone, tablet, computer, or any other).
Internet connection.
Attention.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Go to the Jangala page and choose the manual in the language you want.

Go to the instructions section of the Jangala website by clicking on this link →.
Upon entering, you will see several blue buttons. Choose the one in your preferred language (Spanish?). A new window will open, and you will be able to see the instructions.


Step 2 → Download the instructions

It is possible that the place where you are consulting this information (good connectivity) is not the place where you are going to install your Jangala (low connectivity).
If that is your case, you can download the instructions to your cell phone or computer to always have them available.

Other possible internets
If you manage to turn on your Jangala and connect to the internet from a couple of devices, you will know that your effort has been successful!

What can you achieve with this solution?
Get a very powerful internet running in your community!! Not only because you will have a stronger signal, but because it allows many people to access the internet.

en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.title: The internet in a box: Jangala's Big Box
en/solve/solv-jangala-internet-box.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay, and although I’m not an expert in connectivity, I’ve learned by tinkering, which is to say, through trial and error, researching on the internet with other people, and learning from those who have the experience. Let me briefly tell you what the Jangala Big Box is 👇🏽

Video conceived, created, and produced by SOLE Colombia, 2024
What is managing a Jangala Big Box?
With this solution, you will be able to contact an organization in England that offers a very powerful portable modem, called the Big Box, which allows up to 100 people to connect to the internet at the same time.
The organization that offers it is called Jangala and it is dedicated to providing internet access to people who require urgent humanitarian aid or support for longer-term development processes.

⚠️⚠️ It is important for you to know that these devices are not for personal use and that you must meet some eligibility criteria. They are the ones who, based on the information you register in the application form, evaluate whether your community or project can access their product.

We encourage you, together with your community, to imagine how an internet connection could improve your living conditions and how you can use it for the common good. Develop the idea and tell Jangala about it. We are sure they will consider it.

What is it for?
Imagine a community without connectivity, without technical knowledge for the installation, configuration, and maintenance of a wireless network. Now think that, all of a sudden, everyone manages to connect to a single WiFi → network. What would happen?
Among many things, an entire community could pay for a single internet plan and connect in a shared way. Better yet, they could do it from common equipment, such as computers or tablets, and have higher speed, a better experience, and a collective and fun learning process.
That is what you could achieve if you manage this device: the Big Box from Jangala.
The Jangala Big Box is a lightweight device, the size of a briefcase, that transforms any form of internet connectivity into a WiFi network that is easy to manage and expand, from dozens to thousands of users. It’s like having a phone internet amplifier that can serve hundreds, or even thousands, of computers.
Internet access is an urgent need in many situations around the world: from people trying to make contact after an earthquake to educational projects in remote areas. However, in these contexts, the internet is often unavailable. Networks often go down in emergency situations, and deploying effective internet access in remote areas is complicated, slow, and expensive.
Who is Jangala? Jangala is an NGO in the UK that seeks to solve this with their machines.
This solution will help you learn how to manage this powerful modem with the Jangala organization and have their support to adapt the Big Box to the needs of your context or, if you are part of an organization, to the conditions of the communities you work with.
If you are a low-income community, or in a remote area, you may be considered to receive one of their units at no cost and for life.

What do you need?

An internet connection and a computer (you can also use a cell phone)
To understand English or translate with the online translator DeepL.
Confidence in your management ability
Conditions of digital exclusion; Jangala will estimate if you are suitable to be a Big Box recipient.
Enthusiasm!


How to do it?

Step 1 → Go to www.janga.la and look for the Big Box application form

Go to Jangala get box, to the “Request a Box” section. There you can decide if what you need is a Get Box, which is smaller, or a Big Box.
The following steps have to do with the Big Box application.



Step 2 → Fill out the online form

In the Big Box section, you will find a button that says Apply for a Big Box.
It is necessary to answer the questions in the form; this will help Jangala configure a Big Box that best meets the needs of your community.
The questionnaire is divided into four sections:

Section 1 asks questions about you and/or your organization.
Section 2 is about the place for which you need a Big Box, including location, existing connectivity, and power supply.
Section 3 is about the Wi-Fi configuration.
Section 4 contains final questions about how the Big Box will make a difference.

If there is anything in this form that is not clear, or does not apply to your community’s situation, do not hesitate to send an email to info@janga.la.
Filling out this form can take some time and you may not have all the answers clear. Try to answer as many questions as possible to the best of your ability and don’t forget to press the “Submit” button.


Step 3 → Wait for a response and start a relationship with Jangala

It may take a few weeks to receive a response from the Jangala team. They will write to the email address you registered in the form.
Be patient and stay tuned for the response… that moment will be very exciting!
It is possible that there will be more questions or that a virtual meeting with you will be required. At the time of the meeting, you will be able to clarify more doubts, define the specifics of your Big Box, and the process by which you will receive it by postal mail.
The Jangala team is exceptional: always very kind and genuinely willing to help.


Step 4 → Plan and receive the Big Box by postal mail

After clarifying how Jangala will send the equipment, it will not take more than a couple of weeks to receive the Big Box with the features you need.
It is very important to ask the Jangala team to make it clear in the certified mail shipment that it is goods without commercial value, because, depending on the country where you are, customs may require specific information about the equipment to be able to receive the package.
For example, in Colombia, to enter a cell phone, it is necessary to include the IMEI number (with which a cell phone is registered) on the package’s shipping invoice. If this is not done, the package must be nationalized at customs, which is a complex and expensive process. In any case, the Jangala team will be a great support in solving any challenge, and they cover those costs.


Step 5 → Install the Big Box

Finally, all that remains is to install the Big Box → in the place where it will be used, and that’s it!
The Jangala team will offer you support during installation or use. Once installed, you will have WiFi Internet for about 100 people within a 100-meter radius!
Now, all that’s left is to use it for the common good.

Other possible internets
You will know the day you receive a response from Jangala. Regardless of whether the answer is positive or not, just receiving it is proof that you did the management correctly, and that is already a great achievement!
If you are a charity or a group that needs connectivity for some common purpose, Jangala will love to meet you. Jangala can provide devices and tools in the form of long-term interest-free loans to organizations with limited financial means that provide vital basic services to people affected by disasters or to organizations that need help for long-term project development.
Remember that any of the Boxes provide WiFi through any form of Internet signal (3G/4G, landline, satellite), can use power from various sources (mains, battery, cigarette lighter, renewable source, generator), and can use an external antenna → to pick up 3G/4G signals where phones cannot.

How many people does it connect? 100. With additional equipment, it can reach up to 1,000. With extensive equipment, up to 5,000.
Can it be used in a mobile environment? Yes.
Can it be used outdoors? Yes. It is waterproof and resistant.
Can it power additional Wi-Fi access points? Yes. They can be used to connect up to 5,000 people in a large area.
How many networks can it broadcast? Four. Each of them can be customized in terms of content control, speed restrictions, and data restrictions.




💡 At SOLE Colombia, we have implemented this solution with communities where an antenna is installed in a community space that everyone can access. There, the community decides how much, when, and for what the internet is used.
For example, priority is given to children doing their homework or the community watching a movie together, over individual uses such as accessing social networks. This, of course, implies new challenges. But the starting point is clear: they already have internet access!

💬💪🏽 Learn about our experience with a community in Nuevo México, Santander de Quilichao →



What can you achieve with this solution?
The Jangala Big Box is an opportunity to get free or very low-cost connectivity for an entire community. For example, a school or a refugee camp. Imagine the learning possibilities they would have if they use the internet together!

⚠️⚠️ Mind you, keep in mind that the Jangala Big Box will not solve connectivity if there is no Internet signal (cable, mobile, or satellite) in the area.


Related solutions

Remember that the Jangala Big Box needs some kind of signal to work. If you do it through a SIM Card (cellular signal), this solution can help you decide which internet plan to buy: How to buy a suitable cell phone plan for me? →
Having a “Big Box” means that we must take care of it as a community. Using a playful tool, you can learn to do it together: How to use games to learn to take care of equipment as a community? →
Community internet is more powerful when used in a group. I share some recommendations for finding a meeting space: How to adapt a space to use the Internet in a group? →

en/solve/solv-know-ram.title: "How to know how much RAM I have?"
en/solve/solv-know-ram.content:
Hi! I’m David. I’ve managed to better understand how my equipment works through trial and error, and today I want to share a quick way to get to know the guts of your computer. We will rely on what we already know and confirm some steps with digital tools so you can’t go wrong.

What is RAM memory?
The RAM Memory → is like a kitchen assistant with a short-term memory. Imagine your computer is a kitchen: the RAM is the work counter.
The assistant is very fast at handing you the ingredients you need right now on the counter, but as soon as you turn off the stove (the computer), she cleans everything up and forgets what she was doing.
If your counter is very small (low RAM), the assistant gets cluttered with pots and everything slows down. That is why knowing how much memory you have is key to not overloading your equipment.

What is it for?
Knowing how much RAM you have allows you to understand if your computer can open many programs at the same time or if it will “hang” with heavy tasks like videos or games.

What do you need?

Your computer (Windows or Mac →) turned on.
A couple of calm minutes.


How to do it?
First, identify if your equipment is Windows or Mac →.
On Windows (10 and 11)

Step 1 → The quick path: Settings

Press the Windows + i keys on your keyboard (the letter i for information). A settings window will open.

If you have Windows 10: Go to “System” and then look at the bottom left where it says “About”.
If you have Windows 11: Go to “System” and look for the “About” option at the end of the list.

Look for where it says “Installed RAM”. There you will see a number like 4GB, 8GB, or 16GB.


Step 2 → The administrator path (to see real usage)

If you want to see how much work the “assistant” has at the moment:

Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc at the same time.
Click on the Performance tab and then on Memory.

Here you will see how much memory you are using and how much is left free.


You’re doing well: If you see that the graph is very high (near the top), it means your “counter” is full of pots and plates.

On Mac computers (Apple →)

Step 1 → The Apple menu

Click on the Apple icon () in the top left corner of your screen and select “About This Mac”.
A small window will open where you will clearly see the word Memory.


Step 2 → Using the Terminal (for the curious)

If you want to feel like an expert, you can use the Terminal →.

Open the Terminal (search for it in Spotlight with Cmd + Space).
Type the command: vm_stat and press Enter.

This will show you a lot of technical information, including the use of Swap Memory →.

What is Swap Memory? It is as if the assistant, upon running out of space on the counter, started using a drawer in the cupboard (the hard drive) → to put plates. It is slower than the counter, but it helps the kitchen not to stop.


Recommendations…

If you have 4GB of RAM, try not to have many internet tabs open at the same time.
With 8GB, you can already work comfortably on most office and study tasks.
If you notice that your equipment always uses “Swap,” it might be time to think about increasing the physical RAM or switching to an SSD if your equipment allows it.


How to know if it works?
If you managed to see the number (e.g., 8 GB) and understand if you are using a lot or a little, congratulations! You now know your work tool better.

What can you achieve with this solution?
By knowing how much RAM you have, you stop getting frustrated when the equipment slows down and you start making decisions: should I close this program?, do I need to upgrade my equipment?, can I install this game?

Recommended solutions

Why is my internet slow? →
Give your old computer a second life →

Keep tinkering, that’s how you really learn!

en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.title: How to find the WiFi passwords on my phone?
en/solve/solv-know-wifi-passwords.content:
Hi, I’m Belén. I’m not a tech expert, but I’ve learned how to use technology as it has appeared. I won’t deny it, I like reading the manuals for the devices I buy, and I take it upon myself to understand many of the updates that get installed on my mobile phone… such a nerd!

What does it mean to know the WiFi passwords on your phone?
I remember when you had to enter the modem password every time you connected to the Internet. If there is one thing I appreciate about this new era of smartphones, it is the time saved by not having to type the WiFi password every time you connect. But where are they saved? How can one share those keys or passwords with someone? Keep reading 👇🏽

What is it for?
With this solution, you will be able to explore the WiFi → passwords that you already have stored on your phone.
If you want to do a SOLE in a place where you have been connected before, you can reconnect to the WiFi network without having to re-enter all the characters of the password (which is sometimes very long or very complicated).

What do you need?

Mobile phone with operating system → Android.
Internet connection.
At least one WiFi password saved on your phone.
Curiosity.
Attention.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Explore your passwords

First, access your phone’s “Settings.” Next, go to the WiFi section, where you will see all the available networks around you. Tap the Internet network you already have access to and for which you want to know the password. Once you do, a QR code with this information will appear. Then, take a screenshot of this image.



Step 2 → Decipher the password

The next step is to use a reader that has permission to read this information. We cannot use our own phone’s QR reader, so we can use an online one on the following page: Zxing

Once we are on this page, we upload our image and click the “Submit Query” button. Upon doing so, the network name and the password will appear so you can share it.



Step 3 → Now you can share it!

Now, all that’s left is to share this information with the people you know who need it. Who wants to do a SOLE →? Now that you can share the password, all the teams can start their research and solve whatever Big Question they want!

Other possible internets
With this solution, you will be able to explore all the WiFi passwords that you already have saved on your phone.

What can you achieve with this solution?
You have the ability to know the saved passwords, but not those that you haven’t saved yet. To save them initially, you have to ask the owner of the WiFi to share their password with you, but you won’t have to ask for it again.
Knowing this whole process, is this a solution that could be useful to other people? We hope that, at the very least, it has been useful to you! And if it was, share it with others!
See you soon! 👋🏽
