en/solve/solv-need-3Gantenna.title: Do I need to buy a 3G/4G antenna?
en/solve/solv-need-3Gantenna.content:
Hi, I’m Sanjay. Together with Gabriel, another tinkerer friend, we made our first purchase of a 3/4G antenna after researching commercial solutions to the connectivity problem.
In this solution, I am going to offer you some recommendations for buying a 3/4G antenna.
What is a 3G or 4G antenna?
3G and 4G are abbreviations for the set of technologies required for voice and data transmission in mobile telephony.
This set includes everything from the types of cell phones and antennas to the communication protocols between them, which are necessary to send voice or data via cellular telephony.
I won’t go into the details, but out of curiosity, it is worth knowing that the G stands for generation, and the numbers are the third and fourth generations of these technologies.
Previous generations did not allow sending data, only voice, like a radio. So, for example, old cell phones—which in Colombia we call “flechas” (arrows)—are not useful for receiving Internet data. To be able to connect to the Internet, devices need to be cell phones with 3G technology or higher, that is, to be smartphones →.

What is a 3/4G antenna used for?
I recently understood that the Internet signal that reaches cell phones travels through invisible electromagnetic waves. Cell phones have a small antenna inside that captures those waves. That allows us to have access to the Internet.
Gabriel and I have discovered that buying a commercial 3G or 4G antenna is one of the best solutions for having a stable and reliable Internet connection. Especially in a fixed place like a house, a school, a library, or a store, by making use of mobile telephony in places where coverage is low.
What the antenna does, simply put, is capture and amplify the specific cellular data signal (3G or 4G) that comes in electromagnetic waves through the air from a higher place than where you are—above trees, buildings, or hills—and bring it down via a cable to your level.
Once at that point, the signal can be shared in that space by generating a WiFi network, or by cable, using a modem or router. I know these terms may seem confusing, but as you go through these recommendations, you will have more clarity about them.

If you want to know how you can buy an antenna, and what parameters you should take into account to search for and decide on the 3G/4G antenna that will improve your mobile Internet connection, follow our recommendations.

Before starting, a reflection
Sometimes, we decide to buy the cheapest option because we prefer to save money on a purchase. As they say, “cheap is expensive,” and in the case of technology, such as an antenna, this tends to be true.
We have seen many antennas that become trash, do not fulfill their function (like those from satellite TV providers), and are left installed in cities and rural areas, generating technological waste that, besides being ugly, is never removed or reused.
It is important that you are also clear about the care and maintenance that your purchase may require. Sometimes we buy something and, when it needs maintenance, we don’t have the time or resources to deal with it, and it can become useless. When you agree with others, you can share the care and distribute the expenses, which will make it lighter and more bearable.
Make sure that the antenna you buy works for the conditions of your context and that it is the best option for you.

What do you need?

Recognize the geography of the place where you need a signal.
Identify which operator or operators work best in the region.
An antenna provider.
Some money.
Meet with your community to identify the best option.


How to do it?
Below we present the 4 moments of what we consider when deciding what type of 3G/4G antenna to buy.


Moment 1: How do I know if I need a 3/4G antenna?
There are places where the cellular signal is very weak. You can confirm this on your cell phone by looking at the connection bars: you will see a single bar or something that says H+, E, or even that there is no signal.
However, when you move a few meters or a few kilometers, the signal appears or improves, and you start to see bars with the 3G or 4G symbol on your cell phone.
If this is your case, there may be cell phone towers around you to which you do not have direct visibility, and therefore, you are not able to connect to the 3G/4G network from your initial location.
Buying a 3G/4G antenna will allow you to have a stable Internet connection, but there must be cellular coverage in the area.
It is not an inexpensive solution, but it is the most reliable way to establish an Internet access point for your community if you are in places with low mobile coverage.
If there is no mobile coverage, you will not achieve connectivity with one of these antennas. To get it, you will have to resort to solutions like those we describe in the solution “How to buy a satellite internet service for non-interconnected places?”, where there are various satellite solutions, although they tend to be more expensive.


Moment 2: According to what you need, these are the questions to ask yourself


Where am I located geographically?


The first thing is to understand the geography of where you are located. What you are trying to identify are the cell phone towers that could provide you with a signal. For 3/4G antennas to work, they generally must be able to “see” a tower, or at least they should point toward the same place.
If you live in a region with many mountains, it will be a bit more difficult to access a good signal, unlike in a flat place.
If possible, look for the nearest cell phone tower: look for tall towers with antennas. They are normally located on the peaks of the highest mountains to allow for greater coverage.
If you don’t know where the nearest cell phone tower is, you can also ask your neighbors; perhaps they have already identified it.


Taken from Wikimedia Commons

Which mobile phone service providers have coverage in this area?

In rural areas or places far from urban centers, the coverage of mobile phone operators can be quite inconsistent.
Make sure to find the one that works best in the region. Ask your neighbors which one works best for them. Identify which ones have better coverage, that is, which ones provide a more stable and faster service.
💡 Keep in mind that the coverage of these providers changes over time as they install new repeater antennas or as more people subscribe to their services, saturating their signal.

This information is important for the antenna provider: ensure that the modem they give you has open bands so that you can use the operator you select without restrictions.

Where are the nearest cell phone antenna towers located?

Use a cell phone application to identify which cell phone towers are the closest.
To do this, search in Google Play or the Apple Store for “Cell tower” applications, download one, and use it to identify which antennas, and from which operators, are closest to where you are located.
If there is no signal in the place where you want to test, you can download the map of the antennas in a place with a connection and carry it on your cell phone. It will allow you to interpret it by matching the geographic North and the North of the map.


What is the space I want to provide with internet?

To decide which place you are going to leave the modem connected in, emitting a WiFi signal, it is important that you take into account the geographic location and its connection to electricity.
We recommend thinking about public spaces such as schools, libraries, or community halls, since the internet in those spaces can benefit more people.
If you want the connection for your home, perhaps it is worth putting it in a space like the living room or dining room, rather than in the bedrooms. The spaces in the house intended for rest should be free of the electromagnetic fields of the device, which can affect it, and, on the other hand, physical obstacles can affect the signal in the rest of the house.

How much, and for what, will those who connect use the internet?

Defining how much you are going to use the internet and what you want to use it for is important to know what to expect from the antenna you are going to buy.
To refine your expectations, you can read How is Internet usage measured?

How much money do I, or do we, have to buy an antenna?

In Colombia, in 2024, one of the most powerful antennas on the market, with a robust 15-meter-long cable, plus the modem, cost around COP 1,300,000 or USD 300.
But it is not necessary to face this expense alone; think that the more people contribute to the purchase of the antenna, the cheaper it will be per person. So we encourage you to talk to family and neighbors to agree and share the signal.

Moment 3: What do I need to know to answer these questions?
Recognize the topography of the place

After answering where you are, it is important, if possible, to obtain the precise location of the place where you want to connect.
With the help of an application, locate the exact coordinates of the place where you want to install the antenna.
This data will be useful at the time of purchase. Providers usually have access to updated databases on the coverage of different phone providers, as well as the location, which allows them to advise you more accurately on the type of antenna that best meets your specific needs.
Your phone may have an application to locate your coordinates. If you use Android, go to Google Maps. If you have an iPhone, go to Maps.
Search for your location point, and you will be able to access the exact coordinates of the place where you are. Finally, write down this data to have it on hand when you need it.


Where to buy the antenna?

You can do a SOLE to perform a search on the Internet, where your Big Question contains terms like 4g signal booster antenna. The search should lead you to find nearby distributors.
When you talk to the company that distributes the technology, have all the data you can on hand. Together you will find the best solution for the place where you are going to set up your Internet access point.

What should they give you when you have made the purchase of your antenna?

You have to keep in mind that for the antenna to work, it needs to be connected to a device. So the minimum that your antenna kit should contain is:

A 3/4G antenna
The basic mounting elements
The connection cable
A 3/4G modem

Antenna
The necessary antenna is a yagi type →. It can be similar to the one in the image above, or it can also be encapsulated in a plastic protector, which will protect the antenna and its connections from weather conditions, extending its useful life.
One thing to keep in mind with the antenna is its power. This data is expressed in dB: a 65dB antenna will have more power than a 15dB antenna. As a general rule, the further the antenna is from the provider, the more power will be needed to establish a connection.

Cable
The cable to connect the antenna to the modem is similar to the coaxial cable →, which is used in television connections. However, it is not the same. There is a wide variety of cable types, but at a minimum, in this type of application, cables like RG-6 → should be used. Now, it is recommended to use shielded cables, which minimize signal loss and reduce the production of noise in the system.
You should not modify the cable that the provider gives you in any way: the splicing between the cable and the connectors at the ends is carried out in a way that minimizes noise in the system; any alteration can make all components totally useless.

Modem / Router
Normally, antenna kits come with a modem and a router, which will allow you to connect and share the mobile network signal captured by the antenna.
If you already have a modem, at the time of purchase, verify that it can connect to the antenna and, if necessary, that the provider sends you the necessary adapters to make the connection.

Moment 4: And so… let’s make the decision!

Depending on your geographic conditions, what you want to use it for, and your budget, ask the seller about all possible options.
Don’t forget to talk about the care and maintenance of the devices, especially the expenses involved and the frequency with which you will have to assume them.
The most expensive one is not necessarily the one that will serve you best.

Don’t be fooled
Sometimes, sellers will want to propose more sophisticated and expensive solutions than you will need.
Ask a lot. It is the only way to learn and create criteria to find the best possible option.

How much is enough?
Buying an antenna with the necessary characteristics to access the mobile network will allow you to have a stable connection with which, for example, to meet to learn how to learn, in a group, using the internet.
Also watching movies, consulting a doctor about a situation, communicating with family or friends… so let’s find new ways to use the internet!
Also, when you have a more stable connection, doing a SOLE will be easier.
A single antenna and a single connection, in a group, will be more than enough to be able to enjoy all the options that the internet offers. Even more so, if you use the internet on shared computers, it will be safer, more private, and more fun.

en/solve/solv-organize-space.title: How to adapt a space for group Internet use?
en/solve/solv-organize-space.content:
Hello! I’m Catalina, welcome 👋🏽
I wrote this solution because, over time, I have discovered how the objects around us shape the way we relate to one another. When I joined SOLE, I didn’t just learn a methodology, but an entire way of promoting the use of the Internet in groups through small details (which aren’t so small), such as how a meeting space is arranged.
Have you ever heard of this idea of using the Internet in a group? At SOLE, we are still understanding it. For now, we know it has to do with people getting together to use the Internet, but also with the devices or spaces we use (or invent) to connect, share, and learn with the Internet, especially in person.
Shall we set up your next meeting space together? I’ll join you! 👇🏽

What does it mean to adapt a space for group Internet use?

⚠️ Before you start, it is important to know which space you are going to use. If you don’t have one yet, this solution can help you find one: How to get a community hall or any community space to use the internet in a group?

Adapting a space refers to the way we organize the elements within it: chairs, tables, whiteboards, posters, projectors, whatever.
To host a SOLE, for example, we need to dis-organize the space to avoid it looking like a classroom. This is important because, to promote other ways of learning, it is important that people do not feel like they are in a traditional learning space.
This is important because the ways in which a space is organized generate different interactions between people. Think, for example, of a church and a restaurant.
In a church, all the chairs are arranged in rows facing the front. It is a space of directed attention toward one person (the priest), where there is supposed to be little conversation between people; that is why they are shoulder to shoulder. In a restaurant, on the other hand, people are organized in small groups. There are chairs around various tables where everyone can see each other. It is a space made for interacting, for talking, and of course, for eating.

What is it for?
Planning how a space is organized promotes certain interactions over others. When it comes to using the Internet in a group, we want people to be able to share a computer or the network, but also ideas and experiences—that is, conversations.
So yes, this solution helps ensure that the way you organize a space allows for group Internet use. But it goes further! Using the Internet in a group allows for self-managed learning, planning, and carrying out community projects. If you browse the Internet in a group, it will be harder to fall into traps or fake content because there are more humans to analyze information. But you can also do things that seem simple, like watching a movie, which in turn bring very powerful results, such as several people being able to laugh at the same time.
In short, this solution promotes ways of (re)connecting in a world where it is increasingly common to feel alone.

What do you need?

A space (your own or borrowed)
One table for every 4 people
More chairs than tables; enough for everyone (plastic ones are quite practical)
One computer for every 3-5 people (or at least tablets)
Webcam and microphone (one of the computers can serve this purpose)
A whiteboard or space where you can write (it can also be glass, a window, a blank poster, etc.)
Markers


How to do it?
Rather than a specific step-by-step guide, I prefer to share with you some recommendations for adapting your space, as well as various ways to configure it and the interactions that each of them could trigger.

Recommendation #1 → Plan your meeting, get what you need.

Do you know how many people you are expecting? Have you already planned your activity?
Having a plan of what you will do is key to knowing what you need.
Do you have tables, chairs, a whiteboard? If so, move on to the next step. If not, I can give you some tips on how to get them.
Community spaces usually have tables and chairs. Shops do too. You can borrow them there by making it clear that you take responsibility for them (you can leave a written document that gives the owner peace of mind). If you choose to meet with people at a time when customers don’t visit as much, it is more likely they will lend them to you.
Another option is to use elements that resemble them. At SOLE, for example, we use fruit and vegetable crates to simulate tables and chairs. They are great! And they can often be recycled.
— Photo SOLE stools


Recommendation #2 → Dis-organize the space!

Using the Internet in a group should feel like something pleasant. Something that people choose and not something they have to do. The best way to do this is by making the space feel flexible.
Look at these three different ways to configure the space:
— Photo of spaces
What do they remind you of? How do they make you feel? Here 👇🏽 I share how I remember/feel them:

This is the usual layout of a classroom or a conference space. There is one person (or several) at the front, who usually addresses the audience in a “unidirectional” way, meaning the audience is there mainly to listen, not to intervene. The interaction is more hierarchical: whoever is at the front has the attention.
The circle or crescent layout is, for example, how community meetings or dialogue circles are usually held. This way of positioning allows everyone to see each other and for the sound of voices to circulate and reach everyone easily. This form invites everyone to interact in a “multidirectional” way, making the bond between those interacting less hierarchical.
This is the usual layout of a SOLE or a restaurant. It is a way of positioning that promotes several “small conversations” at the same time. Unlike the first two, this layout allows more people to speak, so the number of people involved in the interaction is reduced. This is an excellent option when we want to cover more topics in the same amount of time or, as in a SOLE, when several people want to focus their attention on something particular.

There are a thousand ways to configure a space. Even these three that I share with you can be mixed together. What I am interested in showing you is that different ways of organizing a space promote different interactions, but also different hierarchies between the people participating in the interaction.
At SOLE, rather than organizing, we like to “dis-organize” the space, because the ideal is that it never looks like a classroom or a Community Action Board event. In group Internet use, it is key to promote horizontal relationships (and not hierarchical ones), where you can talk within small groups, but also between groups.
— Photo SOLE configuration.
I always recommend having a whiteboard or space to write that everyone can see. It works very well as a “memory aid” as conversations develop.

👆🏽 If what you are going to do is a SOLE, you can use the materials from the SOLE Kit to give the space more personality. If it’s not a SOLE, I still recommend decorating with posters or materials that put people in tune with the energy of the activity.



Recommendation #3 → Invent and discover the best way to adapt your spaces

In our experience, this last configuration is the one that has worked best for us to use the Internet in a group. But this is just an idea. Remember that if there is one thing that characterizes a “cacharrero” (tinkerer), it is the exercise of trial and error, so go ahead and try more combinations or new ways to configure your spaces! Surely there will be other ways that work even better for you. Mind you, the only condition is that you share them on Voltaje! (Just kidding, it’s not a condition, but it would be very useful for other people 😋).
Good luck with your meeting!


How to know if this solution works?
Think about what you had in mind when adapting your space. What was your goal? What did you expect to happen? Then (ideally at the end of the meeting), observe the space. What changed in it? What remained the same?
There is no magic formula to know if the space layout worked. But a good sign that it did is that the space has changed. Sometimes people (dis)organize the space more. They move chairs, push tables together, find other places to write… Let them! That is a great way to know that people are taking ownership of the place and that they felt the need to move through it as a result of the conversations they wanted to be in.
Another way is during the meeting. It is not always easy, but try to pay attention to the interactions between people: Where do they talk the most? Where do they laugh? Where do they reflect? Where do they rest? Pay attention to the way the space is arranged every time you see different emotions unfold.

Other possible Internets
We sometimes dream not only of inventing new ways to configure the space, but also of new devices that allow us to interact better and better with the Internet, but in a group. Can you imagine if there were a computer with four keyboards? What would we have to do to write a letter with four hands? What kind of video games could we play? How much more could we learn together?
—four-keyboard computer imagination.
Thinking about new physical ways to foster collective interactions is very powerful in a world where individual interactions are increasingly promoted. How do you design for communities and not just for individuals? What can we do in a group that we cannot do alone? What worlds can we invent and build together?
At SOLE, we have been “inventing” a physical space where the Internet can be used in a group. We call it the SOLE Lab. In fact, there are already three in Colombia!

⚡⚡ Learn about the experience of the most recent one in this inspiration: We built a SOLE Lab in La Guajira to use the Internet in a group, and the others in the “Get Inspired” section.

But we want more communities in Colombia and the world to be able to have one! That’s why now in 2026 we are creating the “do it yourself” version of this space, which will be something like assembling furniture but in a space version.
—video SOLE Lab HUM
And what do you think? Hopefully, these questions will encourage you to imagine other ways of relating to the Internet. Or as we say, other possible Internets!

Related solutions

If you still don’t know how to summon people, check out this solution: How to write an invitation that summons? →

en/solve/solv-pocket-wikipedia.title: How to access an encyclopedia without internet?
en/solve/solv-pocket-wikipedia.content:
Hello! I’m Gabriel and I’m an artist. I like technology and I am one of the first tinkerers at SOLE Colombia. I’m not an expert, but I’ve learned through trial and error, and that’s the best way to learn!

What is the pocket Wikipedia?
Imagine you could fit the largest library in the world into a little box that fits in your hand. That is Kiwix: a program that stores all of Wikipedia (with its text and images) so you can consult it even if you don’t have a single bit of internet.

What is it for?
Having a pocket Wikipedia on your Raspberry Pi → allows you to take knowledge anywhere: a rural school, a community center, or your own home. It’s like having your own water well instead of waiting for it to rain; the information is always there, ready for when someone has a Big Question.

What do you need?

Your Raspberry Pi already up and running (as if it were the building for our library).
A computer to give it instructions.
Internet connection (only this once, to download the books).
Lots of patience: downloading all of Wikipedia takes time, it’s better if you have someone to have a coffee with while you wait!


How to do it?

Step 1 → Connect to your remote library

Before starting, make sure your Pi is turned on. We are going to talk to it from our computer using a Terminal → and starting an SSH → connection. It’s like sending a radio message to someone inside the building.


Step 2 → Download the “librarian” (Kiwix)

Kiwix is in charge of searching for information. First, we are going to download its tools. Copy and paste this into your terminal:
wget download.kiwix.org/release/kiwix-tools/kiwix-tools_linux-armhf.tar.gz



Step 3 → Bring the books (compressed Wikipedia)

Now let’s go for the content. We are going to download a version of Wikipedia in Spanish. It is a heavy file (about 3.3GB), so this is where the coffee and conversation come in.
wget download.kiwix.org/zim/wikipedia/wikipedia_es_all_mini_2022-11.zim


Cheer up: if the internet is slow, don’t despair. Once it finishes, you will never need the internet to read this ever again!



Step 4 → Organize the library shelves

We already have the files, now we have to put them in their place. We are going to decompress the librarian’s tools and move them to the Pi’s “executables” folder.

Decompress:
tar -zxvf kiwix-tools_linux-armhf.tar.gz

Move to its place:
sudo mv kiwix-tools_linux-armhf-3.3.0-1/* /usr/local/bin





Step 5 → Locate the Wikipedia book

The .zim file (which is like a giant compressed book) must go into a special folder so the librarian can find it quickly:
sudo mv wikipedia_es_all_mini_2022-11.zim /var/local/


Step 6 → Hire a librarian who never sleeps

So you don’t have to turn on the program every time you restart the Pi, we are going to create a “service.” This will make Kiwix start automatically as soon as you plug the Pi into power.
Create the configuration file:
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/kiwix.service
Paste this content inside (use the keyboard arrows and Ctrl+O to save, Ctrl+X to exit):
[Unit]
Description=Kiwix Service
After=network.target
 
[Service]
Type=simple
User=root
Group=root
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/kiwix-serve /var/local/wikipedia_es_all_mini_2022-11.zim -p 8080
Restart=always
RestartSec=3
 
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target


You’re doing well: you’re about to finish! You just need to give the power-on command.



Step 7 → Start the engines!

Now tell the Pi to recognize this new service and start it right away:
sudo systemctl enable kiwix
sudo systemctl start kiwix


Step 8 → Open your library from any device

Done! Now, from any cell phone or computer connected to the same network as your Pi, open the browser and type: solevoltaje.local:8080.


How to know if it works?
If when you enter the address you see the Wikipedia search engine and can browse the articles, you did it! You have an entire encyclopedia living inside your little Raspberry Pi.

What can you achieve with this solution?
With your pocket Wikipedia, you can now organize SOLE sessions in any park, mountain, or community hall, regardless of whether there is cell signal. You are democratizing access to information and proving that knowledge does not have to depend on a monthly subscription.

en/solve/solv-powerbank.title: Como elegir la bateria correcta
en/solve/solv-powerbank.content:
Hi, I’m David. I’m your tinkerer guide. I enjoy understanding devices by seeing how they work, checking them, and testing them with sincere curiosity. Not long ago, I was filming some videos in the Sierra Nevada where we could only find a power outlet every 3 days. We had to rely on large batteries so the cameras wouldn’t turn off in the middle of the jungle. That’s where I learned that not all batteries are the same and that labels sometimes tell us half-truths.
I once bought a 20,000 mAh battery, excited about not being disconnected on a trip. When it arrived, it was a heavy “brick.” But the worst part was when I tried to charge my phone: it barely gave me 3 or 4 charges. What happened to the rest of the energy? I started investigating and discovered the marketing trick. Here, I’ll tell you how to demystify those numbers so the same thing doesn’t happen to you.
What is the real capacity of a battery?
Almost all batteries claim to have a number in mAh (milliampere-hours), which is like saying how much water a bucket can hold. The problem is that the energy stored inside is at a low “voltage,” and to transfer it to a phone, you have to increase the force. In that process, part of the energy is lost as heat.
Why is it useful to understand this?
Understanding this helps you avoid spending extra money on equipment that promises a lot but delivers little. If you are in a community where the power goes out often or you have to walk a long way to reach a spot with a signal, knowing how much real energy you have in your pocket is the difference between staying connected or being left in the dark.
How do I know if I need it?

You feel like your power bank drains very quickly.
You are thinking about buying a battery for a laptop and don’t know if it will work.
Your community wants to buy a large charging station to share and doesn’t know which one to choose.






























Battery TypeIdeal UseAdvantageDisadvantageSmall Power BankPhones and tablets.Fits in your pocket.Does not charge laptops.Power Delivery (PD) BatteryModern laptops.Has a lot of force (watts).You need special cables.Power StationCommunity use, lights, radio.It is a large “well” of energy.It is expensive and heavy.
 Power Station
 PD battery, for charging laptops or fast charging for phones
How to do it?

Step 1 → Do the “toll” math
Look at the mAh number on the box. To know how much it will actually give you, multiply it by 0.7. If it says 20,000 mAh, you actually have about 14,000 mAh of usable energy. That missing 30% is lost along the way when the battery boosts its force from 3.7V to the 5V your phone needs.


Step 2 → Look for the “High Power” (PD) seal
If you need to charge a laptop, not just any battery will do. Look for one that says Power Delivery or PD and has at least 45W or 65W (watts). Laptops are more demanding, and if the battery is too weak, it simply won’t charge even if it’s plugged in.


Step 3 → Prepare for the sun
If you are going to be away from an outlet for many days, look for a battery that has an input for a solar panel. Some large batteries (called power stations) come ready to be connected directly to a panel that you unfold on the ground or on top of a vehicle.


Step 4 → Check the cables
For heavy-duty work, use thick, original cables. A thin cable is like a clogged hose: the energy doesn’t pass through quickly, and the battery takes an eternity to charge your equipment.


Warning: never leave a battery charging in the sun inside a closed car. The temperature rises so much that the battery can be damaged or, in extreme cases, catch fire.

Don’t be fooled
The market lies to us with numbers so that you buy the option they want. My recommendation is to always look at people’s reviews regarding what you are looking for to solve your energy needs. Often, cheap cables sold on the street don’t let energy pass with the necessary force, or numbers claiming 1 million mAh in the size of your hand are also misleading, so we must think about whether that is really possible. Can you hold a water tank in your hand?
If you need to charge a laptop, look for the battery to say PD (Power Delivery) and be at least 45W or 65W. If it doesn’t have those watts, the laptop won’t even feel that you connected it, and it will drain itself to charge the battery you just plugged in.
What can you achieve with this solution?
You ensure that community work doesn’t stop. Whether it’s filming a documentary, recording data in a rural area, or keeping a community radio station running, these batteries give you the security that the lack of outlets is not an obstacle to resistance and innovation in your territory.

en/solve/solv-purchase-temp-satellite.title: How to buy temporary satellite internet access?
en/solve/solv-purchase-temp-satellite.content:
A code or PIN to access satellite internet
Hello! I’m Belén. I didn’t write this entire solution, but upon reviewing it, I remembered many SOLE sessions that work thanks to this solution. Finding a place that sells a few data, or minutes, of Internet connection via satellite has allowed us to bring SOLE where we never thought we would reach.
What is getting an Internet PIN?
Accessing the Internet from a satellite connection is a recommended connection method in places where cable or telephone services do not reach, such as rural or remote areas. In a city, it constitutes an alternative and somewhat inexpensive system compared to the usual ones.
In Colombia, a “satellite connection PIN” refers to a code or key that allows connection to internet or communication services via satellites. These codes may be necessary to activate a satellite internet service, such as Starlink, or to configure satellite communication devices used in areas without terrestrial network coverage.
This solution is an explanation of how to access satellite connection as a service by the day or by the hour, something we can pay for in advance.
What is it for?
If your intention is to use the internet connection for something specific, this is the ideal solution. For example, if you want to gather your community to learn things together, using the internet as a group—that is, doing a SOLE—having data to share with two or three computers so that everyone can ask the network about the things they want to learn is the best way to guarantee the connection.
What do you need?

An internet provider in the area.
Money to pay for the PIN.
A device to access the Internet.

How to do it?
Follow these necessary steps to buy the PIN and connect to the Internet:


Moment 1: Recognize if this service exists in your area
First of all, it is necessary to know if this service is regularly offered in your territory. This service exists in places where the mobile data network of conventional operators does not exist, since, if it did, it would be more viable to top up your phone number with a data package or have a postpaid plan.
In some places, Internet operators sublease satellite internet connection in areas where the connection cannot reach by cable or they know that people in the area cannot contract other types of mobile phone services. For example, this is a company that offers this type of service in Barranquilla: Zonawipi


Moment 2: Evaluate other options
If you found that the service is in your area of residence, it is important to see if it is economically more convenient for you. That is, if you have to be buying PINs and traveling to another place to connect every day, this option may not be the most viable. Perhaps another solution would be better, such as taking up a collection to pay for community internet.
If it is definitely the most viable option, buy it!


Moment 3: Buy the PIN and connect
Now that you have decided to buy a PIN, remember to make the most of it. The connection time will be restricted only to the places where this network has reach. In practice, it works like an Internet Café where you connect wirelessly with your own device.
You just have to follow the instructions on the paper where the purchased PIN comes. Normally you must connect to a WiFi → network, which will automatically redirect you to a link where it will ask for the PIN number to give you access to the Internet. That’s it, now go ahead and connect and enjoy!
Remember that you will get very good use out of your Internet connection if you share it with more people who cannot access this resource. A great way to learn and enjoy together is to do a SOLE. SOLE is a methodology in which real-life challenges can be solved through Big Questions, using the Internet. In your community, do you want to learn how to make better use of your crops? Do you want to know what games children in other countries play? Do you have questions about how a specific atmospheric phenomenon is produced or how to take advantage of climate changes? Do a SOLE! You can find more information at Sole Colombia.


How to know if this solution works?
With this solution, you can achieve a temporary connection with internet access in a specific location.
Why might this solution work?
We have to measure very well the bandwidth → offered by the service and, in general, the quality of the service used in relation to its cost. This solution is intended for non-recurring access, since, in the case of becoming recurring, it would be very expensive and would end up being more economical to contract other types of services.

en/solve/solv-raspberrypi-pocket-interne.title: How to install a web server on a pocket computer?
en/solve/solv-raspberrypi-pocket-interne.content:
Hi, I’m Gabriel. I am an artist. Digital devices, how they work, and the way humans interact with them are interesting to me. I consider myself a tinkerer, and I invite you, if you want, to be one too.
What is a Raspberry Pi, or a pocket Internet?
This solution will help you create a small internet on your local network with few resources.
By installing and configuring a server → on the network, your community will be able to access the content hosted on it from their computers or phones. In this way, they can have, for example, a copy of Wikipedia so that everyone can check it whenever they need to, without needing to access the Internet → to do so.
What is it for?
If we talk about using the Internet to solve Big Questions and real-life challenges as a group, having content accessible without an Internet connection can be an excellent option: for example, if you are going to do a SOLE in a very remote place, where you know that connectivity is definitely not going to be viable.
Having downloadable content offline will allow them to research and reach some conclusions, which they can expand on at another time with an Internet connection or when they can connect an “Abuelita” (Grandmother node).
Do you want to know more about how to turn your space into a place to learn, or who the “Abuelitas de la Nube” (Cloud Grandmothers) are? Visit Solecolombia.org to learn how, and browse the site to learn more about the Cloud of Grandmothers that can support the learning processes happening in your space.
How do you know if you need it?
Ask yourself how good your Internet connection is in the place from where you are going to connect. At SOLE Colombia, we know the difficulties of many remote communities, where the internet is scarce or difficult to access, and a solution like this allows people to access downloaded content, which is almost like having access to their twins on the network.
Thus, it becomes possible to browse a replica of some parts of the Internet, learning to use technology in a different way.
Even though its benefits are many and obvious, this is a solution that requires a powerful tinkering spirit and high doses of commitment and patience… we are sure that you can manage to configure your little pocket internet!
What do you need?

Raspberry Pi
MicroSD card 32 GB class 10
Power supply for the Raspberry Pi - check the specifications on Raspberry Pi
Ethernet cable →
MicroSD to USB memory adapter.
Case for RPI (optional)
Internet connection
A computer
Patience

How to do it?


Moment 1: Prepare your Pi
For this solution, we are using a Raspberry Pi v4, but previous versions can work without a problem.
If you are starting with a new Raspberry Pi and have a plastic case, assemble the heat sink on the RPI processor and place it inside its protective case before continuing.
The Raspberry Pi developers have created a tool to facilitate the download, installation, and configuration of the MicroSD memories that will have the operating system that runs the RPI.


Install the specific software for your operating system, Raspberry Pi Imager
To install it on your computer, visit www.raspberrypi.com/software/. There you can download the version of the Raspberry Pi Imager that works on your operating system (Windows, Linux, or Mac). Once you install it, you can continue with the next step.



Connect the MicroSD to your computer
Before running the Raspberry Pi Imager, you must connect the MicroSD → memory to your computer.
To do this, it is necessary to use a USB adapter if your equipment does not have a slot for it.
Once you verify that the memory is on the computer, run the Raspberry Pi Imager and continue with the solution.


Open the Raspberry Pi Imager and choose your operating system





Moment 2: Connect your Pi


Locate it in the Pi Imager
Now that our Pi is connected to the power and to our local network, we must locate it to be able to connect to it.
Before this, a small note: the steps that follow will be carried out through a Terminal. If you use a Unix-type operating system (Linux, MacOS), simply look for the terminal and you can follow the steps there (below you have how to do it). If you use Windows, you can use the CMD in this step and, to connect to the Pi, you can use Putty.
To locate the Pi in a Terminal, we use the ping program; this will try to send a small data packet to the address we indicate and will tell us, among other things, the IP → address of the computer.
Here we are going to make use of the name we gave our Pi, in our case solevoltaje. In the terminal, we type ping solevoltaje.local. The program responds to us, among other things, with the IP → 192.168.0.25, which indicates that our Pi is available for us to connect and start working.



Connect to the Pi
So that the connection between your Pi and the rest of the devices is secure, we connect via an SSH protocol → to our Pi. To do this, we write in our terminal ssh solevoltaje@solevoltaje.local or with the IP Address ssh solevoltaje@192.168.0.25
Remember that we must place our username and domain name or IP → in the parameters that we give to SSH ssh <username>@<domain name>.
As soon as the connection is established, the system will ask us for the password. Type the same one you entered in the configuration in the previous steps and finish by pressing the enter key.


Update the software

Once we are connected to the Pi, we must perform a couple of administrative tasks. The first is to update our operating system software. We do this by typing the following in the terminal:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade

Once the task of downloading and configuring the new software is finished, we can continue with the solution.

The commands we enter in this line start with sudo to have superuser permissions and be able to apply changes to the system.



Expand the SWAP

Now, it is necessary to expand the SWAP memory space so that our Pi can easily deal with operations that require more memory than what we have available in the RAM Memory →. Perform the steps below one after another:
First, we deactivate the SWAP memory
sudo dphys-swapfile swapoff

Then we edit the configuration file and change the size to our needs:
sudo nano /etc/dphys-swapfile

In the file, look for the line that by default says CONF_SWAPSIZE=100 and change it to CONF_SWAPSIZE=2048. Then, save and exit the text editor.
Now we need to activate the new configuration:
sudo dphys-swapfile setup

We activate the SWAP memory again:
sudo dphys-swapfile swapon

Finally, we restart the Pi so that all programs have access to the new SWAP:
sudo reboot

This last command restarts the Pi, closing our remote connection. You must wait for the process to complete in a couple of minutes and reconnect via SSH Protocol to continue.


Now, we install the server

After all this preparatory process, which is simpler than it seems, we proceed to install nginx, a program that will allow our Pi to function as a web server → and in this way we can access resources we have hosted there from other devices via a web browser.
Once we are connected to the Pi, we write in the terminal:
sudo apt install nginx

This line downloads, installs, and starts our server.




Moment 3: Test that everything works well

Now, we test that everything is working.
To do this, on our computer, we open a web browser window and in the address bar we type solevoltaje.local
If everything is working correctly, we should see a page like the one in the image that says Welcome to nginx.


Other possible internets
With this solution, you will manage to have a local server that allows hosting content that will be visible on the local network.
In this way, you can download useful material for SOLE sessions and not need Internet access to answer the Big Questions. You can also think about loading the content you would like to take to a remote place or that you would like to share with other people, for example, movies, educational material, instructions, online games… or anything you can download to use with others!
Thanks to the fact that the Pi is so small, you can take it to different places and have a pocket Internet.
Why might this solution work?
With this solution, you will have a portable server; however, it still does not have any information to share. We recommend you check the other solutions we have in the guide so that you can take advantage of your new server.
Related solutions

How to use the game to learn to take care of equipment in a community? →

en/solve/solv-save-data-phone.title: ¿Cómo hacer que los datos de tu celular duren más?
en/solve/solv-save-data-phone.content:
Hi! I’m Catalina. Has it ever happened to you that you get a message saying your data has run out and you don’t even know where it went? It used to happen to me all the time and it was very frustrating, especially when I needed the internet for something really important like homework or an errand.
I’m not a systems expert, but I started “tinkering” with my phone’s settings and discovered that there are several open faucets where our internet leaks out. I’ve learned that with a couple of methodical adjustments and, above all, by being more conscious of how we use our cell phones, we can make the same plan last much longer. Here, I’ll show you how I did it!

What is data management?
It is learning how to configure your phone so that it only spends internet on what you decide. But before moving any buttons, it is important to ask ourselves: What do I want to spend my data on today? Many times we lose it watching videos that don’t even interest us, just out of inertia. Managing is taking control of your connection.

What is it for and what can you achieve?
This solution allows you to have real control over your spending and ensures that you don’t get left disconnected in the middle of the month. In the end, this can save you money and gives you the freedom to use your internet for what is truly valuable to you and your community.

Before you start…
For these tricks to work, it is best to do them while you are connected to a WiFi network (in a park or at a neighbor’s house), so you don’t spend your own data while configuring the savings.
Question to think about: Before looking for a more expensive plan, have you tried closing the “faucets” where your current data is leaking? Sometimes, what we need is not more internet, but better-used internet.

What do you need?

Your cell phone with an active data plan.
A few calm minutes to check the settings.
A “tinkerer’s” spirit! Don’t be afraid to explore your phone’s menus.


How to do it?

Step 1 → Identify who is “eating” your data

Go to Settings and look for the “Data usage” or “Mobile network” option. There you will see a list of the applications that have used the most internet in the last month.



Step 2 → Set a limit so you don’t get any surprises

In the same data menu, look for “Data limit” or “Data warning”. Configure it so that the phone notifies you when you reach a daily amount (for example, 600 MB). It’s a way of telling yourself: “Watch out! You’ve already spent today’s allowance.”



Step 3 → Activate savings “app by app”

Enter the applications you use the most (such as Instagram, Facebook, or YouTube). Look in their own settings for the “Data saver” or “Content quality” option. Activate it so that videos do NOT play automatically. This way, you only spend internet on the video you really want to watch.



Recommendations

Do I really need it now? Before opening a heavy application, ask yourself if it can wait until you are in an area with free WiFi.
Clean up your phone: Disable “Auto-update” for applications in the Play Store; that consumes entire gigabytes without you even noticing.
The airplane mode trick: If you are not going to use your phone for a long time, turn off mobile data. You prevent the phone from spending internet “searching” for a signal or background updates.


Other possible internets
Managing our individual data well is the first step toward thinking about a collective internet. When we stop being passive consumers of what social networks push on us, we start using technology for what is truly useful to us.
Imagine if what we saved individually could be pooled to pay for a community connection that belongs to everyone. Other internets are possible when we remember that the internet is a tool, not an end in itself. By taking care of your data, you are taking care of a resource that allows you to stay connected with what you love.

Recommended solutions

If you are thinking about changing your provider, check this first: How to choose a suitable cell phone plan? →
To know if the savings are affecting your experience: How to measure your internet speed? →
Once you are an expert at saving, teach others: Sharing internet from your phone →


References

How to make the most of your data plan - La Nación

en/solve/solv-second-life-computer.title: How to give a second life to an old computer by installing Linux?
en/solve/solv-second-life-computer.content:
Hello! I’m David. One of the things that frustrates me the most is seeing how a perfectly good computer becomes slow and unusable just because the operating system → (almost always Windows →) becomes too heavy over the years. It’s like trying to make someone run with a backpack full of rocks. I started researching and discovered that you don’t have to throw your equipment away: you can take off the heavy backpack by installing a free and lightweight system called Linux →. Here, I’ll show you how to do it step by step.

What is installing Linux → Ubuntu?
It is changing the main program that makes your computer work. Ubuntu is one of the friendliest and easiest-to-use versions (or “flavors”) of Linux →. It completely replaces your previous system with a new, free, and much lighter one.
What is it for?
It is used to revive that old computer you have stored away because it “doesn’t work anymore” or “is too slow.” By installing a system that requires fewer resources, the computer will turn on quickly again, you will be able to browse the internet → without it freezing, and you will be able to use free office programs. It is an excellent way to avoid generating electronic waste and save money.
Before you begin…

Attention: This process will erase absolutely everything on your computer and the USB flash drive → you use. Make sure to save your photos, documents, and important files on another drive or in the cloud before starting.

What do you need?

An old computer (that still turns on).
An empty USB flash drive → of at least 16GB.
An internet → connection (to download the initial files).
A bit of patience (the download and installation take time).

How to do it?

Step 1 → Download the necessary files

To start, you need to download two things from the internet.
First, the Linux Ubuntu installer. Go to its official website ubuntu.com and look for the “Download” section. Save the file to your computer.

Second, you need a free program called RUFUS. This program will help us put the installer onto the USB in a special way. Download it at rufus.ie/en/.


Step 2 → Prepare the USB drive

Connect your USB drive to the computer. Remember that everything on it will be erased. Open the RUFUS program you just downloaded (it doesn’t need to be installed, it just opens).

In RUFUS, make sure your USB is selected at the top. Then, click “Select” and find the Ubuntu file you downloaded in step 1. Finally, click “Start.”


You’re doing well: Wait a few minutes for the program to finish. You will know it is ready when the green bar fills up and says “READY.” Your USB is now ready to install!



Step 3 → Start the computer from the USB (Boot)


Now comes the step that scares many, but it is simple. Turn off the old computer. Connect the USB to it. When turning it on, you must repeatedly press a specific key (usually F12, F2, or Esc) before the old system loads, so that a boot menu appears.

Tip: If you don’t know which key it is, search on your phone: “How to access the boot menu on [your computer brand]“.


In this menu, use the keyboard arrows to select your USB drive (it usually has the brand name of the drive or says “USB Device”) and press Enter.

Step 4 → Begin the installation

If you did it right, a black menu with white letters will appear. Select the option “Try or install Ubuntu” and press Enter.

After a few seconds, a graphical screen will appear. On the left, find and select your preferred language. Then click the big button that says “Install Ubuntu.”

The system will ask you to test your keyboard layout. Type some letters (like “ñ” or punctuation marks) to make sure they work correctly.


Step 5 → Erase the old disk and install Ubuntu

You will reach a screen that asks for the “Installation type.” To leave your computer like new and erase any trace of Windows and its problems, select “Something else” or “Erase disk and install Ubuntu” (if this direct option appears, take it).

If you used “Something else,” you will see a list of divisions (partitions) of your old hard drive →. Select them one by one and press the button with the minus sign (”-”) until none remain, to clean house completely.

Then, you can go back and select the recommended option: “Erase disk and install Ubuntu.” Click “Install now.”

My suggestion is that if you haven’t backed up your disk, this is the time. My recommendation is to create a partition using the new partition button on the largest disk, leave at least 40GB for Linux, and with that, you can move files from one system to the other.



Cheer up: A warning window will appear saying that the disks will be overwritten. It is normal to be afraid, but it is the system confirming that you are sure about erasing everything old. Click “Continue.”



Step 6 → Configure your user and location

The system will ask you where you are to set the correct time. Click on the map and press continue.

A button will appear; look for Bogotá (Colombia) or your country’s capital to have the local time.


Now, choose a name for your computer, your username, and a password. Don’t forget it! This password is your key to the machine. You can choose whether you want it to ask for it every time you turn on the machine or to log in automatically.


Step 7 → Finish and restart

Now all that’s left is to wait. The system will copy all the necessary files. You can make yourself a coffee while you watch the images showing you what new things the system brings.


You’re doing well: When everything finishes, a message will appear saying “Installation complete.” Click “Restart now.”


The screen will go black and will ask you, in English, to remove the installation medium (“Please remove the installation medium, then press ENTER”).

Remove your USB drive and press Enter.


And that’s it! Your computer will turn on with its new system, fresh, clean, and fast.

Recommendations if you get stuck

If your computer does not recognize the USB and always starts in Windows, check if you have an option called “Secure Boot” enabled on your computer (on the same screen where you entered the Boot Menu). Sometimes it must be disabled to install new systems.
If you see that Ubuntu is still a bit slow for your computer (because it is veeery old), there are even lighter versions like Lubuntu or Xubuntu. The installation process is exactly the same.

How to know if it works?
When turning on the computer without the USB drive connected, you will no longer see the Windows logo. Instead, you will see the Ubuntu logo and will quickly arrive at a clean and functional desktop where you can connect to the internet and browse without problems.
Other possible internets
You will be able to make equipment that people thought was damaged or obsolete available to the community. By not depending on expensive licenses or needing the latest Processor (CPU) → on the market, any group can set up a small computer lab by recycling technology that others discard. It is an act of technological independence.
Recommended solutions

How to choose a good computer for the community? →
How to share internet from your computer to others? →

References

Installation guide video (YouTube): Ubuntu Installation Tutorial

You have already given that computer a new chance to be useful. Sometimes, things just need us to look at them from another perspective to shine again.

en/solve/solv-share-computers.title: How to share available computers?
en/solve/solv-share-computers.content:
Sole Colombia
Hello, I’m Sanjay. For the last ten years, I have been doing SOLE, and I have led SOLE Colombia to what it is today. For years, I have seen how many devices are available gathering dust in school closets, or with restricted use because the person assigned to their custody believes that strict criteria must be met.
What is sharing available computers and managing their loan?
With this solution, I want to focus on the importance of using the Internet → in a group. It is a very different experience: it is a shared use of devices, which opens the door for us to walk together along the paths of the Internet. You will have the opportunity to come into contact with the experience of the devices that we all use and take care of, which are the gateway to living better together, using the Internet.
What is it for?
Sharing computers makes us all win. We don’t need as much money to buy them or maintain them because we can share the cost among more people, and, also, more people can benefit from their use.
When we share computers and use them in common, they become a safe place to learn and do things together: this is how we take care of the spaces we enter, avoid dangerous portals or inappropriate content by looking out for others, better understand the information we review among several people, find common interests, interact with each other instead of just with machines… we turn technology into a park where we can all play. SOLE is a perfect tool to share your computers with an interesting and common purpose: to solve Big Questions. Do you want to know how? Come in and find out at SoleColombia
What do you need?

Computers to share.
A place with electricity.
Generosity.

How to do it?


Moment 1: Manage computers
The first thing we must have are the computers to be able to share; we can get these in a public library or a school. Usually, there are state programs that provide these computers, and often they remain stored and unused due to a lack of knowledge.
Once you identify the place, you must look for the person in charge; they will be the key person for you to succeed. Tell them about your purpose for using the computers, such as doing SOLE or any other. Also, mention your community’s difficulty or inability to have access to their own computers. Then, try to set the date and time when you will come with your community so that both parties are committed.

Photo: Sole Colombia


Moment 2: Agree on some rules for sharing
Now that the place and the computers are committed, gather your community and talk about the management you already did so that they see the previous work and share the responsibility with you. Afterward, talk about the minimum care they should take and ask them if they can think of other types of care. Remember that this first time will be decisive for whether or not they continue to lend you computers in the future.

Photo: Sole Colombia


Moment 3: Let’s share!
Contact the person in charge of the library or the public space and go with your group to enjoy using the internet as a group. Always remember to enjoy the devices in a shared way; for example, 4 people can sit at the same computer.


Other possible internets
This solution is a series of recommendations that give you a route to more easily manage computers in a public space to share with your community.
Why might this solution work?
This solution will not allow you to get computers permanently, and in places with little state presence, you may not find places where they will lend you these computers.

en/solve/solv-share-internet-cellphone.title: How to share internet from my mobile phone?
en/solve/solv-share-internet-cellphone.content:
Hello! This solution was written by Nicolás, one of the tinkerers at SOLE Colombia.
I, Belén, am reviewing it, and although I like tinkering, sometimes I find it hard to understand how things work. I suppose I’m getting on in years and everything changes very quickly… when I started using computers, they were basically typewriters. But not anymore! I encourage you to lose your fear!
What is setting up a personal WiFi → zone?
Did you know that your smartphone has an almost permanent Internet connection? Usually, cellular plans come with a data plan attached, which allows you to access the Internet.
That connection can become slow or inefficient and needs to be restored. But you might also want to share it with others; do you want to know how? Keep reading.
What is it for?
You might want to share your data plan’s Internet signal with other people. But it can also happen that, even with an Internet connection, the pages we want to open load with difficulty, or the data call connection doesn’t work well.
Almost always, the best way to get everything to start over and work again is to restart everything from scratch.
Once restarted, you will be able to share your phone’s Internet signal to do SOLE with your community!
What do you need?

A cell phone.
Enough data on your cell phone to share with others.
Generosity.

How to do it?

Step 1 → Restart the data connection**

Slide the top of your phone down to access the control panel. Once there, select the “Mobile data” option, turn it off for a few seconds, and turn it back on. Wait a moment for the phone to access the cellular network and that’s it! Your connection will be fresh and working correctly.

Want to know another trick? Turn on airplane mode; this will cause all your phone’s parameters related to the Internet signal to reset.



Moment 2: Configure the mobile hotspot**

Go to settings and look for **“mobile hotspot”**; in English, it appears as **“Hotspot”**.

In this menu, look for the **“Set up mobile hotspot”** option. Several details will appear; for now, we are only interested in configuring the name of the [[en/glossary/conc-wifi|WiFi signal →]] you create and the access password.

Once you change them, press the checkmark (or the X) to save the new configuration.




Moment 3: Share internet
Slide the top of your phone down to access the control panel; you can find the “Mobile Hotspot”, “Hotspot”, or something similar.
Simply activate it to share the Internet signal with whoever you want.
If you want to do SOLE, this is an excellent solution to ensure that all computers can perform their search. You already know that at SOLE Colombia, we are always thinking about how to take advantage of the resources we have individually to lead our communities to improve their Internet experience… there is nothing like using it in a group!



How do I know if this solution works?
With this recipe, you can restart your phone’s cellular network settings. This will improve browsing speed and connection stability. You will be able to share it with other phones and/or computers and search the Internet for the answers to the Big Questions that motivate your SOLE.
Why might this solution work?
Restarting the cellular network connection will improve your connection and you will be able to browse a little faster, but the geographical area where you are located must have coverage from your operator.
This recipe will not work if the phone signal in your area is not of good quality. Learning to share the internet will be a very important step for when you manage to get computers, as it is easier to use the internet in a group with large screens.

en/solve/solv-share-internet-computer.title: How to share internet from your computer?
en/solve/solv-share-internet-computer.content:
Hi! I’m Catalina, welcome to this solution 👋🏽
The first version of this solution was written by another colleague, Nicolás, and I complemented it a bit so we can navigate it together.
This, like other solutions, is designed so that anyone can do it. I am not an expert in technology topics and I succeeded! So, shall we jump in and try it together? Remember that if you have questions, you can join the Cacharreras Community → where we support each other in solving our connectivity (and connection) together.
What is sharing the Internet from your computer?
In short, it means configuring your computer to turn it into an internet router →, that is, a device capable of distributing the Internet signal to other devices. It is similar to when you use your cell phone to share the internet →.

What is it for?
Sometimes we are in places where we only have an Internet connection on a computer and we don’t know the password for the Wi-Fi → network. How do we take advantage of that single connection point? With this solution, we can turn THAT computer into an internet access point or “hotspot” for everyone.

What do you need?

A computer (ideally connected to the Internet via Ethernet → cable).
Cell phones or other devices without Internet access.
Patience.


How to do it?

Step 0 → How do I know if my computer works for this solution?

Any computer works if its Internet connection is via cable, that is, not through a Wi-Fi network. Even old computers can become high-power routers by making some configurations in their operating system →, but they require their connection to be via cable.
If your computer is not connected via cable and is a recent model, it might still work: for a computer to function as a router receiving and distributing a signal via Wi-Fi, its network card must have a capability called Monitor Mode. The easiest way to know if your computer has this card is in true “cacharrero” (tinkerer) style: by testing it!
So let’s get started! 👇🏽


Step 1 → Go to your computer’s Internet settings

⚠️⚠️ Keep in mind that Nicolás wrote this solution using a very popular operating system in Colombia: Windows 10. If you have another operating system, your screen may look slightly different, but the idea is the same.
To start, select the Start button (Windows symbol button). In the settings window, look for the following options: Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile hotspot (click on each option to find the next one).




Step 2 → Activate and configure the Internet zone.

When you are in the mobile hotspot window, activate the option to share the internet with other devices. In the image below 👇🏽 you can see that you can share the Internet via Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. Useful, right?



Step 3 → Connect other people!

You are now ready to share your Internet with others! In the “Mobile hotspot” window, you will find the network name and the password. If you want to change it, you can do so using the “Edit” button.

How do I know if this solution works?
On another device (computer, cell phone, tablet, etc.), activate the search for Wi-Fi networks (or Bluetooth if you chose to share via this medium). If you find the network you configured on your computer, you have half the task done.
Now, connect that other device to the network. If you can browse, it means you did it!

Other possible Internets
With this solution, you can provide Internet access to more devices in one place, without needing the access password for the original network. If you share with other devices, more people will be able to access the Internet. This alternative allows sharing the Internet with up to 8 devices and is geographically limited to the range of the network generated by the computer.
After that, you can promote the use of the Internet in a group to learn how to solve challenges as a community 💪🏽🛠️ .

Related solutions

You can test how good the connection is using your computer as a modem by measuring the Internet speed: How to know the speed of your Internet connection? →

en/solve/solv-share-internet-wirelessly.title: Do you want to share your internet wirelessly?
en/solve/solv-share-internet-wirelessly.content:
Configure your Raspberry Pi
Share your pocket internet
Hi, I’m Gabriel. I’m an artist. Digital devices, how they work, and the way we humans interact with them are interesting to me. I consider myself a tinkerer, and I invite you, if you’d like, to be one too.
I wrote the solution Raspberry Pi: A small pocket Internet so you could set it up, and now, I’ll walk you through how to share your device’s signal with other people or other devices.
What is sharing your Raspberry Pi’s internet?
Having a computer the size of a credit card, being able to connect it to the Internet, and, furthermore, being able to share that connection with the other computers you have for doing SOLE, is like opening the doors to the world’s largest library!
It means turning any space into a Self-Organized Learning Environment where you can open the doors to the creativity of solving challenges, whether complex or simple, in your community. INCREDIBLE! Isn’t it?
To do SOLE, there are only three fundamental things: people, a few computers with an internet connection, and Big Questions.
What is it for?
With this recipe, you will be able to turn your Raspberry Pi → into a portable Router, so your community can connect wirelessly and access the information hosted there, and, if you have a wired Internet connection, you will be able to share it as well.
What do you need?

A Raspberry Pi
A computer
Internet connection - you can check the solution How to know what type of Internet signal you have? to make sure what type of connection you have, and if it is active
Lots of patience

How to do it?

Moment 1: Connect to your Pi
First of all, make sure you have a Raspberry Pi up and running. If you need help with this, check the recipe Raspberry Pi: A small pocket Internet where we tell you how to get started with this device.
Once you have your system running, connect to your Raspberry Pi via a Terminal → by initiating an SSH → connection.
Make sure you have an Internet connection to continue with the following steps.
Moment 2: Update your Raspberry Pi system


The first step is to perform a system-wide update to ensure we have the latest versions of the programs running on our Pi.
To do this, simply type in the terminal:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade

The system will notify us which packages need to be updated. To continue with the process, we must accept by typing y and pressing the enter key.

Moment 3: Install the necessary software


Next, we need to install two programs on our Pi:
sudo apt install -y hostapd dnsmasq

This command will install hostapd, which is a utility that allows us to use our Pi’s wireless as a wireless access point, and dnsmasq, which will allow us to configure a server → DNS → and DHCP → to allow users to connect to the server → and have the necessary network configurations to access it.

Moment 4: Configure a static IP
Disable the wireless interface


In this step, we will configure a static IP address on our Pi’s wireless interface. It is important that you are not connected wirelessly to the Pi, because during the following steps, wireless communication will be suspended. So, make sure you are connected via a cable, or have a screen and keyboard connected directly to the Pi to continue.
Network configurations on the Pi are handled by the dhcpcd program; it is responsible for requesting and assigning the necessary IP addresses for the available network interfaces. At this moment, we have to tell this program to ignore the wireless interface. To do this, we must edit the configuration file:
sudo nano /etc/dhcpcd.conf

… and at the end of it, add this line:
denyinterfaces wlan0

To exit and save the changes, press ctrl + x followed by y when prompted.

Assign a static IP


Now we must assign a static IP address to the wlan0 interface in a different range than our wired network. We are going to edit the file:
sudo nano /etc/network/interfaces

Don’t be afraid. It seems complex, but if you’ve made it this far, you’re almost there. Add the following to the end:
allow-hotplug wlan0
iface wlan0 inet static
    address 192.168.10.1
    netmask 255.255.255.0
    network 192.168.10.0
    broadcast 192.168.10.255

What we are doing is configuring this interface to have the IP 192.168.10.1.
To exit and save the changes, press ctrl + x followed by y when prompted.

Moment 5: Configure our wireless access point


It is time to tell hostapd how to operate. We are going to tell it to broadcast the network name (SSID) and operate on a specific channel. We will put these configurations in the file:
sudo nano /etc/hostapd/hostapd.conf

… where we add the following data:
interface=wlan0
driver=nl80211
ssid=SOLEVOLTAJE
hw_mode=g
channel=11
ieee80211n=1
wmm_enabled=1
ht_capab=[HT40][SHORT-GI-20][DSSS_CCK-40]
macaddr_acl=0
auth_algs=1
ignore_broadcast_ssid=0
wpa=2
wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
wpa_passphrase=LACONTRASENADEACCESO
rsn_pairwise=CCMP

Some things can be changed here:

The network name: we configure this in the ssid= line; in our example, the network will be called SOLEVOLTAJE.
The channel: channel=11 is saying that we are going to operate on channel 11, but we can change it to whichever works best in our location.
The access password: for security, it is necessary that we assign a key to connect to the network. We do this by assigning it in the wpa_passphrase=LACONTRASENADEACCESO line.

Now we must inform hostapd where the configuration is located. We do this by editing the file:
sudo nano /etc/default/hostapd

… and adding the following line to it:
DAEMON_CONF=


Moment 6: Start the services

Before restarting our Pi, we must enable the services so that they run every time we turn it on.
To do this, type the following in the terminal:
sudo systemctl unmask hostapd
sudo systemctl enable hostapd
sudo systemctl start hostapd

sudo systemctl unmask dnsmasq
sudo systemctl enable dnsmasq
sudo systemctl start dnsmasq


… and finally, we restart the Pi to perform our first test:
sudo reboot now


Moment 7: Perform a first test


From another computer or phone, look for the network we just created in the wireless networks, in our case SOLEVOLTAJE, and connect to it.
If you check the network settings, you should see that the assigned IP address should be in the range we selected in the dnsmasq configuration. In our case, the device has the IP 192.168.10.143 assigned.


Moment 8: You can now share the wired connection


At this point, those who connect to our access point will be able to see the files and services we have configured on our Raspberry Pi. If you want to share the wired Internet connection via the wireless network, continue with the following steps.

Moment 9: Forward traffic to the wired connection


It is necessary for our system to forward traffic from the wireless interface to the wired one in order to share the connection. At this point, we have to edit the file:
sudo nano /etc/sysctl.conf

In its content, we look for the line that says #net.ipv4.ip_forward=1 and remove the # at the beginning to indicate that we want to activate this directive. Once we make this modification, we save the file and continue to the next step.

Moment 10: Finally, secure the Firewall


We are now at the last step of the configuration. Here we have to tell the Firewall → to allow network traffic to pass between the wireless and wired interfaces. To do this, we enter these commands in our terminal:
sudo iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -j MASQUERADE
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i eth0 -o wlan0 -m state --state RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
sudo iptables -A FORWARD -i wlan0 -o eth0 -j ACCEPT

At this point, we should already have internet on our wireless clients! However, we need to ensure these changes are not lost when we restart our Pi. To do this, we are going to save the configuration in a text file:
sudo sh -c "iptables-save > /etc/iptables.ipv4.nat"


Moment 11: Now, with Internet!


After this long process, clients connected to our Pi will be able to have access to the Internet connection shared from our Raspberry Pi… SUCCESS!
Did you get tangled up in any of the steps? Tell us how to complete this solution to make it clearer.
Other possible internets
With this recipe, you can configure a portable Router, which is useful for carrying content on your Raspberry Pi and sharing it with the community, without the need for a constant Internet connection.
Additionally, if you have a wired connection, you can share it to make your SOLE sessions more powerful.
Why might this solution work?
Having a portable, low-power router allows us to easily take our content to multiple places where the Internet connection is not constant.
However, the number of clients our Pi can support is low. If you are going to connect more than 10 people at the same time, the connection speed might get a bit slow, and to solve this, you should look for a more powerful router.
If you made it this far, you have learned a lot of things that you can share with your community and, thus, improve connectivity conditions. Using the Internet in a group is a challenging experience, both in terms of technology and in terms of community. Doing SOLE is a way to use the Internet in a group to live better together.
